# 食环署在大陇街附近发现鼠洞后抓获近60只老鼠
香港食物环境卫生署在葵涌垃圾站发现老鼠洞后，两个月内抓获近60只老鼠。它正在加强清洁、防鼠和夜间巡逻，同时敦促跨部门合作和公众行动。

# FEHD catches nearly 60 rats near Tai Loong Street after rodent burrows found

Hong Kong's Food and Environmental Hygiene Department has caught nearly 60 rats over two months at a Kwai Chung refuse point after burrows were found. It is stepping up cleaning, rodent-proofing and night patrols, while urging cross-departmental cooperation and public action.

[![Image 4: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

 By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

 27 Oct 2026 at 03:17 HKT · updated 27 Oct, 04:25 · 2 min read

The [Food and Environmental Hygiene Department](https://clb.org.hk/en/hong-kong/Hong-Kong-issues-October-third-batch-of-Aedes-albopictus-tra-0f795f) said on Monday it has stepped up cleaning and rodent prevention at a refuse collection point and public areas in Kwai Chung after multiple rat burrows were found on a slope at Tai Loong Street Rest Garden, and has deployed a night rodent control team.

The department said it has caught nearly 60 live rats at the refuse collection point and surrounding public areas over the past two months and will continue adjusting its deployment based on conditions.

FEHD staff joined Legislative Council members and Kwai Tsing district councillors on Monday morning to inspect the refuse collection point and nearby public areas.

The department said it has strengthened work in four areas: cleaning, facilities, rodent control and patrols. It has increased the frequency of cleaning and rubbish collection at the refuse collection point to reduce food sources, and checked, repaired and enhanced rodent-proof facilities. It has also deployed a night rodent control team to set traps and bait at rat activity spots and stepped up inspections of nearby restaurants and shops.

On the management of the rest garden and slope, the FEHD said the venue is managed by the Leisure and Cultural Services Department, which is responsible for daily environmental hygiene, rodent prevention and monitoring, while slope maintenance is handled by the relevant departments under established arrangements.

The FEHD said it has provided professional advice to the LCSD on the slope rodent problem and will continue inspections and follow-up, urging the venue's managing department to take appropriate measures. It stressed that cross-departmental cooperation can enhance rodent prevention but does not replace each department's daily management responsibilities.

The department noted that rat activity is not limited by venue boundaries and that rodent control cannot rely solely on government inspections and operations, calling on venue managers, shops, property management companies and the public to tackle the problem at source.

summary: ## 巴西总统卢拉：北京在美国后院的“老朋友”第四次赢得大选 视频加注文字，卢拉总统如何扭转局势击败弗拉维奥·博尔索纳罗？（英语影片） * * Author, 玛丽娜·罗西（Marina Rossi） * Role, BBC巴西葡语记者 * Reporting from, 圣保罗报导 * Author, 利安德罗·普拉泽雷斯（Leandro Prazeres） * Role, BBC巴西葡语记者 * Reporting from, 巴西利亚报导 * Author, 瓦妮莎·布
content:
## 巴西总统卢拉：北京在美国后院的“老朋友”第四次赢得大选

视频加注文字，卢拉总统如何扭转局势击败弗拉维奥·博尔索纳罗？（英语影片）

*       *   Author, 玛丽娜·罗西（Marina Rossi）
    *   Role, BBC巴西葡语记者
    *   Reporting from, 圣保罗报导

    *   Author, 利安德罗·普拉泽雷斯（Leandro Prazeres）
    *   Role, BBC巴西葡语记者
    *   Reporting from, 巴西利亚报导

    *   Author, 瓦妮莎·布施吕特（Vanessa Buschschlüter）
    *   Role, BBC拉丁美洲网上新闻编辑
    *   Reporting from, 伦敦报导

*   Published 2026年10月26日上午10点13分

*   阅读时间: 4 分钟

在经过一场激烈角逐的竞选之后，巴西资深左翼总统路易斯·伊纳西奥·卢拉·达席尔瓦（Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva；劳拉）成功连任，击败了尚未承认败选的右翼对手弗拉维奥·博索纳罗（Flávio Bolsonaro；博尔索纳罗）。

巴西高等选举法院（Superior Electoral Court）宣布，在所有选票点算完毕后，卢拉获得51.79%的选票，而博索纳罗获得48.21%。

但博索纳罗拒绝承认选举结果，称投票延长两小时“无法解释”——尽管他的竞选团队以及其对手的竞选团队都曾要求投票站延长开放时间。他在巴西利亚向支持者表示，他将寻求撤销此次选举。

然而，这并未阻止卢拉及其支持者庆祝他们所称的“历史性胜利”和一次出人意料的逆转胜。

在胜选演说中，将于星期二（10月27日）满81岁的卢拉赞扬年轻选民走上街头“捍卫巴西民主”。

他通往第四个任期的道路并不平坦。自巴西于1988年恢复民主以来，他是首位在第一轮投票落败却最终赢得总统大选的领导人。而他再次当选、展开额外第二个任期，也属前所未有。

他还逆转了拉丁美洲更广泛的趋势——在该地区，选民纷纷惩罚执政者并转向右翼。整个地区内，阿根廷、智利和哥伦比亚等大国如今都由保守派领导人执掌。

](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/ws/640/cpsprodpb/41be/live/5969d000-d094-11f1-93e1-3b657b665bcf.jpg.webp)

图像来源，EPA/ Shutterstock

图像加注文字，卢拉周日投票后向支持者致意。

“我们的喉咙都很疲倦了。”在胜选演说中，卢拉以沙哑的嗓音开场。

他几乎立刻把麦克风交给副总统杰拉尔多·阿尔克明（Geraldo Alckmin），说希望由阿尔克明先发言。

阿尔克明对卢拉说：“你第二次拯救了巴西民主。”卢拉随后感谢竞选团队的统筹者，也感谢“巴西人民的慷慨”，其中包括“走上街头捍卫巴西民主”的年轻人。

他对群众说，人们之所以投票，是因为我们能够说服他们，这一票对我们国家的主权很重要。

他说，这场选举是“消极情绪与谎言的失败”。卢拉在胜选演说中再次强调，巴西“不会接受成为任何人的后院”。

这是他在竞选期间一再重复的说法之一，指向“美国的后院”一词，用来概括美国政策中一种观念：拉丁美洲应处于美国的势力范围之内。

卢拉的竞选活动在首轮失利后重新焕发生机，其动力来自街头示威和大规模的社交媒体攻势。

这位前金属工人自1989年首次参选总统以来一直是巴西左翼的主导人物，然而，他现在面对的是自2003年首次执政以来最具挑战性的政治格局。

他将于2027年1月5日开始的新任期，将在国内外重重掣肘之下展开，其中包括来自美国总统唐纳德·特朗普（Donald Trump；川普）的敌意。

虽然特朗普并未直接为卢拉的对手弗拉维奥·博索纳罗背书——他曾在哥伦比亚和洪都拉斯举行的总统选举中为最终获胜的右翼候选人背书——但几乎可以肯定，他的政府更希望看到一位保守派执掌这个拥有2.13亿人口的国家。

白宫将拉丁美洲视为美国的势力范围，特朗普政府热切希望支持其政策的领导人上台执政，包括在国防、安全和贸易方面的政策。

美国政府还热切希望削弱中国在西半球的影响力。

巴西石油资源丰富，并拥有全球第二大稀土矿物储量，是南美洲唯一非右翼领导人执政的大国，而卢拉在很大程度上被视为对华友好。

弗拉维奥·博索纳罗曾承诺让巴西与华盛顿结盟，而卢拉则警告美国不要干预选举，并坚称巴西“绝不会成为任何人的后院”。

不过，尽管白宫可能感到失望，卢拉的胜利将受到环保人士的欢迎。他们曾担心，博索纳罗若胜选，将使巴西颇具影响力的农业综合企业和采矿业获得更大权力。

他们曾指出，在博索纳罗的父亲雅伊尔（Jair Bolsonaro）担任总统期间，亚马逊地区的森林砍伐和森林火灾创下纪录水平，并认为在这位较年轻的博索纳罗治下，更宽松的环境政策可能再次导致这一关键生态系统遭到破坏。

图像来源，Reuters

图像加注文字，2025年，在巴西马拉尼昂州（Maranhao）新中心（Centro Novo）附近举行的联合国气候变化大会（COP30）期间，绿色和平组织（Greenpeace）空中巡查拍摄的航拍画面显示亚马逊雨林中一处正在燃烧的火点

尽管卢拉的支持者对他的胜利欣喜若狂，但选举结果显示这个国家仍然深度分裂，超过48%的选民选择了博索纳罗。

除了团结这个如此严重极化国家的挑战之外，卢拉还将不得不与巴西民主时代最右翼的国会同朝执政。

博索纳罗的自由党（PL）是此次选举中斩获最多的政党。

然而，卢拉的劳工党（Workers' Party）在决选前成功组织了大型集会，显示出该党所拥有的强大基层支持。

选举前，卢拉曾将这次投票形容为“巴西的分水岭”。

他承诺以“新的治理方式”弥合巴西对立政治阵营之间的鸿沟，并在选前的一场WhatsApp直播中补充说，“这个国家将不会再是原来的样子”。

虽然他几乎没有提供有关新治理方式具体内容的细节，但他坚称自己将“坚定不移地为建设一个更公正的国家而奋斗，让人人都有机会，让政策以民众的需求为导向”。

面对一个大致上充满敌意的国会，这场奋斗对这位资深领导人来说——其第四任期结束时将年满85岁——可能会比他此前三次执政时期艰难得多。

## 卢拉：北京在美国后院的“老朋友”

**BBC 中文记者陈岩**

图像来源，Getty Images

卢拉这个名字，在中国并不陌生。作为巴西左翼的代表，卢拉一向乐于与中国发展良好关系。

2023年4月，他对北京进行国事访问，这是他时隔12年重新执政后，首次出访美洲以外的国家，习近平在那次会谈中称他为“老朋友”。

2023年那次访问期间，卢拉专程前往上海，出席罗塞夫出任新开发银行行长的就职典礼。罗塞夫被视为卢拉一手提携的政治接班人，2011年至2016年任巴西总统，卸任后加入新开发银行。

这家银行由金砖国家（BRICs）于2015年成立，总部设在上海。不仅如此，2024年9月，习近平在北京人民大会堂向罗塞夫颁授“友谊勛章”。这是中国对外国人的最高国家荣誉，她也是该批授勛者中唯一的外国人。

颁奖仪式后不到两个月，习近平便访问巴西，受到卢拉的盛情接待。欢迎仪式上，巴西艺术家用中文演唱了《我的祖国》。2025年5月，卢拉再度国事访华，这是他第六次到访中国，也是同一任期内第二次访华。

巴西与中国在农业（尤其是大豆）、矿产等出口产业上的贸易往来十分紧密，但其实卢拉始终强调战略自主，避免选边站队。

卢拉任内，巴西并未直接加入“一带一路”倡议。2024年11月习近平访巴期间，双方签署合作规划，把“一带一路”与巴西的“加速增长计划”等本国发展战略对接。这显示出卢拉的务实取向：既希望通过与中国合作获取经济利益，又坚持把主导权握在自己手里。

中国资本也在加速进入巴西。据巴中企业家委员会统计，2024年中国对巴西直接投资同比增长113%，约42亿美元，巴西跃升为中国全球第三大投资目的地；2025年增至61亿美元，升至第一位。投资领域从石油、电力等传统行业，扩展到新能源汽车、科技和可再生能源制造。比亚迪在巴伊亚州卡马萨里（Camaçari, Bahia）的工厂，2025年10月下线了该公司全球第1400万辆新能源汽车，这辆车最终交付给了卢拉本人。

另一方面，卢拉经常批评美国，也多次抨击美元霸权，希望以金砖国家机制为支点，不必依附华盛顿。但他并未放弃与美国企业合作。

今年8月，卢拉推动的“巴西AI计划”公布超级计算项目，总投资约23亿雷亚尔（4.6亿美元；30.9亿元人民币；151亿元新台币）。其中，里约热内卢的先进计算中心交由华为和科大讯飞两家中国企业合作建设。

另有约10亿雷亚尔用于采购一台高性能超级计算机，外界预计将由美国企业英伟达中标。

同一项战略安排同时纳入中美企业，说明即便与北京关系密切，卢拉也没有在中美之间一边倒。

这一逻辑同样适用于此次大选中卢拉的对手弗拉维奥·博索纳罗。这位参议员是前总统博索纳罗的长子，与父亲一脉相承，强调国家安全和深化对美合作，家族与特朗普交情甚笃，今年5月他刚在华盛顿与特朗普会面。

但选战临近，弗拉维奥也拒绝把外交描绘成中美二选一。他在9月明确表示，若当选，对华关系将以经济务实为原则，“我们不必选边”。

这也折射出许多中等国家面对中美竞争的心态：不愿倒向任何一方成为附庸，而是希望成为两边都想争取的对象，从中获取更大收益。

title: 福田康夫逝世享年90岁 长期亲华的“短暂”日本首相

content:
图像来源，Reuters

图像加注文字，福田康夫任职日本首相仅仅一年，但早已是执政自民党的“影子外相”。

Published 5 小时前

阅读时间: 5 分钟

日本执政自民党宣布，在2007至2008年间担任日本首相的福田康夫已于近日逝世，享年90岁。

[自民党星期一（10月26日）公布](https://www.jimin.jp/news/information/214461.html)，福田康夫上星期四（22日）逝世，葬礼将仅安排近亲参加。共同社等媒体引述消息人士称，福田康夫因心脏功能衰竭，在东京一家医院去世。

福田康夫从上任到辞任首相仅365天，且当时曾招致批评，但中日媒体均指出其致力改善两国关系，包括促成时任中国国家主席胡锦涛访问日本。

现任日本首相高市早苗赞扬福田康夫在任期间“竭尽所能”；中国外交部称呼其为“中国人民的老朋友”。

## 改善中日关系的“终身事业”

福田康夫2007年9月26日就任日本首相，2008年9月24日卸任，前后仅365天。但在此之前，他担任内阁官房长官三年半，是自由民主党政权迄今任期第二长的官房长官。

福田康夫是在[安倍晋三](https://bbc.com/zhongwen/trad/world-62093144)辞去其首次任期后当上执政自民党党总裁与日本首相。他被视为外交“鸽派”，在任内主张改善周边尤其是对华关系。

福田康夫回避安倍晋三修改和平宪法以促进海外军事部署等较具野心的政策，又促成了胡锦涛到访，那是时隔十年来首次有中国国家元首访日。

图像来源，Reuters

图像加注文字，福田康夫担任首相期间，胡锦涛成为了10年来首位访日的中国国家主席。

福田康夫在日本内阁任内也曾处理中日外交冲突：2001年4月，森喜朗内阁与小泉纯一郎内阁交接之际，[东京批准台湾前总统李登辉到访](http://news.bbc.co.uk/hi/chinese/news/newsid_1293000/12931952.stm)，引起北京强烈不满。作为政府首席发言人的内阁官房长官福田康夫为内阁辩护，称是基于人道理由而向李登辉发出签证。

1995年1月，仍只是众议员的福田康夫曾访问台湾，会晤李登辉。当时由中国国民党执政的台湾总统府仍将访问称为“访华”，[官方新闻稿](https://www.president.gov.tw/NEWS/22444)除了称福田康夫“曾多次访华”外，还称他“担任众议员以来，经常给予我国支持与协助”。

共同社指出，由于在官房长官任内积极推动官邸外交，福田康夫这位发言人也被称为“影子外相”。

图像来源，Reuters

图像加注文字，上任约三个月，福田康夫以日本首相身份访华，与时任中国总理温家宝开展“棒球外交”。

[Skip 2007年12月：福田康夫访华 and continue reading](https://bbc.com/zhongwen/articles/cm4g149yw14lo/simp#end-of-article-links-block)**2007年12月：福田康夫访华**

End of 2007年12月：福田康夫访华

辞任首相后，福田康夫于2010年给中国参与创办的博鳌亚洲论坛担任理事长，并连任至2018年，卸任后留任论坛咨询委员会主席。[2025年3月](https://www.news.cn/20250327/be307fbb96fa4948b12aa1c82d14a2f5/c.html)，福田康夫仍有为博鳌论坛年会一场周边会议发表书面致辞。

[2014年7月](https://bbc.com/zhongwen/trad/china/2014/08/140804_japan_china_talks)，中国与日本再次因东海钓鱼岛（日本称尖阁诸岛；台湾称钓鱼台列屿）主权争议陷入外交僵局之际，福田康夫以博鳌论坛理事长身份访华，秘密替二度出任日本首相的安倍晋三传话，呼吁现任中国国家主席习近平同意对话。

“或许连中方也没想到事态会陷入如此僵局。这真是一件令人遗憾的事。”

报导称，福田康夫在专访中也反问了究竟是哪一方制造了对立的火种。

图像来源，Kyodo News/Reuters

图像加注文字，2014年10月，福田康夫在北京会晤习近平。同年7月，福田康夫曾替安倍晋三充当说客，秘密访华斡旋中日外交僵局。

在星期一的例行记者会上，中国外交部对福田康夫逝世表示“沉痛哀悼”。

外交部发言人郭嘉昆说：“福田康夫先生是中国人民的老朋友，为推动中日关系改善发展作出积极贡献。他长期心系中日友好、秉持正确历史观，担任首相期间签署了中日第四份政治文件，卸任后参观了侵华日军南京大屠杀遇难同胞纪念馆。”

郭嘉昆不点名批评高市早苗说：“福田康夫先生曾指出，中日四个政治文件规定了两国关系遵循的原则，必须时刻牢记，不能走回头路。这一表态掷地有声，体现了日本老一辈政治家的信义和担当，日本当政者应当深思自省。”

台湾总统赖清德[透过社交平台X](https://x.com/ChingteLai/status/2114631536826003860)对福田康夫逝世表达“深切哀悼”。

“台日之间由深厚情谊紧密相连。期盼今后双方交流与合作进一步深化，并愿这份无可替代的友谊长久延续。”

图像来源，China News Service

图像加注文字，从日本政坛引退后，福田康夫仍长期参与中国主导的博鳌亚洲论坛工作。

## “前无古人”的首相父子

据NHK报导，高市早苗对福田康夫辞世感到“悲痛”。

高市早苗在首相官邸对记者说：“在丰富的经验和卓越的见识基础上，即使面对极其困难的课题，他也始终竭尽所能，一项一项持续推动相关工作。”

“作为北海道洞爷湖峰会主席，他也大力向世界展现了我国的存在感。”

图像来源，JIJI PRESS/AFP via Getty Images

图像加注文字，2000年10月底，时任日本首相森喜朗（右）任命福田康夫（左）出任内阁官房长官。福田康夫及后成为自民党迄今任期第二长的官房长官。

福田康夫1936年7月16日生于东京，祖籍群马县高崎市，父亲福田赳夫最初是代表群马县选区的众议院议员，后来出任首相。

尽管出身政治世家，福田年轻时对职业政治并没有太大兴趣，在石油公司以“上班族”身分度过了17年。

然而，原本被培养成政治接班人，过继他人的弟弟横手征夫染上重病后，福田康夫接手成为父亲的秘书，并跟随其进入首相官邸任职。

1990年，福田赳夫退休，当时53岁的福田康夫接替父亲参选，并首次当选众议员。

福田康夫先后给森喜朗和小泉纯一郎两任首相担任官房长官，其中小泉纯一郎任内发生美国911恐怖袭击，福田康夫被日本媒体视为该国应对后续影响的主要人物。

图像来源，AFP via Getty Images

图像加注文字，福田康夫被视为外交鸽派，与他曾经的上级小泉纯一郎（左）形成鲜明对比。

当小泉纯一郎的继任人安倍晋三宣布辞职，福田康夫宣布竞逐党总裁，旋即获得党内不同派系支持。[他的当选](http://news.bbc.co.uk/chinese/trad/hi/newsid_7010000/newsid_7011600/7011682.stm)，使福田家成为日本宪政史上首个父子先后出任首相的家族。

但在他出选时，被外界形容为以脾气急躁见称的福田康夫曾笑说，面对国会朝野分立、在野党有能力拖延立法进程的景况，他当选首相“也许是抽到了下下签呢”。

2008年，冲绳发生驻日美军士兵涉嫌强奸14岁女孩事件，[福田康夫对此表示“不可饶恕”](http://news.bbc.co.uk/chinese/trad/hi/newsid_7240000/newsid_7240300/7240367.stm)，但他曾在2003年被国内媒体曝光其私下称，一些女性衣着暴露自招强奸，“穿成那种样子的人自己也有问题”。

作为一个鸽派人物，福田康夫除了主张与中国修补关系外，也对朝鲜（北韩）采取较灵活立场，尤其是在尝试解决[1970至1980年代平壤绑架问题](https://bbc.com/zhongwen/articles/cj03vgl8dz3o/trad)方面。

图像来源，Reuters

图像加注文字，福田康夫当选日本首相，缔造了父子二代先后担任日本政府首脑的历史。

在立法施政受制于在野党派之下，福田康夫执政风格显得被动，其任内爆发的一连串丑闻也逐步侵蚀其民望：年金纪录遗失、军方贿赂丑闻，以及一项因增加老年人负担而引发强烈不满的医疗制度改革。

2008年4月至6月间，日本经济出现萎缩，只要多持续一个季度，日本便技术上进入经济衰退。8月的内阁改组曾短暂提振福田政府的声势，但在此过程中，他也提拔了自己的竞争对手[麻生太郎](http://news.bbc.co.uk/chinese/trad/hi/newsid_7630000/newsid_7633700/7633700.stm)。

[2008年9月1日深夜](http://news.bbc.co.uk/chinese/trad/hi/newsid_7590000/newsid_7592000/7592086.stm)，福田康夫宣布辞任首相，[舆论譁然](http://news.bbc.co.uk/chinese/trad/hi/newsid_7590000/newsid_7594200/7594287.stm)。一些评论指责他“放弃政权”，《每日新闻》更形容其行为属“毫无信念的政治漂流”。9月24日，麻生太郎当选首相，正式接替福田康夫。

一年后，日本举行大选，福田康夫并未参选，且正式宣布退出政坛，由长子福田达夫继承衣钵。

title: 东京专栏 - 中美俄首脑或举行首次首脑峰会  日本担心什么？
summary: 最近，关于于11月18日、19日在中国深圳举行的亚太经济合作组织（APEC）领导人会议，将举行中美俄三国领导人会谈的消息日益显现出实现的现实性，而三国的首脑会谈，也会对把美国作为唯一同盟国的日本造成一定的冲击。 **三国会谈能否真的实现？** 从现在各方面的消息看，三国领导人会谈可能性很大。据多家媒体报道，俄罗斯总统普京于9日与美国总统特朗普举行电话会谈，并提议借下月在中国举行的亚太经济合作组织（APEC）领导人非正式会议之机，举行中美俄三国领导人会谈。 而美国总统特朗普则在
content:
最近，关于于11月18日、19日在中国深圳举行的亚太经济合作组织（APEC）领导人会议，将举行中美俄三国领导人会谈的消息日益显现出实现的现实性，而三国的首脑会谈，也会对把美国作为唯一同盟国的日本造成一定的冲击。

**三国会谈能否真的实现？**

从现在各方面的消息看，三国领导人会谈可能性很大。据多家媒体报道，俄罗斯总统普京于9日与美国总统特朗普举行电话会谈，并提议借下月在中国举行的亚太经济合作组织（APEC）领导人非正式会议之机，举行中美俄三国领导人会谈。

而美国总统特朗普则在19日表示，他愿意最早于11月与中国国家主席习近平、俄罗斯总统普京举行有关军备控制问题的领导人会谈。如果会谈得以实现，这将是三国首脑首次举行此类磋商。

特朗普对记者表示：“我们可能会举行会谈，讨论核武器和无核化问题。”他还说：“如果习近平主席希望举行会谈，我会同意。我们还会讨论贸易等其他问题。”

从目前来的情况看，美国和俄罗斯已经直接表达了希望会谈的意愿，那么中国怎么样呢？

俄罗斯总统助理（负责外交政策事务）乌沙科夫10月21日透露，鉴于中国、俄罗斯和美国可能于下月举行首次三国领导人会谈，中国政府已着手进行相关准备。

乌沙科夫表示：作为APEC领导人非正式会议东道国的中国朋友们，将着手进行相关准备。更准确地说，他们已经开始准备了。如果条件成熟，中国将把三国领导人会谈纳入APEC领导人非正式会议的日程安排。

普京21日在圣彼得堡与美国总统特使威特科夫举行会谈。会谈结束后，乌沙科夫就三国磋商的构想称：“莫斯科、华盛顿和北京都没有拒绝这一设想。”看来三国首脑首次会谈呼之欲出。

**特朗普会不会顺访朝鲜或在中国与金正恩会面引人注目**

在11月3日举行的美国中期选举中，由特朗普总统领导的共和党正面临一场艰难的选战。目前，共和党在国会参众两院维持的多数席位，都有可能被民主党夺走。特朗普在短期内已经无法挽回支持率低迷，四面楚歌的境地，而在外交与安全保障领域，总统依然拥有很大的权力和自由裁量权。这次欲举行中美俄三国首脑会谈，也是希望在外交上得分。

而特朗普会不会再打出另一张“王牌”，即与他称为“亲密朋友”的朝鲜最高领导人金正恩举行一场出人意料的首脑会谈十分引人注目。朝鲜不是亚太经济合作组织成员，特朗普要实现与金正恩的会谈需要顺访朝鲜或在中国与其会谈。

特朗普或许打算从金正恩那里争取到某种让步，取得一定成果，并以此向选民展示政绩。

10月12日，特朗普在白宫接受记者提问时，当被问及其访问亚洲期间是否可能举行美朝首脑会谈时，他回答说：“也许会见面。那将会令人兴奋。” “我和他（金正恩）相处得很好。”可以认为，特朗普借助媒体向朝鲜方面传递了希望举行首脑会谈的信息。

而特朗普在19日（当地时间）在白宫接受记者采访，有记者问特朗普“你认为下个月能在中国与朝鲜领导人会面吗”时，他表示：“不知道。”

但是同时特朗普总统表示：“我和金正恩委员长相处得非常好”，再次强调了自己与金正恩之间的密切关系。他还说：“我不确定他是否希望举行会谈，但我和金正恩的关系非常好。”

而金正恩于10月24日突然访问中国。日本舆论普遍认为，表面上看，金正恩此行是为了纪念中国参加朝鲜战争76周年以及边境大桥通车等活动，但外界认为，其真正目的一方面是向国际社会炫耀中朝关系的“蜜月状态”，另一方有意重开美朝交涉，也可能是为安排在中国进行美朝首脑会谈“打前战”。

如果特朗普能和金正恩见面，不论是否取得什么成果，可能都会给特朗普所领导的共和党在中期选举中加分。

**日本担心什么？**

那么，日本对这次会谈担心什么呢？

首先，如果中美俄首次实现首脑会谈，将对乌克兰战局乃至东北亚的地缘政治产生深刻的影响。中俄朝在安全保障方面都在威胁着日本，如果特朗普与这些对日本的安全保障形成重大威胁的集权国家在某种意义上握手言欢，达成某种合作的共识，那就一定会严重弱化日美同盟和美韩同盟。

第二，日本对三国首脑会谈的举行对将与会的高市早苗首相的外交活动产生的影响比较担心高市早苗的外交空间可能会受到挤压。高市早苗在10月16日的参议院预算委员会会议上，被问及是否会出席11月在中国广东省深圳市举行的亚太经济合作组织（APEC）领导人非正式会议时回答说：“如果能够获得国会的批准，我就会出席。”如果中美韩三国首脑的会谈先于高市首相与特朗普的首脑会谈，那么高市怎样对应与特朗普的会谈将很难预设，针对中俄加强日美同盟的威慑力等话题也将很难开口，高市如何与特朗普讨论三国会谈都将成为外交难题。

日本方面现在也正在积极争取在亚太经济合作组织领导人会议期间实现与中国国家主席习近平的会谈，如果实现了三国首脑会谈，日中首脑会谈可能会因为中国实现了三大国的合作更加蔑视日本，使日中首脑会谈更难实现。

第三，日本担心在中美俄三国会谈中，美国为了从中俄得到更多的利益，在台海安全等方面作出出人意料的让步，那么对一贯认为“台湾有事就是日本有事”的日本来说，就又增加了新的忧虑。

第四，日本担心历史的叠印。美国总统特朗普9月24日在白宫举行的欢迎中国国家主席习近平的仪式上表示，第二次世界大战期间，美国和中国曾是“盟国”（allies）。美国总统在谈及二战时称中国为“盟国”这种说法极为罕见，在日本政府内部和媒体都引起很大波澜。

而这次中美俄首脑会谈，也会令人想起中美俄共同抗日的历史。韩国《韩民族日报》论说委员朴显10月23日在雅虎新闻网上发表题为《中美俄三国首脑会谈会成为“第二次雅尔塔会议”吗？》的文章，在题目和文章中谈及雅尔塔会议。

雅尔塔会议（Yalta Conference）中，美、英、苏三国首脑（罗斯福、丘吉尔、斯大林）签署了一份针对日本的秘密协定，即《苏美英三国关于日本的协定》（通称《雅尔塔协定》或“雅尔塔密约”）， 在协定中苏联正式承诺，在纳粹德国投降且欧洲战争结束后的2至3个月内，参加同盟国方面对日作战。

朴显在文章中指出：“如果此次会谈得以实现，那么，世界三大核大国领导人齐聚一堂的场景本身就将成为一种信号。这可能成为一个象征性场景，预示着一种‘势力范围秩序’的到来——大国之间取代‘基于规则的秩序’，转而决定弱小国家的命运。”

三国能不能像9月中美首脑会谈那样，谈及中美俄共同抗日的历史，也是日本十分担心的。

title: DPP's Shen unveils Taipei waterway plan, attends Halloween event - Focus Taiwan
zh_title: 民进党沉沉公布台北航道规划并出席万圣节活动 - 聚焦台湾
summary: 中新社台北10月26日电 民进党台北市市长候选人沈伯洋周一在参加万圣节活动前提出振兴首都水道，家长们纷纷表示支持他的育儿政策。在台北中正区竞选总部举行的新闻发布会上，沉从新加坡的城市水管理方法中汲取灵感，概述了振兴城市水道的计划。沉说，该计划重点关注五个优先事项——活跃、美丽、清洁、拘留和生态系统——统称为“ABCDE”。规格
content:
中新社台北10月26日电 民进党台北市市长候选人沈伯洋周一在参加万圣节活动前提出振兴首都水道，家长们纷纷表示支持他的育儿政策。

在台北中正区竞选总部举行的新闻发布会上，沉从新加坡的城市水管理方法中汲取灵感，概述了振兴城市水道的计划。

沉说，该计划重点关注五个优先事项——活跃、美丽、清洁、拘留和生态系统——统称为“ABCDE”。

具体措施包括改善淡水河和基隆河沿线的滨水设施，以方便公众使用；利用湿地和植被改善水质；以及在学校和公园建设小型蓄洪设施，以增强城市的防洪能力。

“我们每天都在用水，但我们的城市实际上距离水还很远。”沉说，他认为城市水管理应该融入教育、文化和环境保护，而不是仅仅关注工程。

沉说，在城市发展过程中，台北的许多溪流和灌溉渠道已被覆盖、填平或纳入地下排水系统，使居民与城市的水道疏远。
他说，该举措旨在重新连接居民与这些水道，并使水成为城市规划的核心考虑因素。

## 万圣节活动

周一晚些时候，沉在天母棒球场外的万圣节活动中打扮成船长，戴着爆炸式假发，向孩子们和其他参加者分发糖果。

台北居民韩武是参加此次活动的人之一，他是一位 35 岁的设计师，带着妻子和 2 岁的女儿前来参加。

吴告诉中央社，他不是民进党的坚定支持者，此前曾支持前台北市长柯文哲，但对沉的育儿建议表示欢迎。

其中一项特别吸引他的提议是，沉计划每周为学龄前儿童提供最多四个小时的免费上门托儿服务。

据市政府称，台北市目前在指定设施提供临时托儿服务，其中大多数收费每小时 200 新台币（6.13 美元）。

吴说，提议的免费托儿服务可以提供急需的缓解，因为他和妻子都工作，他们的女儿工作日每天要和保姆一起度过大约 12 个小时。

“我认为这会给父母一些喘息的空间，”他说，并补充说这项服务可以让他们在周末休息或处理紧急情况。

39 岁的艺术教育家 Yinling Hsu 与丈夫和 6 岁的女儿一起参加了这次活动，她说她也被沉的建议所吸引，该建议旨在解决他所说的父母抚养孩子所经历的“孤立”问题。
台北居民许回忆，女儿在幼儿园生病时，她不得不带女儿去上班，因为她和丈夫都工作，而且亲戚都住在台北以外的地方。

她说：“父母通常需要的是在抚养孩子时出现紧急情况时的支持。”她补充说，拟议的每周四小时免费上门托儿服务可以让父母有时间做出其他安排。

台北市政府对沉的提议的可行性提出质疑，社会福利部在 6 月份估计，与该市以前的计划相比，每周需要 414,000 小时的托儿服务。

【原文 English Original】
Taipei, Oct. 26 (CNA) Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) Taipei mayoral candidate Puma Shen (沈伯洋) on Monday proposed revitalizing the capital's waterways before attending a Halloween event where parents expressed support for his childcare policies.

At a news conference at his campaign headquarters in Taipei's Zhongzheng District, Shen outlined a plan to revitalize the city's waterways, drawing inspiration from Singapore's approach to urban water management.

The plan focuses on five priorities -- Active, Beautiful, Clean, Detention and Ecosystem -- collectively known as "ABCDE," Shen said.

Specific measures include improving waterfront facilities along the Tamsui and Keelung rivers to make them more accessible to the public, using wetlands and vegetation to improve water quality, and developing small-scale floodwater retention facilities in schools and parks to strengthen the city's flood control capacity.

"We use water every day, but we are actually very far removed from the water in our city," Shen said, arguing that urban water management should incorporate education, culture and environmental protection rather than focus solely on engineering.

Shen said many of Taipei's streams and irrigation channels had been covered, filled in or incorporated into underground drainage systems during urban development, distancing residents from the city's waterways.

He said the initiative aimed to reconnect residents with these waterways and make water a central consideration in urban planning.

## Halloween event

Later Monday, Shen, dressed as a ship captain and wearing an Afro wig, handed out candy to children and other attendees at a Halloween event outside the Tianmu Baseball Stadium.

Among those at the event was Taipei resident Han Wu, a 35-year-old designer who came with his wife and 2-year-old daughter.

Wu told CNA he was not a staunch DPP supporter and had previously supported former Taipei Mayor Ko Wen-je (柯文哲), but welcomed Shen's childcare proposals.

One proposal that particularly appealed to him was Shen's plan to provide up to four hours of free drop-in childcare per week for preschool children.

Taipei currently offers drop-in childcare at designated facilities, most of which charge NT$200 (US$6.13) per hour, according to the city government.

Wu said the proposed free childcare could provide much-needed relief, as he and his wife both work and their daughter spends around 12 hours a day with a nanny on weekdays.

"I think it would give parents some breathing room," he said, adding that the service could allow them to rest on weekends or deal with emergencies.

Yinling Hsu, a 39-year-old art educator who attended the event with her husband and 6-year-old daughter, said she was also drawn to Shen's proposals to address what he calls the "isolation" experienced by parents raising children.

Hsu, a Taipei resident, recalled having to bring her daughter to work when the child fell ill at kindergarten because both she and her husband worked and their relatives lived outside Taipei.

"What parents often need is support when emergencies come up while raising children," she said, adding that the proposed four hours of free drop-in childcare per week could give parents time to make alternative arrangements.

The Taipei City government has questioned the feasibility of Shen's proposal, with its Department of Social Welfare estimating in June that it would require 414,000 hours of childcare services per week, compared with the city's existing capacity of 130,000 hours.

## Taiwan's local elections

Shen is challenging incumbent Kuomintang Mayor Chiang Wan-an (蔣萬安) in the Nov. 28 local elections.

The elections are also known as the "9-in-1" elections because voters in Taiwan's 22 cities and counties will cast ballots for candidates vying for nine different local government posts, including city mayors, county magistrates, and city and county councilors.

Other positions being contested include township chiefs, chiefs of Indigenous districts in municipalities, township councilors, Indigenous councilors in municipalities and ward chiefs.

In total, elections will be held for 11,051 officials at all levels of local government.

(By Huang Li-yun and Sunny Lai)

title: “自我革命”、持续清洗：习近平为下一任期铺路
source: 纽约时报中文网 国际纵览
summary: 十多年来，中国领导人习近平一直通过一波又一波的反腐调查和忠诚教育运动来约束该国的官员。 如今，73岁的习近平准备争取再执政五年，他抱怨一些官员依然不忠诚、麻木不仁且腐败，并表示需要采取更严厉的措施。 本月，中国共产党宣布对中国西南部城市重庆的前市长[黄奇帆展开调查](https://english.news.cn/20261013/0ec6725bb5b242e69f65dd7866b5259e/c.html "Link: https://english.news.cn/20
content:
十多年来，中国领导人习近平一直通过一波又一波的反腐调查和忠诚教育运动来约束该国的官员。

如今，73岁的习近平准备争取再执政五年，他抱怨一些官员依然不忠诚、麻木不仁且腐败，并表示需要采取更严厉的措施。

本月，中国共产党宣布对中国西南部城市重庆的前市长[黄奇帆展开调查](https://english.news.cn/20261013/0ec6725bb5b242e69f65dd7866b5259e/c.html "Link: https://english.news.cn/20261013/0ec6725bb5b242e69f65dd7866b5259e/c.html")，这充分展现了习近平巩固权力的行动之无情。黄奇帆曾历经数位曾任其上司的党内官员倒台而安然无恙，卸任后也仍然保持活跃，地位显赫。这类调查几乎总是以官员被判刑入狱而告终。

黄奇帆的新闻传出之际，正值党的精英机构中央委员会准备本周在北京举行会议。在[为期四天](https://english.news.cn/20260921/f67fb4c531814047a7954a05f86d6a66/c.html "Link: https://english.news.cn/20260921/f67fb4c531814047a7954a05f86d6a66/c.html")的会议期间，这个由数百名官员组成的群体预计将为习近平明年开启第四个党领导人任期奠定基础，并批准用于审查官员的严格规则。

党正在为其下一届全国代表大会做准备，每五年举行一次的大会旨在宣布领导层的改组。将在2027年晚些时候举行的这次大会上，习近平必须任命一批新的年轻官员在他麾下工作。专家表示，这一背景或许可以解释他为何重新执着于强化服从。

“习近平希望留下怎样的遗产？我认为，首要的是一个更强大的共产党，甚至可能比一个更强大的中国更为重要，”亚洲协会政策研究所中国政治高级研究员[牛犇](https://asiasociety.org/policy-institute/neil-thomas)(Neil Thomas)表示。“在他看来，前者是后者的首要前提。”

2016年，时任重庆市市长黄奇帆在北京。在接受调查之前，作为一名退休官员，他有超乎寻常的公众知名度，经常发表演讲并撰写书籍。Jason Lee/Reuters

再连任五年将巩固习近平作为中国数十年来最具主导地位的领导人这一地位，尤其是因为他[没有明确的接班人](https://cn.nytimes.com/china/20251021/china-communist-succession-plenum/ "Link: https://cn.nytimes.com/china/20251021/china-communist-succession-plenum/")。

但是，牛犇和他的同事在一份关于这次党内会议的[前瞻中写道](https://asiasociety.org/policy-institute/limits-xis-control-what-watch-chinas-fifth-plenum)，习近平“对那些本应执行其意愿的人始终感到失望”。

现届中央委员会在2022年上届党代会成立时共有[376名成员](http://english.news.cn/special/cpc20/documents.html)。但习近平的清洗行动造成了严重减员。在去年的委员会会议上，出席人数[降至315名官员](https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202510/24/WS68faba01a310f735438b6991.html "Link: https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202510/24/WS68faba01a310f735438b6991.html")。考虑到已经被开除、受调查或失踪的官员，本周的出席人数可能会降至约300人甚至更少。

习近平在今年早些时候的一篇讲话中（该讲话[于本月发表](https://www.qstheory.cn/20261015/a6ed86729ae947d99a83bb431867b7d3/c.html)）表示，有太多的官员未能忠实地执行命令，反而假装顺从。他说，有些人是“两面人”，在忠诚的面具背后隐藏着对党的规则和价值观的蔑视。他将腐败官员比作有病的树木，表示党应该做到“‘病树’该拔就拔、该伐就伐”。

习近平议程中的很大一部分是管理拥有[1.01亿党员](https://www.12371.cn/2026/06/30/ARTI1782784973166823.shtml)的中国共产党的繁重日常工作，这些党员中很多是官员。正是通过这套党内机制，习近平得以管理世界第二大经济体并统治14亿人口。自2012年上台以来，他将党的触角延伸到工厂、村庄、学校以及社会的几乎每一个角落，重塑了党的权威。

**自我革命**

习近平似乎认为，中国官场的诸多问题根源于纪律松懈和思想软弱。他对此给出的药方是“自我革命”，这是一项由持续检查、自我评估和批判会议组成的计划，旨在让干部保持警觉。

“自我革命”并没有放缓。根据官方数据，2023年，[检查人员惩处了49名省部级干部](http://politics.people.com.cn/n1/2024/0125/c1001-40166029.html)和2.4万名县处级干部；而去年，[对应的数字](https://www.news.cn/politics/20260117/b67fae3369f449b68d45d6bee8a010ff/c.html)分别为69人和3.5万人。

习近平的整肃行动最近在军队中最为剧烈。今年早些时候，中国最高级别的将领张又侠被[拘留](https://cn.nytimes.com/china/20260511/china-military-generals/)，并被[指控腐败](https://cn.nytimes.com/china/20260922/china-generals-expelled-corruption/)和不忠。自2022年以来，已有[约100名高级军官](https://cn.nytimes.com/china/20260225/china-military-purges-xi/)接受调查，或直接失踪，很可能正在接受调查。

2023年，张又侠（中）在当选中央军委副主席后宣誓就职。张又侠随后被拘留，并被指控贪腐。Greg Baker/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images

“反腐运动已经不再是一场临时运动了，因为它已经变得如此常态化，”维也纳大学中国政治与法律讲师[李玲](https://ufind.univie.ac.at/en/person.html?id=60055)表示。“一方面，由于腐败机会的减少，给官员的‘胡萝卜’变小了。另一方面，‘大棒’正变得越来越重。”

在明年的党代会召开之前，对官员的审查可能会进一步加剧。由于长期的房地产危机，中国经济有所放缓，也重创了长期依赖土地出让收入的地方政府财政。习近平希望确保，尽管面临种种困难，官员们仍能坚定致力于他的领导，以及将中国建设成为技术先进的超级大国的议程。

“历史表明，在困难时期，党代会召开时可能会出现不同的声音，”李玲说。“注入恐惧感将使达成共识变得更加容易。”

前重庆市长黄奇帆的落马可能会引发一阵恐慌。

74岁的黄奇帆在八年前就从主要公职岗位上退休，但他保持着超乎寻常的高调公众形象，经常就经济问题发表演讲并撰写书籍。但随后调查人员宣布他因“严重违纪违法”正在接受调查。上周，[党还宣布](https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202610/22/WS6ad9dc5ee4b06d4aa056440a.html "Link: https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202610/22/WS6ad9dc5ee4b06d4aa056440a.html")北京市副市长夏林茂正在接受调查。

**前反腐高官是否陷入麻烦？**

党内调查人员最近的其他举措表明，习近平的怀疑可能延伸到了更高的层级，甚至可能包括78岁的前中央纪律检查委员会书记王岐山。王岐山曾负责监督习近平反腐行动的第一阶段工作，现已退休。

王岐山的几位长期助手已因涉嫌腐败被拘留，包括金融领域官员周亮和纪检官员黎晓宏。王岐山的另一位[前秘书](https://news.inewsweek.cn/politics/2026-06-04/30474.shtml)董宏于2022年[因腐败指控被判刑](https://english.news.cn/20220128/86a0f11ae8f94788b060a325ff91d77d/c.html)。今年，[王岐山的两名前下属](https://web.archive.org/web/20261020104155/https://www.ccdi.gov.cn/toutiaon/202608/t20260828_509362.html)被降职，不再担任中央纪律检查委员会的职务，这表明他们可能也处于阴影之下。

王岐山的助手成为目标的具体原因尚不清楚，王岐山本人也没有被指控有违法行为。但这些案件引发了人们的猜测，认为习近平对于退休官员可能通过其网络和门生保留的影响力保持警惕。

2023年，习近平在北京与王岐山握手。王岐山曾负责监督习近平反腐败运动的第一阶段工作，但王岐山本人的一些长期助手后来却成为纪律检查机关的调查对象。Noel Celis/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images

“我能理解习近平的想法，王岐山即使为他做了那么多脏活累活，但他依然是少数有能力、甚至有足够胆量给习近平制造麻烦的人之一，”布鲁金斯学会研究中国政治的研究员、曾在美国中央情报局工作过的[秦江南](https://www.brookings.edu/people/jonathan-a-czin/)(Jonathan Czin)表示。“这关乎习近平的心态以及他对风险的认知。”

这种看似无休止的审查带来的负面效应在于，习近平可能会发现，越来越难确保数以百万计基层官员保持工作积极性。[最近的一项研究](https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/doi/abs/10.1086/738564)发现，官员们往往不敢承担风险。他们有时感到彻底丧失干劲。

“地方政府——尤其是农村地区的地方政府——没有能力和资源去满足中央层层下达的所有要求，”该研究的合著者、澳大利亚国立大学教授[本杰明·希尔曼](https://researchportalplus.anu.edu.au/en/persons/benjamin-hillman/)表示。“地方官员有时不得不弄虚作假。”

【大紀元2026年10月26日訊】（大紀元記者林丹紐約報導）中國新時代人民黨（簡稱中國新民黨）10月24日在紐約法拉盛舉行集會，紀念第81個聯合國日，呼籲「把中共從聯合國趕出去」。與會者回顧中華民國參與創建聯合國的歷史，批評中共對民主國家及國際組織的滲透，並提出廢止聯大第2758號決議、推動聯合國改革等主張。

[![Image 6: 中國新民黨法拉盛集會紀念聯合國日，籲將中共逐出聯合國。](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14876704-195445-450x253.jpeg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14876704-195445-450x253.jpeg)

中國新民黨法拉盛集會紀念聯合國日，籲將中共逐出聯合國。（主辦方提供）

活動現場展示中華民國國旗，並拉起「紀念聯合國日，把中共從聯合國趕出去」及「抵抗才有希望，革命才是出路」等橫幅。

中國新民黨創辦人楊茂森表示，中華民國是聯合國創始會員國，也是首個簽署《聯合國憲章》的國家。中共取得中國在聯合國的代表權後，向民主國家，尤其是美國及聯合國各機構滲透，企圖以極權專制的價值觀改變二戰後建立的國際秩序，已對自由民主世界構成嚴重威脅。

他說，國際社會應重新審視中國在聯合國的代表權問題，並呼籲讓聯合國「回歸法律，回歸常識，回歸常態」。

中華民國海外公民委員會執行長曹勝華指出，1971年通過的聯大第2758號決議應該廢止廢止。他認為，這項決議使中共得以取代中華民國在聯合國的代表，國際社會應正視其後續影響。

曹勝華表示，蘇聯解體並不意味著民主與共產體制之間的對抗已經結束。他批評中共採取「韜光養晦」策略，利用民主國家提供的發展機會逐步壯大，最終試圖以專制價值觀改變世界秩序，呼籲美國及其他民主國家提高警覺。

他建議，由美國總統川普聯合烏克蘭及中華民國政府，推動召開聯合國創始會員國領袖會議，重申聯合國成立初衷，商討改革事宜。

中華民國國軍老兵關愛中心董事長胡福慶則關注俄羅斯入侵烏克蘭及台海安全。他表示，身為安理會常任理事國，俄羅斯發動侵略戰爭，中共則頻繁以軍事演習威脅台灣，這些情況與聯合國維護和平的宗旨背道而馳。

中國新民黨成員白祺帆回顧柏林圍牆倒塌、東歐民主化及蘇聯解體，指出蘇聯共產黨、東歐社會主義政權解體展現了人民追求自由、擺脫共產統治的力量。

聯合國日定於每年10月24日，紀念《聯合國憲章》於1945年當日生效。活動由中國新民黨創始人楊茂森組織，王建盾、張偉明、白祺帆、曹勝華、胡福慶、林學軍等人參加。

## 中国市场放缓，英国传统精英私立学校纷纷进军印度

图像来源，Harrow School, Bengaluru

图像加注文字，在哈罗公学的班加罗尔（Bengaluru）校区，学生们穿着传统的哈罗帽子和制服。

*       *   Author, 尼基尔·伊南达尔（Nikhil Inamdar）
    *   Role, 印度孟买报道

*   Published 1 小时前

*   阅读时间: 3 分钟

位于印度西北部旁遮普邦（Punjab）昌迪加尔（Chandigarh）市郊，一间拥有473年历史的英国传统公学今年开设首个全女子国际校园。

与英格兰贝德福德郡（Bedfordshire）校园内标志性的哥德式中央建筑相比，印度校舍采用较现代化设计，设有专门兴建的教学大楼。但校园内一座醒目的红砖钟楼，仍保留着这所英国学校的传统印记。

位于莫哈利（Mohali）的贝德福德学校（Bedford School）是最新一所在印度设校的英国公学。至少已有六所英国公学（历史悠久的精英私立收费学校），包括三所在英国历史最悠久的学校，近年陆续在印度各地开设校园。

它们的扩张，正值中国市场环境趋紧，以及英国自2025年1月1日起对私立学校学费征收增值税（VAT）之际。

自2023年起，素有印度“矽谷”之称、汇聚大量软件和初创企业的班加罗尔（Bengaluru），已成为著名的哈罗公学（Harrow School）在印度的据点。印度首任总理尼赫鲁（Jawaharlal Nehru）便毕业于该校。

思贝礼学校（Shrewsbury School）则在印度中部城市博帕尔（Bhopal）设立校园；而威灵顿学院（Wellington College）选择落户浦那（Pune）。这座印度西部城市因拥有享负盛名的大学和学院而自称为“东方牛津”。

据报，米尔菲尔德学校（Millfield）、伊利沙伯女王学校（Queen Elizabeth's School）以及其他几所英国学校，未来数年亦将在印度开设分校。

数十年来，印度一直设有仿照英国殖民时期公学制度运作的寄宿学校，主要服务精英和贵族家庭。然而，随着新兴富裕阶层壮大，愈来愈多印度家庭希望让子女接触更国际化的教育，市场亦迅速扩展。

哈罗公学的班加罗尔分校校长卡洛琳·帕斯科（Caroline Pascoe）向BBC表示：“我们的国际课程对许多家长而言是一大吸引力。”

哈罗公学及贝德福德学校是印度少数提供完整剑桥课程（Cambridge curriculum）的学校之一，涵盖小学至高考（A-level）阶段。剑桥课程是一套全球教育体系，目前获全球约10,000所学校采用。

图像来源，Bedford School, Mohali

图像加注文字，至少六间英国公学进入印度，最新的一所是贝德福德学校。

哈尔西姆兰·辛格·科查尔（Harsimran Singh Kocchar）的大家族本身就在印度经营连锁学校，但他仍决定把五岁女儿帕丽妮特（Parineet）送入莫哈利的贝德福德学校。

他表示，原因在于学校“重视品格培养及自信，而不只是学业成绩”。

辛格又说，吸引他的另一个因素，是学校不像许多印度同类学校般存在“VIP文化”。

他说：“所有孩子都被一视同仁对待。部长和高级官员的子女不会享有较多特权。”

帕斯科表示，除了愈来愈多富裕的本地家庭外，海外印度人亦是这些学校的重要市场，包括长年在外国生活后回流印度的人士，以及仍居于英国或中东、希望子女保持与印度文化联系的家庭。

哈罗公学班加罗尔校区有60%的教职员来自海外。与其他英国公学一样，该校把自身独特传统带到印度校园。教师被称为“Beaks”，学生穿着传统哈罗帽和校服，并参加“The Long Ducker”跨国赛跑，该活动在哈罗全球各校同步举行。

校内亦设有英式教育标志性的“学院制度”。

这些充满英国传统色彩的校园文化，同时融入印度本地习俗，例如每天早上齐唱印度国歌，以及庆祝印度教重要节日象神节（Ganesh Chaturthi）。

图像来源，Harrow School, Bengaluru

图像加注文字，像班加罗尔的哈罗公学这样的学校会鼓励学生参加音乐和戏剧等课外活动。

印度不断增强的经济实力，以及迅速增加的新晋百万富翁人口，为英国公学扩张提供了有利条件，但这波增长部分亦是受到中国市场放缓所推动。

过去十年间，英国公学海外扩张很大程度上依赖中国和香港市场。目前由50所英国学校营运的151个海外分校校区中，有一半位于中国和香港。

不过，根据英国智库“私立教育政策论坛”（Private Education Policy Forum，PEPF）于2025年[发表的研究](https://www.pepf.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/SatelliteCampuses_PEPFReport_270525.pdf)，随着监管政策改变，以及各国政府加强审查甚至出现抗拒态度，相关增长已经放缓。

PEPF指出，中国于2024年实施的新法例要求学校将爱国主义教育融入所有学科，进一步增加海外学校在中国发展的挑战，甚至导致部分原定兴建的校园计划被取消。这促使有关学校开始考虑印度和越南等其他市场。

此外，英国在2024年秋季财政预算案中宣布对私立学校学费征收20%增值税（VAT）。莫哈利贝德福德学校（Bedford School Mohali）创校校长娜欧蜜·阿特金斯（Naomi Atkins）表示，这项措施迫使许多私立学校寻求海外发展机会。

她向BBC表示：“它们正处于非常艰难的处境。即使是过去从未考虑国际扩张的学校，如今也突然开始积极进入印度市场。”

图像来源，Harrow School, Bengaluru

图像加注文字，在印度，富裕的当地家庭和海外印度人是英国学校的主要目标市场。

不过，阿特金斯承认，印度并非一个容易开拓的市场。

这些学校大多透过与当地投资者或营运商合作设立分校。

阿特金斯表示，过去在其他国家，英国学校一般可从合作伙伴收取相当于收入10%的费用，但在印度，利润率在某些情况下可能低至仅1%。

她又表示，部分学校亦高估了印度市场的规模。

尽管印度有接近2.5亿名在学学生，但英语教育早已深深植根当地，来自本土学校的竞争远较中国、韩国或越南等非英语国家激烈得多。

此外，印度人均收入仍然较低，而英国学校的高昂学费亦限制了增长空间。部分学校的全寄宿学费可高达15,000英镑甚至更高。

阿特金斯说：“我曾在印尼、马来西亚和中国工作，但印度人对价格敏感得多，他们喜欢寻找划算的选择。”

正因如此，莫哈利贝德福德学校的学费约为其他英国学校的一半。

根据PEPF数据，2011/12学年至2022/23学年间，英国学校海外分校共录得1.524亿英镑利润，而且相关收益多年来显著增长。

不过，在印度，这些学校的发展看来更可能是缓慢而稳定，而非爆发式增长。

印度的殖民历史背景，以及新兴富裕阶层的崛起，确实为这些历史悠久的英国学校带来可观的商机，但至少在短期内，这个市场规模仍不足以弥补中国市场萎缩造成的损失。

我们使用了人工智慧协助翻译这篇文章，它的原文是英文。在发布之前，BBC记者检查了翻译的内容。

_山姆·沃德插图_

中国秘密警察拘留了你。

这场磨难始于安全人员的突然袭击。他们指控你犯罪，限制你并将你推入车内。你被蒙上头巾或蒙住眼睛，戴上手铐，绑架到秘密地点，关在有软垫的牢房里，并以“危害中国”的罪名威胁要严惩。与此同时，你的家和办公室也会被搜查。

如果你是这个政权的批评者，长期担心它有一天可能会对你不利，那么这可能是一个奇怪的解脱时刻：你最坏的情况已经出现。如果你认为自己了解规则并且可以依靠官方联系或当局的合理性，那么你会经历幻想破灭和信任背叛的震惊。

您很难适应单独监禁和感官剥夺。房间里只有一张硬铺；你只有几件衣服和基本的洗漱用品。没有镜子——甚至无法保证看到自己的脸。最令人抓狂的是，你不能出去。你的宇宙现在以几平方英尺来衡量。
拘留你的便衣公安或国家安全人员不会告诉任何人你的位置或情况。法律赋予您聘请律师并咨询律师的权利。但在国家安全案件中，它还授权你的狱卒拒绝与律师接触，他们肯定会这样做，至少在他们完成对你的讯问和立案之前，这可能需要一年的时间。

与亲人和朋友、与世界、与自己的身份隔绝，你会体验到孤独的寒意和对联系的渴望。从现在开始，你唯一的人际关系就是与绑架者的关系。人权律师隋牧青回忆道，“思念家人的痛苦是最严重的痛苦”，这代表了许多人的心声。

> 电影中对酷刑的描述通过震撼和奇观实现，而指定居所监视居住则通过全面性和持续时间实现。根据法律，这种刑期最长可达六个月，随后通常会被判处数年拘留和监禁。它造成的伤疤持续时间更长。
这种令人心碎的经历是人权非政府组织保障卫士出版的最新一期《失踪者人民共和国》的主题。第三版收集了中国和外国公民被中国共产党安全机构绑架的新第一人称叙述，该程序被称为“指定居所监视居住”或简称“指居”。官方的英文翻译是“指定地点居住监视”（RSDL），这是一种平淡的官僚口气，故意掩盖逮捕前在秘密设施中的拘留，在那里，你的折磨者让你遭受骇人听闻的虐待，而你唯一的权利就是服从。

[![图2](https://www.thewirechina.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Cheng-Lei-On-Life-in-Chinese-Prison.png)](https://www.thewirechina.com/2026/01/04/heng-lei-on-life-in-chinese-prison/)
在撰写本书的前言时，我想反映他人的痛苦和生存，而不是讲述我自己在 2018 年至 2021 年期间作为[政治人质](https://www.strategicnarratives.org/p/ Five-years-of-freedom-and-the-prc)的经历。

我分析了其中的十篇文章和前两版中的几篇文章，以及中华人民共和国成立之初到现在的囚犯的故事。我还读了最近的[回忆录](https://www.harpercollins.com/products/ Cheng-lei- Cheng-lei?variant=4

【原文 English Original】
_Illustration by Sam Ward_

China’s secret police have detained you.

The ordeal begins with a surprise raid by security officers. They accuse you of crimes, restrain you and shove you into a vehicle. You are hooded or blindfolded, handcuffed, abducted to a secret location, locked in a padded cell, and threatened with severe punishment for “harming China”. Meanwhile, your home and office are searched.

If you are a critic of the regime who has lived with the perennial anxiety that it might one day move against you, this can be a moment of strange relief: your worst-case scenario has unfolded. If you thought you understood the rules and could count on official connections or the reasonableness of the authorities, you experience the shock of illusions dispelled and trust betrayed.

You struggle to adjust to solitary confinement and sensory deprivation. The room has only a hard bunk; you have only a few articles of clothing and basic toiletries. There are no mirrors — not even the reassurance of seeing your own face. Most maddeningly, you cannot go out. Your universe is now measured in a few square feet.

The plainclothes Public Security or State Security officers holding you won’t inform anyone of your location or conditions. The law entitles you to retain and consult a lawyer. But in state security cases, it also empowers your jailers to deny access to counsel, which they are sure to do, at least until they have finished questioning you and building their case, which could take a year.

Disconnected from loved ones and friends, from the world, from your own identity, you experience a chill of isolation and a longing for connection. From now on, your only human relationships are with your captors. Human rights lawyer Sui Muqing speaks for many when he recalls that “the pain of missing my family was the worst suffering.”

> What cinematic depictions of torture achieve through shock and spectacle, RSDL accomplishes through comprehensiveness and duration. By law it can last up to six months, usually followed by years of detention and prison. The scars it inflicts last much longer.

That soul-crushing experience is the subject of the latest edition of _People’s Republic of the Disappeared_, a new book published by the human rights NGO Safeguard Defenders. This third edition collects new first-person accounts of both PRC and foreign citizens abducted by the Chinese Communist Party’s security apparatus under a sinister procedure it calls _zhiding jusuo jianshi juzhu_ 指定居所监视居住 or _zhiju_ 指居 for short. The official English translation is “Residential Surveillance at a Designated Location” (RSDL), a bland bureaucratic mouthful that deliberately masks pre-arrest detention in a secret facility where your tormentors subject you to appalling abuse and your only right is to obey.

[![Image 2](https://www.thewirechina.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Cheng-Lei-On-Life-in-Chinese-Prison.png)](https://www.thewirechina.com/2026/01/04/cheng-lei-on-life-in-chinese-prison/)
In writing this book’s foreword I wanted to reflect the suffering and survival of others, rather than relating my own experience as a [political hostage](https://www.strategicnarratives.org/p/five-years-of-freedom-and-the-prc) from 2018–2021.

I analyzed its ten essays and several more from the two previous editions, as well as stories of prisoners from the PRC’s early decades to the present. I also read the recent [memoir](https://www.harpercollins.com/products/cheng-lei-cheng-lei?variant=46124399886370) of Cheng Lei, the Australian broadcast journalist whose stint as a CGTN news anchor was abruptly terminated by Ministry of State Security agents in 2020. They detained her in retaliation against Australian policies that had enraged their Communist Party masters. Together, these accounts reveal an enduring core curriculum of fear, coercive interrogation, thought remolding and forced submission to the power of the Party-state.

Through its control of all four dimensions in RSDL, especially time, the state becomes the sole point of reference. Blackout curtains cover the windows. With no clocks, no daylight and constant artificial light, circadian rhythms come unanchored. At least for the initial months, there will be nothing to read and no correspondence with the outside world beyond 30-minute consular meetings if you’re a foreign citizen. Monotony turns hours into eternity.

Footage from Canada’s CTV News of Michael Kovrig and Michael Spavor’s return to Canada, following their release from detention on September 24, 2021. _Credit: [CTV News](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vaNnjv24E6Y)_

Humans are wired to avoid uncertainty, but in RSDL the unpredictable becomes the only certainty. You don’t know where you are, how long you will be there, what they will do next, or whether you will survive with your sanity intact. What cinematic depictions of torture achieve through shock and spectacle, RSDL accomplishes through comprehensiveness and duration. By law it can last up to six months, usually followed by years of detention and prison. The scars it inflicts last much longer.

Solitary confinement feels like a kind of [social death](https://academic.oup.com/minnesota-scholarship-online/book/24160?login=false) that dissolves your identity and ability to make sense of a world that has apparently forgotten you. “If they just dug a hole and threw me into it, maybe no one would even know,” recalls women’s rights activist Li Qiaochu. With no social contact, anxiety overwhelms your ability to self-regulate. United Nations standards prohibit solitary confinement over more than fifteen consecutive days, beyond which it can amount to [torture](https://docs.un.org/en/A/66/268), according to the UN’s special rapporteur on the subject. Other UN experts deem RSDL an [enforced disappearance](https://ishr.ch/toolbox/resources/briefing-paper-un-experts-documentation-of-residential-surveillance-at-a-designated-location-rsdl-in-china/) and call for its end. Your jailers do not care.

An excerpt from the UN Special Rapporteur of the Human Rights Council’s interim [report](https://docs.un.org/en/A/66/268) on torture and other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment, 2011.

Surveillance and control are absolute. Escape and privacy are impossible. Cameras track your every gesture, as do the two guards who are always in the cell with you. They watch you sleep, shower and use the toilet. They may stand or sit beside you, encroaching on your personal space. They communicate only to give orders or fetch necessities. Adding to the humiliation, even your most basic acts and needs require their permission. Bathing is a privilege, not a right. You learn to handwash your clothes in a basin and wipe your cell clean.

The guards restrict your position and posture, forcing you to sit for hours in an interrogation chair, or on your bunk; to stand all day, or only sleep in certain positions, hands always visible. Your body stiffens, aches and grows weak from immobility and inadequate nutrition. Physical deterioration ensues. As muscles atrophy, the will follows.

If your case has drawn outside pressure and attention, they may not actively escalate your suffering further, instead counting on time to grind you down. For the less fortunate, more aggressive torture tactics can include vicious beatings and relentless verbal abuse. You might be forced, as Xie Yang was, to sit for hours at a time on a high stool, legs dangling, not reaching the ground, pressure swelling the legs and causing excruciating pain.

> A common tactic is to create a prisoner’s dilemma by warning (perhaps falsely) that others who know you have already confessed and incriminated you. Fear and shame become viruses you are exposed to daily, until your mental immune system collapses.

If that proves insufficient to force your compliance, officials may deprive you of sleep for days, as they did to several of these writers. Sleep deprivation is insidiously debilitating: it impairs reasoning, judgement, inhibition, memory and attention, and can induce hallucinations, delusions and paranoia. It also increases sensitivity to pain and disrupts hormones and the immune system. The world becomes incoherent, false memories arise, and you become compliant, emotionally dependent, easily suggestible, and unable to evaluate consequences. Like hunger and immobility, lack of sleep erodes your will to resist without leaving physical evidence.

A Cultural Revolution poster which says ‘Adhere to the truth, rectify mistakes; strengthen unity, forge ahead courageously!’. _Credit: [ChinesePosters.net](https://chineseposters.net/posters/d85-256)_

These stress and torture tactics soften you up for hundreds of hours of interrogation. Your case officers combine questioning methods from Chinese police procedures with thought reform and political loyalty techniques that date back to the Communist Party’s even more vicious early decades. Endless gaslighting narratives invert reality, casting you as the wrongdoer and these thugs as agents of righteous authority. They question not only your actions and motives, but your worldview, through relentless repetition compelling you to revise it to match their manufactured one. RSDL thus becomes a form of forced labor in which your daily toil is to answer your masters while they try to humiliate you into begging for mercy. From now on, as Li Qiaochu writes, “living is just being ceaselessly interrogated.”

In this war of psychological attrition, the officers meticulously go through the file they surely have on you for anything they might distort to incriminate you. A stray text message, your WeChat contacts, a business card, an email … anything they can access. Through hour after hour of circuitous questioning, they lie to you, twist your words, try to trick you into incriminating others, and incessantly harp on the slightest inconsistency. A common tactic is to create a prisoner’s dilemma by warning (perhaps falsely) that others who know you have already confessed and incriminated you. Fear and shame become viruses you are exposed to daily, until your mental immune system collapses.

[Safeguard Defenders](https://safeguarddefenders.com/en)’ book _The People’s Republic of the Disappeared_ (3rd edition)

Interrogations cycle between pressure and rapport, cruelty and kindness. They manipulate you with circular reasoning such as, “if you didn’t do anything against the law, then why are you here?” Through endless repetitions of this Kafkaesque logic, their premise justifies itself through familiarity, while your truth is rendered meaningless. RSDL authenticates itself within its own closed system.

The shifts from questioning to isolation and back are jarring. Loneliness makes you yearn for interaction and more willing to comply to maintain it — even with your tormentors. Cooperating may earn small privileges: books to read, movement, better food, and hints that you can hasten the process and lighten your sentence through compliance. By turning basic rights into special favors, they create feedback loops of learned helplessness that condition your brain’s reward centers to crave obedience as a means of survival.

Fail to comply and the interrogators could remind you of the pain your disappearance is causing your loved ones, stoke fears that defiance means never seeing them again, or even threaten to harm them as well. The mental anguish can break the strongest of wills. As Taiwanese human rights advocate Lee Ming-Che recounts, “the officers exploited my mental fragility with calculated threats and promises, preying on my desperation.”

Psychologically and biochemically, RSDL shakes the [three foundational conditions](https://psycnet.apa.org/doiLanding?doi=10.1037%2F0003-066X.55.1.68) of human wellbeing: agency (autonomous control over your own mind, body and actions); stability and predictability; and connection — the social ties through which we regulate our emotions.

Left: Lee Mi

title: How Taiwan’s November Local Elections Could Change the World
zh_title: 台湾 11 月地方选举将如何改变世界
summary: 从左到右：2026 年 10 月 10 日，李家芬、立法院院长韩国瑜、总统赖清德、第一夫人吴美如和副总统萧碧琴出席在台北举行的台湾双十国庆庆祝活动。_图片来源：总统府，来自 [Flickr](https://flic.kr/p/2sFrV8Y)_中期选举后，11 月举行的另一场选举也对全球安全至关重要。曾被《经济学人》称为“地球上最危险的地方”的台湾，将于11月28日举行市长和县长选举，为2028年总统大选奠定基础。
content:
从左到右：李家芬、立法院院长韩国瑜、总统赖清德、第一夫人吴美如和副总统萧碧琴于2026年10月10日在台北出席台湾双十国庆庆典。_图片来源：总统府 via [Flickr](https://flic.kr/p/2sFrV8Y)_

尽管许多人都关注美国中期选举，但 11 月的另一场选举也对全球安全至关重要。曾被《经济学人》称为“地球上最危险的地方”的台湾将于 11 月 28 日举行市长和地方法官选举。他们将为 2028 年总统竞选奠定基础，并带来华盛顿和北京之间爆发危机的风险。

台湾中央选举委员会于 2024 年 1 月 19 日正式认证赖清德和萧美琴当选总统和副总统。_图片来源： [DPP](https://www.facebook.com/photo.php?fbid=954044309418660&set=pb.100044392990655.-2207520000&type=3)_

凭借精明的竞选活动，台湾执政的民进党（DPP）有可能在反对派国民党（KMT）的据点中遭遇历史性的颠覆。民进党在 11 月的关键胜利将反过来推动台湾总统赖清德在 2028 年的连任竞选，但赖清德的胜利也预示着来自北京的更严厉的军事胁迫。
11月民进党的崛起意味着2028年的总统竞选很可能将由黎智英与台湾第二大城市台中市的温和国民党市长卢秀岩对决。现在这有可能成为一场势均力敌的竞争，增加了北京明年通过经济甚至军事压力介入的可能性。

中国海警和其他机构已经开始进行登船练习，使台湾以东的航行正常化，并对前往台湾港口的外国船只进行拦截。这些举动显然是对台湾实施经济隔离的准备。如果黎智英和民进党在 11 月的选举中占据优势，中国可能会在 2028 年投票前试图恐吓台湾选民，或许会实施软封锁。

###### **台湾2028年对阵已定**

习近平和国民党主席郑立文，北京，2026 年 4 月 10 日。_图片来源：发言人毛宁，来自 [X](https://x.com/SpoxCHN\_MaoNing/status/2042557566820196766/photo/1)_
国民党2028年的潜在候选人范围正在迅速缩小。饱受争议的国民党主席郑丽媛野心勃勃地获得提名，但她的毒性如此之大，以至于该党的候选人在今年 11 月的选举竞选活动中都彻底避开了她。她缺乏执政经验和亲中立场——在四月份与习近平的谄媚会面中表现得最为明显——意味着她几乎没有从台湾公众那里赢得[信任](https://www.setn.com/news/1864142)。

国民党在 11 月表现不佳将浇灭郑的总统野心，并迫使她辞去党主席职务。这也将使卢秀妍成为国民党2028年提名的最有力竞争者。卢在即将到来的选举中任期有限，因此将不得不辞去八年后的台中市长职务，从而腾出时间参加总统竞选。

卢是一个相对温和的人，主张增加军费开支，并[批评](https://www.hakkatv.org.tw/news-detail/1668400819682072)她自己的政党与中国结盟过于紧密。她还培养了一种协作[关系](https://www.cna.com.tw/news/aipl/2025072701

【原文 English Original】
From left to right: Lee Chia-fen, Legislative Yuan President Han Kuo-yu, President Lai Ching-te, First Lady Wu Mei-ju, and Vice President Hsiao Bi-khim attending Taiwan's Double Tenth National Day celebration in Taipei, October 10, 2026. _Credit: 總統府 via [Flickr](https://flic.kr/p/2sFrV8Y)_

While many eyes are on the U.S. midterms, another set of November elections also matters for global security. Taiwan, which _The Economist_ once called “the most dangerous place on Earth”, holds mayoral and magistrate elections on November 28. They will set the field for the 2028 presidential race, and with it the risk of a crisis between Washington and Beijing.

Taiwan’s Central Election Commission formally certify the election of Lai Ching-te and Hsiao Bi-khim as President and Vice President, January 19, 2024. _Credit: [DPP](https://www.facebook.com/photo.php?fbid=954044309418660&set=pb.100044392990655.-2207520000&type=3)_

Taiwan’s ruling Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) is within reach of historic upsets in strongholds of the opposition Kuomintang (KMT), thanks to shrewd campaigning. Key DPP wins in November would in turn turbocharge Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te’s reelection campaign in 2028 — but a Lai win would also portend harder military coercion from Beijing.

A DPP surge in November would mean the 2028 presidential field would most likely pit Lai against Lu Shiow-yen, the moderate KMT mayor of Taichung, Taiwan’s second-largest city. This now has the potential to be a close race, raising the chances that Beijing will get involved through economic or even military pressure next year.

The China Coast Guard (CCG) and other agencies have already been practicing ship boardings, normalizing movements east of Taiwan, and hailing foreign vessels heading to Taiwanese ports. These moves are clearly a form of preparation for imposing an economic quarantine on Taiwan. If Lai and the DPP emerge from November’s election in a position of strength, China will likely try to cow Taiwanese voters in the run-up to the 2028 vote, perhaps by operationalizing a soft blockade.

###### **Taiwan’s 2028 Matchup is Already Set**

Xi Jinping and KMT Chairwoman Cheng Li-wun, Beijing, April 10, 2026. _Credit: Spokesperson Mao Ning via [X](https://x.com/SpoxCHN\_MaoNing/status/2042557566820196766/photo/1)_

The KMT’s field of potential candidates for 2028 is shrinking fast. Controversial KMT chairwoman Cheng Li-wun, who has ambitions for the nomination, has become so toxic that the party’s candidates are outright avoiding her on the campaign trail for this November’s elections. Her lack of governing experience and pro-China stance — exhibited most clearly during her obsequious meeting with Xi Jinping in April — mean she has earned little [trust](https://www.setn.com/news/1864142) from Taiwan’s public.

A poor KMT showing in November would extinguish Cheng’s presidential ambitions and pressure her to resign as party chair. That would also leave Lu Shiow-yen as the strongest contender for the KMT’s 2028 nomination. Lu is term-limited for the upcoming elections and will thus have to leave her office as Taichung’s mayor after eight years, freeing her up for a presidential run.

Lu is a relative moderate who has advocated for higher military spending and [criticized](https://www.hakkatv.org.tw/news-detail/1668400819682072) her own party for aligning too closely with China. She has also cultivated a collaborative [relationship](https://www.cna.com.tw/news/aipl/202507270111.aspx) with Taiwan’s third-party, the Taiwan People’s Party (TPP), opening the door for an alliance in 2028 that would provide a stern test for Lai. (The KMT’s failure to work with the TPP the last time around cost it the 2024 presidential vote.)

The Western press has, though, largely overlooked Lai’s remarkable turnaround in fortunes. In July 2025, after a failed campaign to recall legislators and an aborted visit to the United States, Lai’s approval rating fell to just 31 percent. Today it’s at 51.4 percent, thanks in part to missteps by KMT chairwoman Cheng, and an economy surging on the back of the AI chips boom.

Taiwan’s GDP is now forecast to grow by 11 percent in 2026, a 39-year high. On August 17, Lai announced that the government would be handing out NT $10,000 (USD $313) to each citizen as a dividend from the AI boom, buying him and the DPP more love from voters.

Premier of Taiwan’s Executive Yuan, Cho Jung-tai (center), and officials announce the “AI Dividend, Shared by All” initiative, detailing plans for a universal NTD $10,000 cash distribution, August 20, 2026. _Credit: [Executive Yuan](https://www.ey.gov.tw/Page/9277F759E41CCD91/c9b62b00-c255-4c12-9eda-85409410beac)_

###### **Watch Taipei’s Local Elections**

The DPP is currently overperforming in two traditional KMT strongholds: Taipei City, and its surrounding municipality, New Taipei City. The last and only time the DPP won Taipei, Taiwan’s capital, was in 1994, and the last time it won New Taipei was in 2001. It could now win both in the same election, giving Lai’s re-election prospects a substantial boost. By contrast, it would be an unmitigated disaster for the KMT to lose one, let alone both races.

> A DPP breakthrough around the capital would give Lai momentum, all but finish Cheng Li-wun and clear Lu Shiow-yen’s path to the KMT nomination. It could also trigger Beijing to tighten the screws. Watch China’s coast guard as closely as Taiwan’s ballot box.

In Taipei City, the DPP is running Puma Shen Po-yang, a young, defense-minded legislator and founder of the civil defense group Kuma Academy. Shen is running an energetic and well-resourced campaign, swapping his proselytizing on national defense (which had made him one of Beijing’s least-favorite Taiwanese politicians) for an emphasis on quality of life and urban planning.

The DPP’s candidate for mayor of Taipei in the 2026 elections, Puma Shen. _Credit: [DPP](https://www.facebook.com/dpptw/posts/%EF%B8%8F%E5%8F%AA%E8%A6%81%E6%9C%89%E4%BA%BA%E9%96%8B%E5%A7%8B%E6%95%B4%E5%BA%A7%E5%9F%8E%E5%B8%82%E5%B0%B1%E8%83%BD%E4%B8%80%E8%B5%B7%E5%81%9A%E5%88%B0%E5%8F%B0%E5%8C%97%E5%B8%82%E9%95%B7%E5%80%99%E9%81%B8%E4%BA%BA-%E6%B2%88%E4%BC%AF%E6%B4%8B%E6%9C%80%E5%A5%BD%E7%9A%84%E5%9F%8E%E5%B8%82%E4%B8%8D%E8%A9%B2%E7%95%99%E4%B8%8D%E4%BD%8F%E4%BA%BA%E6%9C%80%E5%A4%9A%E7%9A%84%E9%A0%90%E7%AE%97%E4%B9%9F%E4%B8%8D%E8%A9%B2%E6%8F%9B%E4%B8%8D%E5%88%B0%E5%B8%82%E6%B0%91%E5%B0%8D%E6%9C%AA%E4%BE%86%E7%9A%84%E6%9C%9F%E5%BE%85-%E5%8F%B0%E5%8C%97-%E6%B2%88%E4%BC%AF%E6%B4%8B%E5%92%8C%E5%9C%98%E9%9A%8A%E6%95%B4%E7%90%86%E5%B8%82%E6%94%BF%E8%B3%87%E6%96%99%E7%A0%94%E7%A9%B6-199/1614841823338902/)_

The DPP has given Shen a successful makeover, swapping the scruffy hair and hoodies he donned as a legislator for a neater haircut, a suit and tie. In the streets of Taipei, images of Shen’s face outnumber those of his opponent, incumbent mayor Chiang Wan-an, ten to one. His team has given his campaign a clever, orange-coloured theme — providing a thematic distance from the green-themed DPP in the minds of KMT-leaning Taipei voters.

Despite earlier being projected to lose in a landslide, Shen has narrowed his deficit in the [polls](https://tw.news.yahoo.com/%E6%B4%8B%E6%B5%81-%E8%BF%BD%E5%88%B0%E5%8F%AA%E5%B7%AE1-2%E5%80%8B%E7%99%BE%E5%88%86%E9%BB%9E-%E6%9E%97%E4%BF%AE%E6%B0%91-%E6%B2%88%E4%BC%AF%E6%B4%8B%E6%95%A2%E8%AE%93%E6%B0%91%E7%9C%BE%E9%9A%A8%E6%A9%9F%E5%87%BA%E9%A1%8C-030900469.html) to just 1.2 percent behind Chiang as of September 22. And while Chiang may still win, Shen is establishing himself as a next-generation powerhouse for the DPP.

###### **Beijing’s Response**

China will almost certainly try to scare Taiwanese voters in the run-up to the 2028 elections. Beijing has already [branded](https://web.archive.org/web/20260922163359/https:/www.gwytb.gov.cn/xwdt/xwfb/wyly/202607/t20260722_12778251.htm) Lai Ching-te a “destroyer of peace” and [termed](https://web.archive.org/web/20260813090907/https:/www.gwytb.gov.cn/xwdt/xwfb/wyly/202410/t20241014_12656119.htm) Puma Shen a “diehard Taiwan independence separatist”, a label which can carry the death penalty in China.

[![Image 6](https://www.thewirechina.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/J-Michael-Cole-QA.png)](https://www.thewirechina.com/2026/01/18/j-michael-cole-on-the-best-and-worse-cases-for-taiwans-future/)

If the November elections strengthen Lai’s hand, expect PRC pressure to intensify through to 2028. Yet Beijing’s attempts to bend the outcome of the vote could backfire as they have in the past.

The China Coast Guard and the Maritime Safety Administration are already setting the groundwork for coercive moves. Since June, the Coast Guard has expanded “law enforcement patrols” to the waters off Taiwan’s east coast and has begun radioing foreign vessels bound for Taiwanese ports. These signal Beijing’s preparations for a potential economic blockade — one whose timeline could move up if Beijing’s preferred partners, the KMT, falters.

November’s vote will not pick Taiwan’s next president, but it will shape the race to do so. A DPP breakthrough around the capital would give Lai momentum, all but finish Cheng Li-wun and clear Lu Shiow-yen’s path to the KMT nomination. It could also trigger Beijing to tighten the screws. Watch China’s coast guard as closely as Taiwan’s ballot box.

* * *

John Pomfret was the _Washington Post_’s Beijing bureau chief from 1996 to 2003.

Seamus Boyle is a senior associate at Garnaut Global LLC, a global strategic consultancy.

title: Donate to SAVE US FROM THE MEGA EMBASSY! SUPPORT OUR LEGAL CHALLENGE, organized by Mark Nygate
summary: We are 100 families taking on the CCP - and we need your help. 我們是「皇家鑄幣廠居民協會」，由約一百戶職工家庭組成。我們懇請你伸出援手。 In 2018, our homes-key-worker flats in Tower Hamlets were sold in a secretive deal to the People's Republic of China. We had no say. No war
content:
We are 100 families taking on the CCP - and we need your help.

我們是「皇家鑄幣廠居民協會」，由約一百戶職工家庭組成。我們懇請你伸出援手。

In 2018, our homes-key-worker flats in Tower Hamlets were sold in a secretive deal to the People's Republic of China. We had no say. No warning. And now, we face living under the shadow of a hostile superpower.

2018年，我們居住的Tower Hamlets地段，在未經通知、無任何諮詢下，被秘密售予中國政府。我們無從置喙，如今更面對一個敵對政權的威脅。

The UK Government is expected to approve plans to build the largest embassy in Europe - right here, at Royal Mint Court, next to the Tower of London… and directly on top of our homes.

英國政府即將批准於倫敦塔旁的皇家鑄幣廠（Royal Mint Court）興建歐洲最大規模的中國大使館，預定地點正正位於我們所居之上。

This is not just a planning dispute.

我們擔憂的不僅是一項城市規劃決策，而是一場關乎國家安全、人身安全與基本權利的危機。

China has never shown any regard for our safety - and now the Government and the Metropolitan Police have abandoned us too.

自2018年起，中國政府從未就此提供明確回應，我們甚至不知道會否被驅逐、是否仍能繼續安居於此。而如今，政府與執法機關也對我們置之不理。

We are the Royal Mint Court Residents Association. People backed our previous Crowdfunder campaign that helped pay for a barrister to present our evidence including an independent security assessment showing the serious risks to us from a terror attack on the mega-embassy.

我們是「皇家鑄幣廠居民協會」。我們之前的眾籌活動獲得許多人的支持，資助我們聘請資深大律師提交證據，包括一份獨立的安全評估報告，指出超級大使館可能帶來的恐襲風險。

We are now launching an urgent legal challenge - a Judicial Review - to change the law and stop this injustice.

我們現在正展開一項緊急法律挑戰 — 即司法覆核 — 希望改變現行法律，阻止這場不公。

We need your help to protect our community from the mighty Chinese Communist Party.

我們需要你的幫助，去保護我們的社區，免受強大的中國共產黨威脅。

Whatever you can spare us, will help David stand-up to Goliath.

無論你能捐出多少，都能幫助大衛對抗歌利亞。

We are seeking to pursue a Judicial Review because we have believed all along that the planning process has been flawed. Here are some of the reasons we think are likely to be relevant:

我們決定提起司法覆核，是因為我們始終認為整個規劃程序存在問題。以下是我們認為可能相關的一些原因：

“Closed mind”: Ministers may have signalled early approval to China, before formal procedures were followed, breaking the law and abusing planning powers. In a similar vein, objections disappeared after UK ministers returned from Beijing. Residents have felt like pawns in a geopolitical game since the start.

預設立場：部長們可能在正式程序開始前就向中方表示支持，違反法律並濫用規劃權力。在部長們從北京回來之後，原有的反對聲音突然消失。居民們從一開始就覺得自己成了地緣政治博弈中的棋子。

Security concerns: Building a fortified embassy with homes on site and critical infrastructure nearby, ignoring espionage concerns and the real human risk to dissidents, is indefensible.

安全隱患：在住宅區內及重要基礎設施附近建設高度防禦的大使館，無視間諜活動與對異見人士的人身威脅，完全不能接受。

Procedural unfairness: We were shut out of the process. No consultation. No transparency. No respect for the people who live here.

程序不公：我們被完全排除在決策過程之外。無諮詢、無透明、無對居民的尊重。

Legitimate expectation: We were promised due process and protection. We got silence.

合理期望落空：我們被承諾將獲程序保障與保護，實際卻是得不到任何保障。

What’s wrong with the embassy plan?

We still live here. 100 families. Nurses, teachers, pensioners. Our 100 homes are on land now owned by the Chinese government. That means the Chinese ambassador is our landlord - with rights to enter our homes.

我們仍然住在這裡 ，足足一百戶家庭，包括護士、教師、退休人士。我們的一百個住所現已位於中國政府擁有的土地上。這代表中國大使成為我們的業主，有權進入我們的住所。

China refuses to answer us. Since 2018, we’ve begged for assurances: will we be evicted? Will we be safe? Can we stay? Beijing’s answer: not until we get planning permission. This refusal, and the proposal to install a temporary style wooden boundary fence as a dividing line, raises fears that the Chinese Government intends to take back the entire 100 apartments at St Mary Graces Court once they secure diplomatic status for the site, leaving us homeless.

中國拒絕回應我們的訴求。自2018年起，我們不斷尋求保證：我們會被驅逐嗎？我們是否安全？我們能否繼續居住？北京的答覆是：等規劃許可下來再說。這種拒絕，以及擬議中以臨時木欄分隔的做法，讓我們擔心中國政府一旦取得外交地位，將會收回整個St Mary Graces Court的100個單位，使我們流離失所。

This embassy is a fortress. It’s not a normal diplomatic building. It will have secret communications centres, fortified walls, and surveillance technology that can monitor our entire estate, even our bedrooms. It will also stand on top of critical UK cables that MI5 warn are a security risk to the UK.

這座大使館是一個堡壘，並非普通的外交建築。它將設有秘密通訊設施、加固圍牆、監控技術，可監視整個屋苑，甚至包括我們的睡房。而它的地基下方，更有英國重要電纜 ，MI5曾警告這是對國家安全的威脅。

The UK Government knows the risk - and ignored it. Our independent security report warns that this site puts families and national security at risk. Even the UK’s Head of Counter-Terrorism originally objected - citing threats to residents and dissidents. But since ministers returned from Beijing, objections have mysteriously vanished.

英國政府明知有風險，卻選擇無視。我們的獨立安全報告指出，該地點將危害居民與國家安全。甚至連英國反恐部門首長最初也曾反對 ， 指出對居民與異見人士的威脅。但自從部長從北京回來後，這些反對聲音神秘地消失。

Ministers made no mention of the 100 families living here. We are alarmed that the letters from Home Secretary Yvette Cooper and Foreign Secretary David Lammy have ignored the fact that UK families live in 100 apartments on the land that is actually part of Royal Mint court - and is owned by the Chinese government. Our Resident’s Chairman has personally appealed to ministers, submitted the full Crilly Consultants security report, and our plight has appeared in The Times, FT, BBC, CNN, and more. What is happening to democratic accountability in this country?

部長們從未提及這裡有一百戶居民。我們對內政大臣Yvette Cooper及外交大臣David Lammy的信件感到震驚，因為他們完全忽略了皇家鑄幣廠的土地上住有英國公民、100個家庭。我們的居民協會主席曾親自致函部長、提交完整的Crilly安全報告，而我們的處境亦已被《泰晤士報》、《金融時報》、BBC、CNN等多間媒體報導。英國民主問責制度何在？

The first duty of the UK government is to protect its citizens. We understand the UK’s diplomatic obligations - but not at the expense of its own people. The refusal to acknowledge the basic risks of housing a high-security foreign embassy on top of a residential block is deeply troubling. It appears the government is prioritising relations with Beijing over the safety of its own citizens.

英國政府的首要職責是保護其國民。我們明白外交義務，但不能以犧牲本國人民為代價。將一個高安全級別的外國大使館設於住宅區上方，而拒絕承認基本風險，是極度令人不安的。

It’s not just about us. Dissidents, including Hong Kongers, Uyghurs, Tibetans, Taiwanese and Chinese exile communities are terrified. They’ve told us they no longer feel safe protesting outside the site, and on British soil. Their presence, and ours, will be met with constant surveillance and intimidation by a regime known to harass and threaten activists - even abroad.

這件事不僅關係到我們。流亡港人、維吾爾人、西藏人、台灣人及中國異見社群皆感到恐懼。他們表示不再敢在該地點或英國土地上公開抗議。他們與我們一樣，將面對來自這個以恐嚇異見者聞名的政權的持續監控與威嚇。

The people have spoken, and they support us.

人民已經發聲，並支持我們。

On 8 February 2025, thousands of British citizens - including Hong Kongers, Uyghurs, Tibetans, Taiwanese and Chinese pro-democracy activists, and human rights campaigners - gathered outside Royal Mint Court in protest against this embassy.

2025年2月8日，數以千計的英國公民 ，包括港人、維吾爾人、西藏人、台灣人、中國民主人士與人權倡議者， 齊集皇家鑄幣廠，抗議中國大使館計劃。

They were joined by cross-party MPs, journalists, and allies. Together, they said NO to the Chinese embassy, and YES to democratic values, safety, and justice.

他們與跨黨派議員、記者及盟友並肩站立，一同說出明確立場：反對中國大使館，支持民主、安全與公義。

Further mass protests followed on 15 March, 3 May, and 14 June - showing growing national resistance to the plan.

3月15日、5月3日及6月14日亦舉行後續大型集會，反對聲浪日益壯大。

They continue to protest, and have made it clear: they won’t stop until this mega-embassy deal is over.

抗議仍在持續，並清楚表示：他們不會停止，直至該項目取消為止。

But the Government is not listening.

但政府並未聆聽我們的訴求。

So now, we go to court.

所以現在，我們只有訴諸法庭。

But we need your help - fast.

但我們需要您的協助 - 迅速的協助。

The legal fees for a Judicial Review are beyond the reach of ordinary families. But with your help, we can stand up to both Beijing and Whitehall.

司法覆核的法律費用遠超普通家庭的負擔。但在您的幫助下，我們能夠與北京和英國政府對抗。

This case is about more than one building. It’s about:

這宗案件關乎的遠不止一座建築。它關乎：

Protecting British citizens from state overreach

保護英國公民免受國家權力的侵害

Defending UK democracy from foreign influence

捍衛英國的民主，抵抗外國影響

Challenging backroom deals that put power over people

挑戰那些將權力凌駕於人民之上的秘密交易

If we succeed, we won’t just protect our homes. We’ll set a precedent that no foreign government can build on British soil without respecting British citizens and British values.

如若成功，我們不僅能保護我們的家園，我們更是創下先例：任何外國政府不得在罔顧英國公民和英國價值的前提下在英國土地上建造任何建築。

Will you stand with us?

您願意與我們並肩作戰嗎？

Please chip in whatever you can. £10. £100. £1,000. Every penny goes to legal costs to take this to court. We are a group of teachers, nurses, shop workers and pensioners. We don’t have the Chinese Communist Party’s millions - but with your help, we do have people power.

請您捐出任何您能負擔的金額 — 不論是 £10，£100 還是 £1,000。每一分錢都將用於支付法律費用，讓我們將此案帶上法庭。我們只是一群教師、護士、店員和退休人士。雖然我們沒有中國共產黨的龐大資金 — 但在您的幫助下，我們擁有的是人民的力量。

Share this far and wide.

請廣傳此訊息。

Donate if you can.

如有行力，請捐款。

Stand up for democracy.

為民主發聲。

Because if they can do this to us, they can do it to anyone.

唇亡齒寒。

PLEASE NOTE

請注意：

This is a secure UK-based platform, fully registered and subject to UK law.

這是一個安全的英國平台，註冊並受英國法律管轄。

It is widely used to support political and legal campaigns, including by MPs, NGOs, and grassroots movements - some of which are openly critical of the Chinese government.

該平台廣泛用於支持政治和法律活動，包括國會議員、非政府組織和基層運動 — 包括曾公開批評中國政府的政治活動。

The platform offers full transparency, with public donation records and payment processing via Stripe or PayPal.

該平台提供完全透明的捐款記錄，並通過 Stripe 或 PayPal 處理支付。

There is no history of censorship or compliance with pressure from the Chinese state.

台以往並無自我審查紀錄，也未曾屈從於中國的壓力。

It adheres strictly to GDPR regulations, ensuring donor and campaigner data is protected.

平台嚴格遵守 GDPR 規範，確保捐款者和活動者的數據安全。

About your donations

關於您的捐款

2.95% + 0.25 of each donation goes to the platform; 100% of the remaining funds will be used to cover legal costs.

每筆捐款將扣除 2.95% 加 £0.25 之平台手續費，其餘款項將全數用以支付法律相關費用。

If the legal case is dismissed, your donation will be directed to charity unless you request a refund. If you would like your donation returned, please email us. We will calculate and refund your contribution (with platform fee deducted).

如法律訴訟最終被駁回，捐款將撥捐予慈善機構，除非閣下主動申請退款。如欲索回捐款，請電郵至，我們將在扣除平台手續費後，計算並退還閣下之捐款。

About campaign updates

關於活動更新

We will post updates every two weeks, which you can follow directly on this page.

我們每兩週更新一次進展，您可以直接於此頁面查看。

法国/社会冲突

据法国内政部周日发布的全国初步统计，周六在法国爆发的抗议活动导致1314人被拘留，消防部门出动75次扑救火灾；此外，53名执法人员受伤，24家商铺遭抢劫。

 作者：

古莉

法国内政部在声明中指出，周六共“统计到289起公共道路活动”，包括示威和集会，参与者达41万；而10月17日则发生了441起活动，示威者人数达55万人。

该声明继续写道：“游行队伍按照事先规划并经与地方当局协商确定的路线在公共道路上游行，并在国内安全部队的监管下顺利进行”。

**极左翼风险群体**

然而，在多个城市，“由激进左翼和极左翼活动分子等组成的风险群体，在大部分游行队伍的前方、内部或边缘聚集”，从而引发了冲突。

在包括巴黎、马赛、波尔多、图卢兹和图尔在内的多个城市，游行尾声时爆发了示威者与治安部队的冲突，后者使用催泪瓦斯进行反击。

#香港首届济公轿赛复兴驱瘟传统
周日，香港在维多利亚公园举办了首届受民间神济公启发的轿子竞赛，复兴了 19 世纪的驱瘟仪式。该活动由东正园佛教总会主办，以障碍挑战和文化活动为特色，是为期三天的国际佛教文化交流活动的一部分。

# Hong Kong stages first Ji Gong palanquin race to revive plague-banishing tradition

Hong Kong hosted its first-ever palanquin race inspired by the legendary folk deity Ji Gong at Victoria Park on Sunday, drawing crowds eager to witness a revival of a storied plague-banishing ritual from the 19th century.

The tradition is rooted in the long-held Chinese folk belief that parading deities in palanquins can dispel evil and purify the community.

The event, organised by the Tung Cheng Yuen Buddhist Association and supported by the Chinese Temples Committee along with over 20 cultural and educational organisations, formed the centrepiece of the three-day 2026 International Ji Gong Cultural Festival.

The competing teams carried palanquins from Tik Lung Lane to Wan Chai Pier, then crossed the harbour by boat to Hung Hom, in a nod to Ji Gong’s epidemic-dispelling journey. Along the route, participants tackled various obstacle challenges that tested their teamwork, patience, and problem-solving skills.

Beyond the race, the festival featured Cantonese opera performances for seniors, blessing ceremonies, interactive booth games, and a Ji Gong plague-expelling ritual procession. Attendees also enjoyed hands-on activities such as fan-shaped soap workshops, compression art sessions, and lacquer fan crafts to immerse themselves in Chinese cultural practices.

Organisers noted that the event serves as a reminder for the public to remain vigilant against epidemics and to safeguard traditional religious rituals.

The Center for Strategic and International Studies conducted an extraordinary survey of 64 leading experts on China, Taiwan, and cross-Strait relations, including 28 former senior U.S. government officials, 23 former government policy and intelligence analysts, and 13 academics and think-tank experts. What their answers reveal is not that China is preparing to invade Taiwan tomorrow, as the neocons would like everyone to believe, but that Beijing remains willing to wait so long as nobody crosses the line of formal Taiwanese independence. Some [**84% said Beijing is willing to wait for unification**](https://chinapower.csis.org/survey-experts-china-approach-to-taiwan/ "84% said Beijing is willing to wait for unification") but will not accept the status quo permanently, while only 10% believed China seeks unification at the earliest opportunity. Not one of the 64 experts believed Beijing would ever accept an independent Taiwan.

This is precisely why Taiwan has become so dangerous. The West keeps portraying the conflict as if Xi Jinping wakes up every morning staring at a calendar trying to decide when to launch an amphibious invasion. Yet 83% of these experts said China did not plan to use significant kinetic force against Taiwan by 2027, and 80% said China’s enormous 2022 military exercises did not indicate Beijing had accelerated its timetable. Only 6% of respondents outside the former senior government group saw 2027 as a hard deadline, while not one former senior U.S. official did. The obsession with 2027 has nevertheless become extremely useful for the military establishment because every supposed deadline becomes another justification for weapons, deployments, bases, and spending.

The survey found that 44% believed Beijing has a hard deadline of 2049, the centennial of the People’s Republic, while 42% believed China could wait indefinitely provided unification remains possible. This is an important distinction because China thinks in terms of generations while Western politicians think in terms of the next election. Beijing does not need to invade Taiwan if economic, political, and military pressure can gradually change the situation in its favor. Only 20% of those surveyed believed China even possessed a coherent roadmap for peaceful unification, which tells us this is not some perfectly scripted invasion plan sitting in Xi’s desk drawer.

[![Image 2: TaiwanMagnified](https://www.armstrongeconomics.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/TaiwanMagnified.jpg?w=300)](https://www.armstrongeconomics.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/TaiwanMagnified.jpg)

Where the numbers become alarming is not an unprovoked invasion but what happens when politicians begin crossing China’s red lines. More than three-quarters of the experts, 77%, believed China would invade within six months if Taiwan formally declared independence. Among former senior U.S. officials, that number was 79%. Even some of those who did not expect an immediate invasion believed Beijing would respond with a blockade or enormous military exercises. This is why politicians encouraging Taiwan toward formal independence are playing with the lives of 23 million people. They can deliver all the speeches they want about democracy from Washington, London, or Brussels, but they will not be the civilians sitting underneath the missiles if their political experiment goes wrong.

Not one expert believed an explicit American commitment to defend Taiwan would cause China to invade immediately, but 64% believed Beijing would respond strongly enough to provoke a U.S.-China or China-Taiwan crisis, while another 31% expected a more limited negative response. Only two of the 64 experts believed formally committing America to Taiwan’s defense would actually deter China from using force because Beijing already assumes that the United States will intervene anyway.

A direct invasion is not even the most likely path toward conflict. Only 8% of the experts described an amphibious invasion within ten years as likely, while 63% called it possible and 27% unlikely. Force short of invasion received much higher probabilities, with 52% saying deliberate escalation such as a blockade was likely or very likely. An accidental military incident was considered even more dangerous, with 34% saying a collision or accident around the Taiwan Strait was likely and another 22% calling it very likely. When warships and aircraft from opposing nuclear powers continually operate around the same small body of water, war does not require some grand master plan. It requires one mistake followed by politicians who refuse to back down.

A later CSIS survey of American and Taiwanese experts reinforces that point. Roughly 90% of U.S. experts and 62% of Taiwanese experts believed China already possessed the capability to impose a law-enforcement-led quarantine that substantially reduces trade into Taiwan. Around 80% of American experts and 60% of Taiwanese experts believed Beijing could execute a PLA [**blockade**](https://chinapower.csis.org/data/survey-results-chinas-approach-to-taiwan/ "blockade"), while Taiwanese experts were considerably more skeptical that China could successfully carry out an invasion. If Beijing wanted to coerce Taiwan during the following five years, experts considered a quarantine the most likely option. If China decided it wanted immediate unification, however, approximately 80% regarded a highly kinetic joint blockade as likely or very likely.

[![Image 3: Taiwan ECM 2](https://www.armstrongeconomics.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/05/Taiwan-ECM-2.jpg?w=300)](https://www.armstrongeconomics.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/05/Taiwan-ECM-2.jpg)

This is where the economic consequences become enormous because Taiwan does not need to be invaded for the world economy to be thrown into chaos. A quarantine or blockade would immediately threaten shipping, insurance, semiconductor supply chains, electronics, automobiles, communications equipment, and virtually every modern industry dependent upon advanced chips. The later CSIS survey found most American and Taiwanese experts did not believe Taiwan could withstand a Chinese blockade for longer than three months without substantial U.S. intervention. Washington would then face the decision nobody wants to discuss honestly: accept China’s blockade or attempt to break it militarily and risk direct war between two nuclear powers.

Taiwan is also the world’s semiconductor pressure point. The island’s importance to advanced chip manufacturing means a serious blockade would not remain a regional event. Factories thousands of miles away could discover that a conflict they thought had nothing to do with them suddenly prevents them from obtaining critical components. Markets would begin repricing the risk immediately, shipping premiums would explode, companies would scramble for inventory, and governments would discover once again how fragile global supply chains have become. This is why capital will react long before politicians formally declare that a war has begun.

What I find particularly revealing in the later CSIS survey is the difference between American confidence and Taiwanese confidence in Washington. An astonishing 96% of American experts were completely or moderately confident that the United States would intervene militarily if China invaded Taiwan during the following five years. Taiwanese experts were less confident in American intervention and considerably less confident that U.S. allies would join the fight. It is always easier for people thousands of miles away to be certain about somebody else’s war.

This is precisely why Taiwan remains one of the critical geopolitical pressure points as we move toward 2029. The danger is not simply that China arbitrarily decides to invade. The greater danger is escalation, miscalculation, political promises that cannot be withdrawn, and Western policymakers convincing themselves that every additional provocation somehow produces deterrence. China has made its position on formal independence perfectly clear, and even the experts inside the Western foreign-policy establishment overwhelmingly acknowledge that Beijing would react with force if that line were crossed.

If Taiwan declares formal independence, 77% of the experts surveyed believed China would invade within six months. That is not a statistic policymakers should treat as another war-game scenario. It is a warning about what happens when politicians deliberately remove the ambiguity that has helped keep the peace.

# 台湾光复81周年 央视发布卫星俯瞰台湾影片 解放军报要求“随时准备打仗”

茉莉花综合报道 2026年10月25日 12:09

10月25日是台湾光复81周年，也是中国大陆设立“台湾光复纪念日”一周年。央视新闻当天发布一段42秒的影片，用“吉林一号”卫星从太空俯瞰台湾，把台湾标为中国的一个省，并称从太空连台湾的每条街道都看得清楚。

影片拍到台北的中正纪念堂、故宫博物院、台北大巨蛋、国父纪念馆和台北港，以及玉山山脉、日月潭、花莲清水断崖等地。影片把国父纪念馆标作孙中山纪念馆，配乐是歌曲《故乡的云》，歌词反复呼唤归来，结尾的文字是“歸心不變，團圓有時”。同一天，解放军报的文章说：“对于冥顽不化的“台独”分子和别有用心的外部干涉势力，就要用他们看得懂、感到怕的方式予以警醒和惩戒”；文章还点名批评赖清德今年5月搭乘斯威士兰国王的私人飞机出访。

卫星影片中的台北故宫博物院俯视画面。

解放军东部战区同一天发布海报，用历史照片填满台湾岛的轮廓，下方配上军舰、战机和持枪军人的剪影，写着“銘記光復歷史，捍衛山河一統”。解放军报25日发表文章说，台湾问题是中国核心利益中的核心，军队必须充分做好应对各种复杂情况的准备，一旦有事能够快速有效处置。文章要求提高“以武促统”的战略能力，做到随时准备打仗、随时能打胜仗，并说“没有战的能力，就难有祖国统一”。文章还提到，解放军近年多次在台湾周边海空域组织演习演训，“全向围岛进逼之势勒得越来越紧”。

新华社当天转述习近平的论述说，台湾是中国一部分，两岸统一的历史大势无法阻挡，文章以“祖國必須統一，也必然統一”作结。人民日报在微博上呼吁民众坚定对中华民族、中华文化和祖国的认同。国台办发言人张晗21日说，纪念活动是要回顾抗战胜利和台湾光复的历史，凝聚推进完全统一的力量。中国全国人大常委会2025年作出决定，把10月25日设为台湾光复纪念日，纪念1945年10月25日台湾光复。

台湾光复纪念日前后的时间线

1.   1945年10月25日 台湾光复
2.   2025年 中国全国人大常委会决定把10月25日设为台湾光复纪念日
3.   2026年10月21日 国台办发言人张晗说将举办纪念活动
4.   2026年10月25日 央视发布卫星俯瞰台湾影片；东部战区发布海报；解放军报发表文章

香港民众安全服务队于 2026 年 10 月 25 日举行一年一度的山地安全推广日，并设有新的青少年区，并设有八个纪律部队。官员们强调了在低空经济沙箱计划下使用无人机进行搜救行动，并向

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

2026 年 10 月 25 日 16:53 香港时间 · 更新于 10 月 25 日 17:59 · 阅读时间 2 分钟

 图片：[香港特区政府新闻公报](https://www.info.gov.hk/gia/general/202610/25/P2026102300501.htm)

香港民众安全服务队于10月25日举办「山地安全推广日2026暨社区紧急事故体验日」，吸引八支纪律部队及其青少年制服队参加。特派员庞英荪表示，活动在保安局协调下增设“纪律辅助人员青少年专区”，设有互动游戏摊位，介绍本市的应急体系及各部门的工作。
彭表示，是次活动配合《香港特别行政区经济和社会发展第一个五年规划（2026-2030年）》，鼓励年轻人通过科技和创新思维参与，提高山地安全和社区应急意识。他还为“山地伤亡处理课程”和“登山安全与山地救援课程”的毕业生颁发了证书。

CAS 参谋长梁冠康表示，CAS 一直与其他政府部门合作开展山区搜救行动。他举例说，2026年8月，香港警方、消防处和政府飞行服务队联合采取行动，成功找到了一名在鲤鱼门失踪超过一周的女子，并将她送往医院。他说，此次行动展现了各部门的专业精神。

梁说，CAS在日常行动和搜索中积极部署无人机，以提高效率并简化程序。在低空经济监管沙盒计划下，CAS将试点无人机巡逻、山火探测以及自动体外除颤器等山地设备或急救物资的运送，这可以帮助救援人员更好地利用救援黄金时间。
其他嘉宾包括警务处处长谢孟华、保安局副秘书长甄祥华、政府飞行服务队总监廖家俊、消防处新界南分区指挥官何俊邦，以及渔农自然护理署、通讯事务管理局办公室、天文台、康乐及文化事务署、医疗辅助队、地政总署和多个登山团体的代表。活动设有游戏摊位、山地活动装备展示，以及八个由青少年团队经营的摊位，以提高山地安全和应急意识。

Hong Kong
Hong Kong's Civil Aid Service held its annual Mountain Safety Promotion Day on 25 October 2026, featuring a new youth zone with eight disciplined services. Officials highlighted the use of drones in search-and-rescue operations under a low-altitude economy sandbox scheme, and awarded certificates to

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

25 Oct 2026 at 16:53 HKT · updated 25 Oct, 17:59 · 2 min read

 Image: [香港特區政府新聞公報](https://www.info.gov.hk/gia/general/202610/25/P2026102300501.htm)

Hong Kong's Civil Aid Service (CAS) held the "Mountain Safety Promotion Day 2026 and Community Emergency Experience Day" on 25 October, drawing participation from eight disciplined services and their youth uniformed teams. CAS Commissioner Pang Ying-sun said the event added a new "Disciplined and Auxiliary Services Youth Zone" under the coordination of the Security Bureau, featuring interactive game booths to introduce the city's emergency response system and the work of each service.

Pang said the event aligned with the "First Five-Year Plan for Economic and Social Development of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (2026-2030)", encouraging young people to engage through technology and innovative thinking to improve mountain safety and community emergency awareness. He also presented certificates to graduates of the "Mountain Casualty Handling Course" and the "Climbing Safety and Mountain Rescue Course".

CAS Chief of Staff Leung Kwun-hong said the CAS has worked alongside other government departments in mountain search-and-rescue operations. He cited a joint operation in August 2026 with the Hong Kong Police, Fire Services Department and Government Flying Service that successfully located a woman who had been missing for over a week at Lei Yue Mun and sent her to hospital. The operation demonstrated the professional spirit of all departments, he said.

Leung said the CAS has actively deployed drones in daily operations and searches to improve efficiency and streamline procedures. Under the low-altitude economy regulatory sandbox scheme, the CAS will trial drone patrols, wildfire detection, and the delivery of mountain equipment or first-aid supplies such as automated external defibrillators, which could help rescue personnel make better use of the golden hour of rescue.

Other guests included Police Commissioner Monday Tse, Security Bureau Deputy Secretary Yan Cheung-wah, Government Flying Service Controller Liu Ka-chun, Fire Services Department New Territories South Divisional Commander Ho Chun-pong, and representatives from the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department, the Office of the Communications Authority, the Hong Kong Observatory, the Leisure and Cultural Services Department, the Auxiliary Medical Services, the Lands Department and multiple mountaineering groups. The event featured game booths, displays of mountain activity equipment, and eight booths run by youth teams to promote mountain safety and emergency response awareness.
