content:
距离九合一选举剩下约6个星期，各区选战都已进入白热化的「选战模式」。受到台北市「洋流崛起」影响选情，过往让蓝营引以为豪的双北票仓，都传出失守危机。而新北市因身为全台最大票仓，被国民党视为「绝对不能输的重中之重」与2028年总统大选重返执政的关键基地。

距离九合一选举剩下约6个星期，各区选战都已进入白热化的「选战模式」。关键选区包括新北市、台北市、新竹县、彰化县及基隆市，其中又以「新北市为最关键一战」。美国史丹佛大学胡佛研究所政治学者祁凯立（Kharis Templeman）曾表示，新北市是观察台湾政治走向最重要的风向指标。

祁凯立分析，新北市人口超过400万，是台湾人口最多的直辖市，蓝绿实力相近，可视为双方实力正面对决，且全国性因素预料将在新北市选举结果中扮演重要角色。某种程度来说，无论谁拿下新北，都有理由称自己表现超出预期，将这次选举视为胜利。

**新北国民党21年执政遭挑战？**

从台北县到新北市，国民党已连续执政21年。自2005年周锡伟担任台北县长到2010年朱立伦选上新北市长。如今新北市长侯友宜两任任期届满，国民党由李四川接棒参选，民进党则由苏巧慧出马挑战，双方目前战况陷入胶着状态。

以《巨闻天下》民调结果来看，李四川从7月的50.85%，一路滑落到现在的45.74%，下滑了5.11个百分点。反观，苏巧慧则稳步爬升到45.18%，双方差距只剩0.56个百分点，进入肉搏拉锯战。以此走势来看，李四川一路从稳赢到跌破防线，被解读为是对国民党选情上一大警讯。

若以台北市信民两岸研究协会在13日公布最新的新北市长选情民调，苏巧慧获得43.1%支持度、李四川则获得30.0%，差距直接拉到13.1个百分点。民调专家戴立安以此民调数据分析，这是因为台北市民进党参选人沈伯洋的「洋流」外溢，直接拉抬了新北市长选情，洋流现在已经变成海啸。但也有专家表示，虽然民调受洋流效应影响产生震荡，但双方在得票率推估上仍可能在误差范围内，即所谓「沉默的蓝营选民」尚未表态。

**新北市长候选人苏巧慧与李四川**

民进党候选人苏巧慧自2016年起当选连任第9、10、11届新北市第五选举区立委，也是现任民进党立法院党团副干事长。国民党主席郑丽文曾以「出身民进党最大、最有力家族的公主」形容苏巧慧，因为她的爸爸正是前行政院长苏贞昌，所以自5岁起她就有跟着父亲上街拜票的经验。

副总统萧美琴曾表示，苏巧慧不仅在教育、社福、环卫及经济等领域做足了准备，更是大家心中温暖的「水獭妈妈」，集结了狗派跟猫派的温暖热情，与强大的创新行动力。

苏巧慧在早早确定目标后，就开始地方拜票、扫街、扫市场，并让她的民调得以快速跟上其竞选节奏。她将竞选主轴聚焦在年轻族群、地方创生、文化、AI等建设，以此力拼翻转新北市。但另一方面，来自父亲苏贞昌的政治包袱，可能让不喜欢苏贞昌的选民因此选择将票投给对手。

另一方面，国民党候选人李四川现年68岁，自2010年起担任过新北市副市长、台北市副市长、高雄市副市长、行政院秘书长、国民党秘书长等要职。 2022年，受台北市长蒋万安邀请出任台北市副市长。并在2026年2月，代表台北市政府与辉达正式签约后不久即卸任，投入新北市长选举。

李四川向来的强势区域为新北的瑞芳 、贡寮等海岸线行政区，以及人口稠密的新店、中永和等区。但部分评论表示，李四川的形象太老，难以吸引年轻人。且李四川越上新闻节目，整体就越失分。竞选节奏落后与年老形象成为他最主要的劣势。

两位候选人相较之下，李四川长期主打能做事的工程师、技术官僚形象，但在没有新政见牛肉与愿景支撑下，开始让年轻中产家庭、女性选民感到枯燥无味。相反地，苏巧慧主打实质育儿、教育与生活感牛肉，成功精准吸纳了浮动的票源。这可能是造成双方支持度逐渐拉平的原因之一。

**守住新北市对蓝营的意义**

国民党在这次九合一县市长选举中面临保住既有执政版图的压力，难度比表面上看起来更高，民进党则可能席次反而增加。这与国民党许多现任县市长因任期限制必须卸任、失去现任优势，赖清德总统施政满意度提升，以及经济蓬勃发展有利执政党等因素有关。

在这场难打得选战中，受到台北市「洋流崛起」影响选情，过往让蓝营引以为豪的双北票仓，都传出失守危机。而新北市因身为全台最大票仓，被国民党视为「绝对不能输的重中之重」与2028年总统大选重返执政的关键基地。

有台湾学者表示，新北市对国民党而言，有不能输的压力，若能稳住新北，不仅能为蓝营2028重返执政保留关键量能，也能验证台北市长蒋万安「万安旋风」的外溢效应。

《经济日报》报导，美国学者祁凯立对此分析，如果国民党在这次选举结果不如预期，可能会促成党内权力调整，反而可能为2028总统大选创造更有利位置。因此九合一选举结果未必能代表2028总统大选胜负。

# Taiwan a 'faithful partner': St. Vincent envoy at Independence Day fete

10/21/2026 08:50 PM

[](jsvscript:)[](jsvscript:)[](javascript:void(0))[Listen](javascript:)

Deputy Foreign Minister Chen Ming-chi (陳明祺), left, and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines' ambassador to Taiwan Kenton Chance.CNA photo Oct. 21, 2026

Taipei, Oct. 21 (CNA) The ambassador of St. Vincent and the Grenadines (SVG) to Taiwan on Wednesday called Taiwan a "faithful partner" that has helped his country develop and prosper, as the Caribbean nation marked the 47th anniversary of its independence at a reception in Taipei.

"Today, we pay tribute to our developmental partners, the countries, international agencies and organizations that have contributed and continue to contribute to our development over the last 47 years," Ambassador Kenton Chance said in his address.

"In this regard, I express particular gratitude to the Republic of China (Taiwan), which has been a faithful partner over the last 45 years," he said.

Chance also urged his compatriots to learn from Taiwan's success.

"My fellow Vincentians, Taiwanese today enjoy the fruits of the hard work of their forebears while building an even more resilient and prosperous country for the next generation," he said.

"I urge every Vincentian in Taiwan to take inspiration from our host and build sacrificially so the next generation can experience in St. Vincent and the Grenadines a level of development similar to what we enjoy now in Taiwan," he added.

Representing the Taiwanese government at the reception, Deputy Foreign Minister Chen Ming-chi (陳明祺) wished the Caribbean ally a happy Independence Day.

Chen said 2026 also marks the 45th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries.

"Throughout these years, our two nations have developed a close friendship built on mutual trust, shared values, and meaningful cooperation," he said.

Looking ahead, Chen said Taiwan was committed to deepening its partnership with SVG, particularly in economic cooperation, tourism and agriculture.

"By working together in these areas, we hope to create new opportunities for our local businesses, support economic growth, and bring lasting benefits to both our peoples," Chen added.

SVG is one of 12 countries that maintain diplomatic relations with the Republic of China, Taiwan's official name. The two countries established diplomatic ties on Aug. 15, 1981.

(By Joseph Yeh)

title: Takaichi’s history remarks aim to smooth the path to a meeting with Xi, Taiwanese expert says
summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said before the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit that her Cabinet would uphold the position expressed in the Murayama Statement. A Taiwanese expert said the remark was a conciliatory sig
content:
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said before the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit that her Cabinet would uphold the position expressed in the Murayama Statement. A Taiwanese expert said the remark was a conciliatory signal to Beijing as Tokyo seeks a meeting between Takaichi and Chinese President Xi Jinping (習近平) in November.
**Murayama Statement**

Asked about her views on history at a House of Councillors Budget Committee meeting on Oct. 16, Takaichi [said](https://tchina.kyodonews.net/articles/-/14976?words=%E6%9D%91%E5%B1%B1%E8%AB%87%E8%A9%B1) that, as stated in the 70th-anniversary statement marking the end of World War II, the positions of successive Japanese Cabinets would remain unchanged under her administration.

She said this included the 1995 Murayama Statement, issued on Aug. 15 that year by then Prime Minister Tomiichi Murayama.

The statement was the first in which the Japanese government officially acknowledged that Japan’s wartime aggression and colonial rule caused great damage and suffering in Asian countries, and expressed deep remorse and heartfelt apology.

 Chinese President Xi Jinping meets Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi on the sidelines of the APEC meeting in Gyeongju, South Korea, on the afternoon of Oct. 31, 2025. (Ministry of Foreign Affairs PRC)

**A conciliatory signal?**
This year’s APEC summit will be held in Shenzhen, China, on Nov. 18–19. Whether Xi and Takaichi will meet during the summit has drawn attention.

Takaichi [confirmed](https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/10/18/japan/politics/takaichi-china-apec-parliament/) plans to attend the China-hosted APEC leaders' summit pending Diet clearance, signaling a readiness to engage Beijing in person despite deeply strained bilateral ties.

Kuo

Yu~~-~~jen (郭育仁), director of the Institute of China and Asia-Pacific Studies at National Sun Yat-sen University, told TCN that Japan was working to arrange a meeting between the two leaders. Takaichi’s pledge to uphold the Murayama Statement ahead of APEC, he said, was a gesture of goodwill toward Beijing.
Given Beijing’s recent posture, a formal bilateral meeting remains improbable, Kuo said, suggesting that any encounter would likely be choreographed as a "chance meeting" in the corridors.

Should no interaction take place at all, he said, it would signal that already strained Tokyo-Beijing relations are continuing to deteriorate.

**A Taiwan contingency is a Japan contingency**

In November 2025, Takaichi told Japan’s House of Representatives that a Chinese armed assault on Taiwan—such as a naval blockade enforced with military force—could be deemed a "survival-threatening situation" under Japanese security laws. Such a determination, she noted, could legally permit the Self-Defense Forces to exercise limited collective self-defense, provided other legal requirements were met.

Beijing responded with retaliatory measures, cooling cultural exchanges, dampening outbound tourism to Japan, re-imposing a ban on Japanese seafood, and restricting exports of dual-use goods to Japanese military users and for military uses, including uses that contribute to Japan’s military capabilities. China’s dual-use control list covers roughly 1,100 items, including critical minerals such as rare earths, gallium, and germanium.

Kuo said Takaichi’s commitment to the Murayama Statement did not mean she was retracting her “Taiwan contingency, Japan contingency” remarks, adding that the two issues were unrelated.

Pointing to enduring structural rifts over history, the disputed Diaoyu (Senkaku) Islands, and cross-strait issues, Kuo noted that Takaichi previously stated in parliament that Tokyo refrains from commenting on Taiwan's status under international law because Japan has renounced sovereignty over the island.

Kuo said the remarks indirectly touched on the “undetermined status of Taiwan” theory, which Beijing opposes, but should not be conflated with Takaichi’s earlier comments about a Taiwan contingency.

 A China Coast Guard officer observes the Diaoyu Islands from aboard a patrol vessel. (CCG)

**Xi-Takaichi meeting could signal easing tensions**
Kuo said a meeting between Xi and Takaichi at APEC was unlikely, but that Beijing also had an interest in easing tensions with Tokyo amid the current international environment.

Kuo pointed out that,ahead of Japan’s year-end revisions to its National Security Strategy, National Defense Strategy, and Defense Buildup Program, the Japan Innovation Party has called for the blueprints to endorse nuclear-powered submarines and create an exception to Tokyo's Three Non-Nuclear Principles to permit US nuclear-armed assets entry during contingencies.

Pointing out that the APEC summit coincides with coalition-level preparations to deliver defense recommendations to Takaichi, Kuo noted that Tokyo could deploy flexible terminology like "consider" in the revised security documents to retain strategic room for maneuver.

While such defense debates risk antagonizing Beijing, they could paradoxically create openings for renewed bilateral dialogue, Kuo argued. Tokyo’s public discourse on nuclear-powered submarines and potential exemptions to the Three Non-Nuclear Principles may function as a calculated form of strategic signaling toward China, he added.

Beyond the defense document updates, Kuo noted, Takaichi has set her sights on a major constitutional overhaul next year. The four-point reform agenda targets enshrining the legal status of the Self-Defense Forces in pacifist Article 9, creating executive emergency authorities during national crises, ending merged House of Councillors constituencies to ensure representation for each prefecture, and improving educational access.

Kuo said China would not want Japan to revise Article 9 and might therefore seek to coordinate with Tokyo on the matter.

**Japan-Taiwan security cooperation**

Regardless of whether Tokyo and Beijing break the ice on the sidelines of APEC, the direct military threat China poses to Japan remains fundamentally unaltered, Kuo said.

Looking ahead, he predicted that Japan’s updated security documents, due by year-end, will define its stance on security cooperation with Taiwan with unprecedented clarity.

Even if Japan-China relations ease temporarily, Kuo said, Takaichi is unlikely to change her policy toward Taiwan and remains strongly inclined to advance security cooperation with the island.

 In April 2025, Japanese lawmaker Sanae Takaichi led a delegation to visit Taiwan and posed for a photo with Foreign Minister Lin Chia-lung (林佳龍). (MOFA Facebook)

**Taiwan should proceed cautiously**
Kuo said a substantive improvement in Japan-China relations would be difficult under Takaichi’s administration.

Since November last year, he said, China has restricted group travel to Japan and rare-earth supplies, sought to court Japanese opposition parties and factions outside the mainstream of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party, and criticized Takaichi in international forums, putting pressure on her.

Despite Takaichi’s push to deepen economic, technological, and defense alignment with Taiwan, Kuo noted she remains constrained at home by pushback from career diplomats, business interests, opposition parties, and rival ruling-party factions.

Takaichi remains exceedingly unlikely to walk back her statements regarding a Taiwan contingency, Kuo noted. Given the resulting pressure from Beijing and domestic critics, cultivating a close, steadfast rapport with US President Donald Trump has become paramount to underwriting her security agenda, Kuo added.

Kuo urged Taipei to recognize the practical constraints shaping Japan’s cross-strait policy, noting that bilateral cooperation has traditionally advanced most effectively out of the public eye.

Taiwan should respect Tokyo’s appetite for discretion rather than pressing for high-profile diplomatic milestones, allowing practical partnerships to develop steadily beneath the political radar, Kuo added.

title: South Africa’s digital ID system and green book phase-out
summary: _“South Africa is actually building the next evolution of that kind of digital identity system... what we are doing is we are now credentialising your identity in a verifiable format, where at the moment the_[_Estonian solution_](https://ww
content:
_“South Africa is actually building the next evolution of that kind of digital identity system... what we are doing is we are now credentialising your identity in a verifiable format, where at the moment the_[_Estonian solution_](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2025-05-28-digital-dispatch-from-estonia-the-egovernance-capital-of-the-world/)_is card-based ... what we are doing is now made in a purely digital format that’s on your smartphone.”_

That was the explanation Lohan Spies, founder of DIDx, gave when Daily Maverick asked his views on the cooperation between Estonia and South Africa in this digital public infrastructure (DPI) journey.

You can trust him because DIDx is, by its own admission in the bio the company’s PR sent over ahead of our meeting in Techno Park, “a technology-based business that builds Africa’s trusted digital identity and payments infrastructure”.

Spies, a cybersecurity veteran who was building with blockchain before it was cool, founded the company in 2019 and established it as the continent’s most experienced builder of decentralised identity infrastructure.

He also shares Communications Minister Solly Malatsi’s sentiment that Estonia is “a reference point for a lot of DPI development that is happening, and there’s nothing wrong with observing best practice and how it can be useful for our context”.

Spies independently confirmed the minister’s claims that what we are building in South Africa is “not just a cut and paste … because the environments are different, and societal digital skills proficiency is also different”.

Someone [owes the Estonian ambassador an apology](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2026-09-23-estonian-echoes-sas-digital-public-infrastructure-looks-like-it-was-made-in-estonia/).

### **Show, don’t tell**

South Africa is undergoing a comprehensive digital migration designed to overhaul how civil registration, national security and public service delivery function. It’s anchored by the Department of Home Affairs (DHA) strategy for 2025-2030, with the primary objective of transitioning from an inefficient, paper-heavy legacy system into a digital-first organisation under the banner of “Home Affairs @ home”.

This transformation leverages the DPI infrastructure of a secure digital identity framework, an automated risk engine, data-exchange channels and mobile credentials to grant every South African secure identity authentication from smartphone devices or partner facilities.

According to Home Affairs Minister Leon Schreiber, “digital IDs enable instant, paperless processing for banking, work visas and business registrations through an automated risk engine, eliminating months of administrative delays”.

That DHA Strategic Plan reveals that attracting highly skilled workers and streamlining access to work visas can significantly boost economic output; bringing in 11,000 skilled workers annually adds 1.2% to annual GDP growth, while a 10% increase in tourism (through a digitised travel visa system) adds 0.6% to GDP.

And before we start marching (and marching), a digitally authenticated population register linked to the automated biometric identification system prevents illicit entries, fraudulent citizenship acquisition and internal collusion.

When demonstrating the live working prototype using his personal record on the population register, Schreiber emphasised that digital credentials would restore transparency and dignity.

He also confirmed that “on the 31st of March 2028 the Green ID book will officially cease to be recognised as a valid form of identification in terms of section 251B of the Identification Act”.

### **All the pieces clicking together**

Addressing GovTech on behalf of the Presidency’s Digital Services Unit within Operation Vulindlela, Kule Duma detailed the foundational mechanics of South Africa’s Digital Transformation Roadmap.

> “The experience of someone going to a government office is often layered by bureaucracy... They often must borrow money as a first stop, or they must use the very grants that we pay them ... jump on two or three taxis ... get into that long line and at the end they’re told you don’t have the sufficient documentation... We know that we can bring digital services to the tip of people’s fingers.”

He also articulated the central solution: “How should one person experience this one government and one government service ... if I provide government my information once, you shouldn’t have to ask me for that information ... that is the way that we drive it through the data exchange.”

Kule Duma on stage at GovTech 2026. (Photo: Lindsey Schutters)

Spies explained the details as best he understands them – DIDx is doing work in an SA Revenue Service skunkworks project, but his experience of these systems bridges the gap.erv

“DHA will be an issuer, and DHA will issue me with my verifiable credential in [mDoc format](https://www.nist.gov/blogs/cybersecurity-insights/digital-identities-getting-know-verifiable-digital-credential-0),” he says. “Once I then issue that credential to the holder, which is me, the citizen, that then lives in my mobile device, and on the mobile device we make use of the secure enclave on the device. So we make use of what the OEM manufacturer provides us ... to protect the private keys.”

It’s simple, actually, and Schreiber’s demo, erm … demonstrated it perfectly. “In that demo, the reality is they actually move the data by Bluetooth phone to phone,” Spies points out.

“So there’s no third party involved in that at all ... the security there is literally in proximity. It’s directly Bluetooth phone to phone ... you can be completely offline and I can share my credentials.”

### **Goodbye, green mamba**

The paper-based green ID book lacks modern cryptographic security and embedded biometrics. It is easily forged, altered, or duplicated by criminal syndicates, making it the primary vehicle for identity theft and impersonation.

Green ID books also cannot support automated online authentication, remote Know-Your-Customer checks for banks, or digital wallet credentials required for e-commerce and integrated public services.

The solutions being built like Schreiber’s Home Affairs @ home and the Presidency’s MyMzansi app propose a world where citizens can request, renew or authenticate civic identity products (IDs, birth/marriage certificates, passports) online using facial recognition on a mobile phone or computer, with physical cards delivered directly to their doorstep.

The green South African ID book is being phased out in favour of a digital ID system. (Photo: trying2 [adult.com](http://adult.com/) / Wikipedia)

By transferring routine transactions to digital self-service channels, we no longer lose full working days or pay transport costs standing in the queue at Home Affairs offices.

And all that is built on the foundation of a digital ID that anchors the experience with state platforms, including tax compliance with the SA Revenue Service, social grant distribution through Sassa, healthcare records and digital payment systems.

And the future is being built by South Africans. **DM**

# 民進黨：中共涉假車禍跨國鎮壓 暴行令人髮指

2026-10-21 17:23 中央社／ 台北21日電  中共  車禍  民進黨

關閉

民進黨發言人吳崢。聯合報系資料照

[**中共**](https://udn.com/search/tagging/2/%E4%B8%AD%E5%85%B1)涉跨國鎮壓買凶攻擊相聲演員黃逸豪，檢方起訴5嫌建請法院重判。[**民進黨**](https://udn.com/search/tagging/2/%E6%B0%91%E9%80%B2%E9%BB%A8)發言人[**吳崢**](https://udn.com/search/tagging/2/%E5%90%B3%E5%B4%A2)今天表示，中共干預、介入台灣的力道越來越殘暴，嚴重踩到台灣民主法治紅線，台灣不分黨派的政治工作者，應齊聲譴責中共這種令人髮指的暴行。

相聲演員黃逸豪9月演出前遭車撞受傷，新北地檢署查出中共涉跨國鎮壓教唆國內人士阻止其演出，且嫌犯原要讓黃逸豪斷手斷腳，因聽到慘叫才停止，最後依重傷害未遂等罪起訴5人並求處重刑。

針對上述案件，吳崢在民進黨中執會後記者會表示，相信民眾看到這件事情都會非常震驚，此事的本質已近乎恐怖主義的跨國鎮壓，且這位演員不是公職人員、從政者，只是一位在台灣享受言論自由的台灣人民。

吳崢指出，中國竟然連台灣人在台灣的言論也要管、甚至買凶進行這種極度殘暴的行為，相信所有台灣人民絕對不能接受，這已嚴重踩到台灣的國安、治安以及民主法治的紅線。

吳崢說，中國對台灣不論是介選、認知作戰，到現在直接買凶攻擊，意圖使民眾的人身安全受到損傷，這都凸顯中共對台灣干預及介入的力道越來越加強、殘暴。

吳崢認為，台灣不分黨派、支持台灣自由民主的政治工作者，都應齊聲、同聲譴責中共這種令人髮指的暴行，也拜託民眾參與選舉活動、行使自由民主的權利時，一定要多加留意，保護自己的人身安全，行政團隊也會盡全力做好相關因應與應變。

民進黨中國部於臉書撰文，嚴厲譴責中共當局毫不遮掩的流氓行徑，並正告北京當局，立即停止各項跨國鎮壓與對台灣人民威脅的惡劣行徑，台灣人民的生命安全與言論自由，絕不容許任何境外勢力任意侵犯。

此外，陸劇「逐玉」男主角張凌赫申請來台被拒，中國國台辦發言人張晗稱，大陸演藝人員赴台開展文化交流，是「兩岸民眾樂見並期盼的民間往來，有利於增進兩岸民眾相互了解」。民進黨政府拒不同意有關大陸演藝人員赴台交流，這有損兩岸文化交流，應摒棄政治操弄，取消不合理限制。

吳崢說，陸委會已清楚說明此事。出入境管理本來就是國家主權的象徵，例如他10幾年前參加完學運，跟青年夥伴申請港簽時也是直接被拒絕，這都是各國會有的管理作為。

吳崢指出，國台辦希望台灣行政團隊重視台灣粉絲心願，看來國台辦現在也感受到「民主是個好東西」，中國人民在網路上也表達希望中國民主化等心願，值得國台辦參考。

title: US Grapples With China-Linked Critical Minerals Shortfall Left Unresolved By Trump-Xi Summit
summary: WASHINGTON -- When US President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping met in Washington last month, they failed to make headway on one of the most contentious issues in the bilateral relationship: Beijing’s sweeping critical minerals e
content:
WASHINGTON -- When US President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping met in Washington last month, they failed to make headway on one of the most contentious issues in the bilateral relationship: Beijing’s sweeping critical minerals export restrictions that have roiled Pentagon and commercial supply chains alike.

Trump and Xi agreed to extend a trade truce -- set to expire on November 10 -- by two months. But the extension doesn’t address Washington’s core concerns about inadequate minerals exports from China.

During testimony in July before the Senate Finance Committee, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said that China’s mineral exports are “not as much as we would want. It’s not at the pace we would want.”

#### SEE ALSO:

[Trump, Xi Strike Stabilizing Tone At Beijing Summit Shaped By Iran Conflict](https://www.rferl.org/a/trump-xi-summit-iran-war-china-hormuz-nuclear-trade/33757431.html "SEE ALSO: Trump, Xi Strike Stabilizing Tone At Beijing Summit Shaped By Iran Conflict")

China dominates global production and refining of critical minerals and rare earth permanent magnets, which retain their magnetic properties indefinitely without the need for external power. Rare earth permanent magnets are essential for the functionality of everything from electrical vehicle motors and wind turbines to fighter jets and missile guidance systems.

The International Energy Agency (IEA), an autonomous intergovernmental organization based in Paris, estimates that China is the top refiner for 19 out of 20 key strategic minerals, with an average market share of 70 percent.

China has an even tighter grip on permanent magnets with a 94 percent global market share, according to the IEA.

Beijing has weaponized its critical minerals dominance to counter US sanctions on its semiconductor sector and the Trump administration’s tariffs. It has calibrated the export controls to inflict maximum pressure on Pentagon supply chains while avoiding large-scale disruption to consumer industries, which would risk escalation with Washington that China’s ruling Communist Party (CCP) does not want.

Overall, China exported 512 metric tons of rare-earth permanent magnets to the US in August, down 21 percent from July and 13 percent from a year earlier, according to Chinese customs data.

Heading into the summit, Xi sought to leverage China’s strategic metals dominance to secure a lasting trade truce with the United States, says Tomasz Nadrowski, portfolio manager at the New York-based Amvest Terraden Critical Minerals Fund.

“China has this spigot that it can turn on and off -- which determines the flow of critical minerals to the US and other countries,” he told RFE/RL in an interview.

“Extending the trade truce two years would have given this tool additional value,” further locking in US dependency on China’s critical mineral supply chains.

The Trump administration was concerned that with a two-year truce, “everyone [both commercial and defense manufacturers] would relax and think, 'We don’t need to build any new capacity,” he says.

#### SEE ALSO:

[China Looks To Shore Up Influence In Central Asia After US Minerals Diplomacy](https://www.rferl.org/a/china-central-asia-wang-yi-diplomacy-minerals-mining-kyrgyzstan-debt/33597375.html "SEE ALSO: China Looks To Shore Up Influence In Central Asia After US Minerals Diplomacy")

“The US cannot afford to accept strategic chokepoint dependencies for inputs that are essential to our defense industrial base and foundational industries like automotive,” Mahnaz Khan, vice president of policy for critical supply chains at the Silverado Policy Accelerator in Washington, said in an interview.

The two-month truce agreed to by Trump and Xi “buys the United States time, but it doesn’t eliminate the underlying vulnerability,” she said

## **Partnering With Central Asia**

As it works to reduce critical minerals dependence on China, the Trump administration has cast a wide net. In an August [**fact sheet**](https://www.whitehouse.gov/fact-sheets/2026/08/fact-sheet-president-donald-j-trump-announces-billions-in-new-deals-and-investments-to-power-american-mining/), the White House said it has signed or approved more than 160 mineral deals since January 2025, totaling about $40 billion.

While the administration prioritizes domestic minerals production, in some cases, overseas projects are more feasible. This holds true for tungsten, which the United States has not produced at home since 2015. Tungsten is a crucial input for military-grade steel, aerospace components, munitions, and ground vehicle armor. Given its high density, the metal is used for stabilization and control in missiles and aircraft.

Tungsten’s importance for defense led the Trump administration to throw its support behind a $1.1 billion project in Kazakhstan. Under an agreement signed in November 2025 between US-based Cove Capital (now known as the Cove Kaz Capital Group) and the state-run Kazakh mining company Tau-Ken Samruk, the two parties will jointly develop one of the world’s largest tungsten resources.

“Kazakhstan made a conscious political choice to make an award to a US company, though rumor has it that China was also bidding for the same project,” Akbota Karibayeva Meyer, a research fellow at the Caspian Policy Center in Washington, told RFE/RL. The decision exemplifies Kazakhstan’s multi-vector foreign policy, which aims to preserve strategic autonomy by balancing ties with major powers, she explains.

#### SEE ALSO:

[US Revisits Georgia's Black Sea Port As Strategic Corridors Rise](https://www.rferl.org/a/us-georgia-black-sea-iran-trump-trade/33727854.html "SEE ALSO: US Revisits Georgia's Black Sea Port As Strategic Corridors Rise ")

Drilling, feasibility studies, and site preparation began after the agreement’s formal closing. Yet full commercial production is several years away.

“Are these projects in Kazakhstan viable? Sure, they’re viable. The economics are very hard to pencil out without a subsidy, though,” Ian Lange, a professor at the Colorado School of Mines and deputy director of its Critical Materials Innovation Hub, said in an interview.

“Ideally, I might want to do something [in terms of a mining investment] that limits the government’s expenditure and provides for some competition,” he says.

The Trump administration is also working with Uzbekistan to source critical minerals.

In February, the US commodities firm Traxys signed a $1 billion deal with the Uzbek government focused on the exploration and extraction of tungsten, molybdenum, and copper. This agreement aligns with a separate critical minerals pact reached between the US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) and Uzbekistan.

Elsewhere in Central Asia, the potential for cooperation with the US exists. Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan both have major reserves of antimony, a critical mineral used as a flame retardant, an alloying agent for lead, and a compound in semiconductors.

During a September visit to Bishkek, US Special Envoy for South and Central Asia Sergio Gor and US Senator Steve Daines, chairman of the Senate Central Asia Caucus, discussed mining cooperation with Kyrgyz officials.

#### SEE ALSO:

[China Looks To Shore Up Influence In Central Asia After US Minerals Diplomacy](https://www.rferl.org/a/china-central-asia-wang-yi-diplomacy-minerals-mining-kyrgyzstan-debt/33597375.html "SEE ALSO: China Looks To Shore Up Influence In Central Asia After US Minerals Diplomacy")

During their trip, they also met with the presidents of Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and Tajikstan.

While the US continues to make progress sourcing critical minerals from Central Asia, “it is important to recognize the limiting factor of geography,” Karibayeva Meyer says.

Given its proximity to Central Asia, “it is much easier for China to be involved in the region.”

## **Short And Long-Term Challenges**

In the short term, the US faces a key hurdle in its critical minerals diversification push: from January 1, 2027, the Pentagon will prohibit the use of certain metals sourced from the “foreign adversary countries” of China, Russia, North Korea, and Iran.

The ban, outlined in [**Executive Order 14415**](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2026/07/securing-americas-defense-supply-chains-and-ensuring-domestic-acquisition-of-critical-materials/), sharply narrows the possibility of receiving waivers for the use of rare-earth magnets, tungsten, tantalum, and molybdenum from those four nations. Defense firms can no longer be granted a waiver based on cost or convenience reasons. To receive one, they must show that compliant materials are completely unavailable despite exhaustive efforts to source them.

The Aerospace Industries Association (AIA), a Washington-based trade association, said in a [**recent report**](https://www.aia-aerospace.org/publications/strengthening-critical-minerals-supply-chains/) that some of its member companies expect to achieve compliance for certain applications by January 1. Others may need until 2028 or later, given the paucity of compliant aerospace-grade material for several covered materials.

AIA recommends that the Trump administration align compliance requirements with supply chain readiness and preserve flexible waiver authorities.

Lange of the Colorado School of Mines says that the administration may offer defense firms some additional leeway.

In the longer term, analysts say that the United States must focus greater effort on critical minerals processing. Decades of outsourcing production to China have resulted in high regulatory costs, a shortage of specialized metallurgical expertise and a dearth of commercial-scale downstream facilities.

**“**I do see processing as the top, most enduring impediment to large-scale diversification away from China,” Cory Combs, head of critical mineral and supply chain research at the consultancy Trivium China, told RFE/RL.

“Mining is generally much less technologically complex. Processing is where the most critical know-how bottlenecks lie. China's own experience, with decades spent building its processing capabilities, reflects the challenge,” he says.

He further notes that the US lacks strong demand signals in the parts of the production chain between processed minerals and end uses, which limits the scale of offtake agreements necessary to properly fund processing expansions.

Given long project lead times, permitting bottlenecks and capital constraints, analysts expect that Washington will need more than a decade to develop a midstream critical minerals supply chain not dependent on China.

In the meantime, Beijing will aim to exploit that continued dependency to deter the US from imposing further curbs on its development of advanced technologies integral to semiconductors and artificial intelligence.

So far, it has been successful.

Earlier this year, the Trump administration delayed adding more than 100 Chinese firms to the Commerce Department Entity List -- a trade and export blacklist -- because of concern over how Beijing might further throttle rare earth shipments.

China’s continuing dominance of critical minerals could also constrain Washington’s ability to intervene in a Taiwan Strait crisis.

A [**Heritage Foundation report**](https://www.heritage.org/tidalwave/chapters/chapter-6-assessing-the-us-indo-pacific-munitions-system)published in January warns that if China fully weaponizes its export restrictions at the onset of a war, the US could deplete existing stockpiles of minerals needed to produce new advanced munitions in under 90 days.

title: 康乃尔大学轮奸案：Jane Doe 称校长质疑她提出的指控
summary: 图像来源，Reuters 图像加注文字，康乃尔大学的教职员在上周的教务委员会会议上就学校处理性侵案件的方式进行了辩论。 * * Author, 纳尔丁·萨阿德（Nardine Saad） * Author, 普拉蒂克莎·吉尔迪亚尔（Pratiksha Ghildial） * Published 2 小时前 * 阅读时间: 3 分钟 一名康奈尔大学前学生声称，自己在一所兄弟会会所（fraternity house）遭多人轮奸。她表示校长的反应令她感到“得不到支持，也不被相信”。
content:
图像来源，Reuters

图像加注文字，康乃尔大学的教职员在上周的教务委员会会议上就学校处理性侵案件的方式进行了辩论。

*       *   Author, 纳尔丁·萨阿德（Nardine Saad）

    *   Author, 普拉蒂克莎·吉尔迪亚尔（Pratiksha Ghildial）

*   Published 2 小时前

*   阅读时间: 3 分钟

一名康奈尔大学前学生声称，自己在一所兄弟会会所（fraternity house）遭多人轮奸。她表示校长的反应令她感到“得不到支持，也不被相信”。

这名女学生以 Jane Doe （女性无名氏）名义发函，指控校长米高·科特利科夫（Michael Kotlikoff）曾质问她，为何事发数星期后才报案。

这所位于纽约州北部的常春藤联盟（Ivy League）院校表示，该前学生对校长反应的描述“并不正确”。

Jane Doe 把信件寄给校内教职员。本月，教职员将就科特利科夫的表现举行罕见的投票。Jane Doe 上月入禀法院提出诉讼，指控自己在2024年10月参加 Chi Phi 兄弟会派对时遭多名男子强奸。

视频加注文字，全美各地“我是 Jane Doe”抗议活动呼吁停止性暴力（英文影片）

Jane Doe 指控七名前兄弟会成员。BBC的美国合作伙伴哥伦比亚广播公司（CBS）联络他们时，七人全部否认有不当行为。目前没有任何人因此被刑事起诉。

Jane Doe 曾向校园警察报案，当地检察官当时决定不提出起诉，但案件其后已重新展开调查。

康奈尔大学回应 Jane Doe 最初提出的指控时表示，校方已展开内部调查，并进行民权调查。

BBC 取得一封日期为10月14日、共两页的信件。Jane Doe 在信中告诉教务委员会（faculty senate），在她举报强奸事件后，透过他人得知科特利科夫的反应。她表示，校长“最初的反应”大致是：“她为甚么等了这么久才举报事件？”

Jane Doe 于11月8日向校园警察报案，距离她参加兄弟会派对约三星期后。

她指出，科特利科夫曾与她所属姊妹会（sorority）的时任主席交谈，当时亦有其他职员在场。其中至少一人似乎对这名大学校长提出的问题“感到不安”。

Jane Doe 在信中写道：“这削弱了我对校方行政团队的信心。我原本希望、亦期望这所曾是我的梦想学校，能够以理解、敏感和公平的态度看待我的经历，但这件事令我对校方能否做到这一点失去信心。”

她表示，自己写这封信，是希望教职员在10月28日就是否通过对科特利科夫领导层的不信任动议投票前，能够“作出知情的选择”。

大学证实已收到 Jane Doe 律师寄来的信件。

但康奈尔大学发言人向 BBC 表示：“信件提及，科特利科夫校长在2025年1月的一次会议上提出的问题，其相关描述来自他人转述。而根据一份有文件记录、由亲历者提供的第一手说法，这个描述并不正确。”

视频加注文字，“我感到非常震惊”——大学生们对康乃尔大学强暴案调查的反应（英文影片）

发言人表示，科特利科夫就涉嫌强奸事件延迟被举报一事提出的问题，“是针对当时在场的旁观者，而不是 Jane Doe”。发言人指出，尽管2024年10月事件发生后，社交媒体上一直有相关讨论，但旁观者并没有使用康奈尔大学的匿名举报专线。

发言人说：“他质疑的并不是 Jane Doe 报案一事。”

科特利科夫领导这所位于伊萨卡（Ithaca）的学府已有26年。上星期三（14日），他在教务委员会上接受了一连串尖锐提问。

BBC 取得的会议录音显示，教职员对科特利科夫处理案件的方式表示“深感不安”，并指他缺乏“情感上的反应”。

科特利科夫则列举校方因应 Jane Doe 指控而推行的改革，包括禁止举办兄弟会派对。

他说：“对于2024年10月在康奈尔大学发生的事件，我们所有人都感到极度难过。”

康奈尔大学教务委员会是校内的管治机构，由教授及其他学术人员组成。委员会已安排于10月28日就科特利科夫的领导表现进行不信任投票。

会议录音显示，教职员指出校园内的性不当行为是一个系统性问题，需要“从制度层面予以重视”。

支持提出不信任动议的劳工史教授保罗·奥尔蒂斯（Prof Paul Ortiz）表示，学生曾告诉教职员，他们“天黑后走到图书馆都感到不安全”。

他指控康奈尔大学把强奸事件当成“更像是一个‘公关问题’，而不是一宗令人发指的罪行”来处理。

# 美国制裁前谷歌工程师丁林葳创办的公司和奇绩创坛四个主体 中国商务部说坚决反对

茉莉花综合报道 2026年10月21日 08:52

美国国务院10月19日根据《保护美国知识产权法》，以涉嫌窃取美国人的商业秘密为由，制裁与中国公民、前谷歌软件工程师丁林葳有关联的五家实体：丁林葳2023年在中国创办的上海至算科技有限公司，以及奇绩创坛北京投资管理有限责任公司、北京奇绩创坛一期和二期创业投资中心、北京奇绩创坛致远企业管理中心。受影响的是这五家实体和与这五家实体往来的美国人：美国财政部外国资产控制办公室同一天把这五家实体列入非SDN菜单式制裁清单，措施包括冻结这些实体的全部财产和财产权益，除进口货物外禁止与这些实体的一切交易，并另发通用许可证，允许结束涉及这些被冻结实体的交易。

国务院说，这次制裁是在司法部和联邦调查局调查丁林葳之后作出的；美国联邦陪审团今年1月29日裁定丁林葳犯有七项盗窃商业秘密罪，他被裁定窃取了数千页包含谷歌超级智能相关技术商业秘密的机密信息，为自己和设在中国的科技公司牟利。按指控，丁林葳在2023年12月辞职前不到两个星期，把2000多页商业秘密转到个人云端账户；至算科技自称能开发加快机器学习运算的软件平台，包括用超级计算芯片训练大型超级智能模型。奇绩创坛的前身是创业孵化器Y Combinator 2018年开设、由前微软和百度高管陆奇主持的中国业务；Y Combinator 2019年11月关闭中国业务后，陆奇把团队独立出来，成立了奇绩创坛。

丁林葳案和奇绩创坛的几个时间点

1.   2018年 Y Combinator开设中国业务，由陆奇主持
2.   2019年11月 Y Combinator关闭中国业务，陆奇把团队独立出来，成立奇绩创坛
3.   2023年 丁林葳在中国创办上海至算科技有限公司
4.   2023年12月 按指控，丁林葳辞职前不到两个星期，把2000多页商业秘密转到个人云端账户
5.   2026年1月29日 美国联邦陪审团裁定丁林葳犯有七项盗窃商业秘密罪
6.   2026年10月19日 美国国务院制裁与丁林葳有关联的五家实体
7.   2026年10月20日 中国商务部回应说坚决反对，敦促美方纠正

数据：美国国务院、美国司法部和中国商务部的说法，据媒体报道

中国商务部新闻发言人10月20日回应说，美方炒作所谓“窃取商业秘密”问题，污名化中国企业并实施制裁，严重损害中国企业合法权益，中方坚决反对；发言人说，中国人工智能企业的快速发展得益

title: Army Activates Air Defense Guam Battalion Focused on Chinese, North Korean Threats - USNI News
zh_title: 陆军启动关岛防空营重点应对中国和朝鲜威胁 - 美国海军学院新闻
source: 美国海军学会新闻 USNI（军事/海上）（Google新闻聚合）
summary: 美国陆军下士。 2019 年 2 月 6 日，在关岛安德森空军基地的末段高空区域防御 (THAAD) 系统教练机上进行导弹装卸演习时，第 94 陆军防空与导弹防御司令部鹰爪特遣队的爱国者发射站增强型操作员兼维护员罗赫利奥·阿尔格塔 (Rogelio Argueta) 下达命令。 美国陆军照片 美国陆军最近启动了一个驻关岛防空营，旨在保护该岛免受中国和朝鲜日益严重的空中和导弹威胁。第43防空炮兵团第3营，活跃
content:
美国陆军下士。 2019 年 2 月 6 日，关岛安德森空军基地，第 94 陆军防空与导弹防御司令部“爪子”特遣部队的爱国者发射站增强型操作员兼维护员罗赫利奥·阿格塔 (Rogelio Argueta) 在末段高空区域防御 (THAAD) 系统教练机上进行导弹装卸演习时发出命令。美国陆军照片

美国陆军最近在关岛部署了一个防空营，旨在保护该岛免受中国和朝鲜日益先进的空中和导弹威胁。

10月16日组建的第43防空炮兵团第3营将继承“黑爪”特遣部队的关岛防御职责。上一次陆军轮换任务始于 2013 年，旨在应对潜在的朝鲜弹道导弹威胁。

近年来，随着中国人民解放军火箭军的崛起，该任务的重点已扩大到在潜在冲突中抵御中国导弹的攻击。 [五角大楼于 2023 年启动关岛防御系统计划](https://news.usni.org/2023/05/10/pentagon-starts-work-to-build-ballistic-missile-defense-capability-in-guam)满足击败北京的弹道、巡航和高超音速武器所需的要求罢工[.](https://news.usni.org/2023/05/10/pentagon-starts-work-to-build-ballistic-missile-defense-capability-in-guam)
陆军在该营启动的新闻稿中写道：“关岛的战略位置使其成为美国在整个地区军事行动的重要组成部分，支持联合部队行动，同时使防空和导弹防御成为保护支持这些任务所需的部队和基础设施的关键部分。”

2026 年 10 月 16 日，隶属第 94 陆军防空与导弹防御司令部第 43 防空炮兵团、第 38 防空炮兵旅第 3 营的美国陆军士兵参加在关岛安德森空军基地举行的启动仪式。美国陆军照片

随着印太对手远程精确打击能力的增强，地面部队着眼于在关岛加强态势。 3-43 ADA 将运行爱国者、末段高空区域防御和新的中级火力防护能力系统，[_星条旗报_于 8 月报道_。](https://www.stripes.com/theaters/asia_pacific/2026-08-21/guam-defense-patriot-ifpc-systems-22615488.html) 与传统的爱国者和萨德系统相比，IFPC 将提供针对飞机、导弹和无人机的中短程防御。

组合后，这些系统提供了一个分层网络，可以应对潜在的西太平洋冲突中可能出现的各种空中和导弹威胁。
“士兵们开发了连接传感器、指挥和控制系统、发射器和拦截器所需的新程序、关系和集成，以促进统一的防御架构。3-43 ADA 现在支持陆军对关岛战略防御系统的贡献是再合适不过了，”3-43 ADA BN 指挥官约书亚·乌内斯中校在新闻稿中说。

据陆军称，从特遣部队到营的过渡标志着国防部“在印度-太平洋地区建立永久防空能力”的承诺。

2025 年 12 月 16 日，在关岛安德森空军基地举行的指挥变更仪式上，分配到“利爪”特遣部队的美国陆军士兵列队。美国陆军照片

关岛目前的防空系统由六座陆军“萨德”发射装置和美国海军“宙斯盾梳”组成

U.S. Army Cpl. Rogelio Argueta, Patriot Launching Station Enhanced Operator-Maintainer, assigned with Task Force Talon, 94th Army Air and Missile Defense Command gives commands, during a practice missile reload and unload drills on a Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD) system trainer at Andersen Air Force Base, Guam, Feb. 6, 2019. US Army photo

The U.S. Army’s recently activated a Guam-based air defense battalion meant to protect the island from increasingly advanced air and missile threats fielded by China and North Korea.

The 3rd Battalion, 43rd Air Defense Artillery Regiment, activated on Oct. 16, will inherit the defense of Guam responsibilities of Task Force Talon. The previous Army rotational mission began in 2013 to counter potential North Korean ballistic missile threats.

With the rise of the People’s Liberation Army Rocket Force in recent years, the mission has expanded its focus to defend against a barrage of Chinese missiles in a potential conflict. T[he Pentagon initiated plans for the Guam Defense System in 2023 t](https://news.usni.org/2023/05/10/pentagon-starts-work-to-build-ballistic-missile-defense-capability-in-guam)o meet the requirements needed to defeat Beijing’s ballistic, cruise and hypersonic strikes[.](https://news.usni.org/2023/05/10/pentagon-starts-work-to-build-ballistic-missile-defense-capability-in-guam)

“Guam’s strategic location makes it an important part of U.S. military operations throughout the region by supporting joint force operations while making air and missile defense a critical part of protecting the forces and infrastructure needed to support those missions,” reads the Army release on the battalion’s activation.

U.S. Army soldiers assigned to 3rd Battalion, 43rd Air Defense Artillery Regiment, 38th Air Defense Artillery Brigade, 94th Army Air and Missile Defense Command, participate in an activation ceremony on Andersen Air Force Base, Guam, Oct. 16, 2026. US Army photo

The ground branch has eyed a reinforced posture on Guam with the increase of Indo-Pacific adversaries’ long-range precision strike capabilities. The 3-43 ADA will operate Patriot, Terminal High Altitude Area Defense and new Intermediate Fires Protection Capability systems, [_Stars and Stripes reported_ in August.](https://www.stripes.com/theaters/asia_pacific/2026-08-21/guam-defense-patriot-ifpc-systems-22615488.html) Compared to the legacy Patriot and THAAD systems, IFPC will provide medium- to short-range defense against aircraft, missiles and drones.

When combined, the systems provide a layered network to engage a variety of air and missile threats that could be fielded in a potential Western Pacific conflict.

“The soldiers developed new procedures, relationships and integration required to connect sensors, command and control systems, launchers and interceptors to promote a unified defensive architecture. It’s only fitting that 3-43 ADA now stands up the Army’s contribution to the strategic Guam Defense System,” Lt. Col. Joshua Urness, 3-43 ADA BN commander, said in the release.

According to the Army, the transition from task force to battalion signals the Defense Department’s commitment “toward permanent air defense capabilities in the Indo-Pacific.”

U.S. Army soldiers assigned to Task Force Talon stand in formation during a change of command ceremony at Andersen Air Force Base, Guam, Dec. 16, 2025. US Army photo

Guam’s current air defenses are composed of six Army THAAD launchers and U.S. Navy Aegis Combat System warships assigned to its defense on an as-need basis. Future plans aim to integrate a networked system capable of conducting 360-degree detection and interception of air and missile threats.

Since Task Force Talon’s original mission over a decade ago, the complexity and quantity of Indo-Pacific missile threats has only increased. Today, the People’s Liberation Army Navy is in the [process of fielding](https://news.usni.org/2026/03/05/chinese-navy-expanding-nuclear-attack-boat-fleet-and-missile-strike-capabilities-oni-commander-says) more nuclear attack boats equipped with vertical launching systems. [The Pentagon has also said it expects the PLAN to have a nine carrier strike group force by 2035,](https://news.usni.org/2025/12/24/china-wants-nine-aircraft-carriers-by-2035-says-new-pentagon-report) which will expand Beijing’s blue water projection capabilities.

title: East Africa: Ruto Hands Comesa Chairmanship to Mnangagwa
summary: Nairobi — Africa must take greater responsibility for financing its development by strengthening its own financial institutions, President William Ruto has said. The President urged African States to show confidence in African institutions,
content:
Nairobi — Africa must take greater responsibility for financing its development by strengthening its own financial institutions, President William Ruto has said.

The President urged African States to show confidence in African institutions, saying they have already demonstrated their capacity by financing Africa's trade, insuring the continent's risks and standing with African States when others stepped back.

He called on African governments to place more of their reserves with African institutions, channel development projects through them and back their bonds and guarantees.

Through the Alliance of African Multilateral Financial Institutions, he explained, African institutions can now pool their strength and act on a continental scale.

"We cannot ask the world to trust African institutions if we do not trust them ourselves. Africa holds more than $4 trillion in domestic financial assets. Yet much of these sit in foreign accounts, earning little while our own projects wait for capital," he said.

President Ruto made the remarks on Thursday during the 25th Summit of the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA) Heads of State and Government held at the New Parliament Building in Harare, Zimbabwe.

Zambian President Hakainde Hichilema, COMESA Secretary-General Chileshe Mpundu Kapwepwe and AfCFTA Secretary-General Wamkele Mene were among those present.

Kenya, President Ruto pointed out, has increased shareholding in Afreximbank, the Africa Finance Corporation and African Trade and Investment Development Insurance (ATIDI).

"Just for your information, the $16 billion East Africa refinery that will be built in Kenya will be almost wholly funded by African financial institutions. That is the scale of the resources that we have," he said.

He noted that Africa cannot be ambitious in its plans and timid in financing them.

"Every programme we agree upon must be matched by the resources to deliver it. Otherwise, our communiqués will promise what our budgets cannot pay for," he said.

At the summit, President Ruto handed over the chairmanship of COMESA to Zimbabwean President Emmerson Mnangagwa.

He expressed confidence in President Mnangagwa's leadership to take COMESA forward.

"Under his stewardship, and with the support of every Member State, I trust that we will turn the ambition of One Market, One Future into progress our people can see and feel," he said.

The President said he was proud of the progress made during Kenya's chairmanship, including stronger economic growth, increased intra-regional trade and deeper digital integration.

"When we assumed the Chair, we set one priority: Leveraging digitalisation to deepen regional value chains for sustainable and inclusive growth. Today, that priority is a programme, not a slogan," he said.

As the outgoing chairperson, President Ruto also presented and launched the COMESA 2026-2030 Medium-Term Strategic Plan and the 2025 Annual Report.

The report, he said, outlines the need to accelerate intra-African trade, eliminate non-tariff barriers, improve connectivity and ensure the benefits of integration reach every segment of society.

He noted that as the global order shifts and protectionism rises, Africa's response must be deeper regional integration, stronger value chains and increased trade among African States.

He pointed out that the greatest market for Africa's goods is Africa.

"Regional integration is no longer a dream we discuss. It is an economic and strategic necessity. We must trade more among ourselves, build resilient regional value chains and deepen our productive capacity so that we can withstand the next shock and seize the next opportunity," he said.

The President, therefore, called on the COMESA Secretariat to fast-track the COMESA Market Levy to secure sustainable and predictable financing for regional priorities.

He explained that integration should be measured not by the volume of trade or the strength of institutions alone but by the opportunities created for citizens of the continent.

The President also said Africa seeks a new engagement with its partners, rooted in sovereign equality, built on mutual benefit and measured by shared prosperity.

President Ruto reiterated that the era of extracting Africa's natural resources without corresponding benefits for the continent must give way to mutually beneficial partnerships.

"To every partner who seeks our minerals, our markets and our young workforce, our offer is clear: Invest with us, process with us, build with us. We will be fair in our partnerships, firm in our interests, open in our markets, and reliable in our word," he said.

He added: "Africa does not come asking for a seat at the edge of the table. We come to help set it."

On his part, President Mnangagwa commended President Ruto for his steadfast leadership during his tenure, steering COMESA with purpose and clarity, particularly in digitalisation and regional value chains.

He called on the summit to advance practical and sustainable solutions that will strengthen resilience, reposition the region to better navigate global shocks and promote the prosperity of the continent.

"With unity of purpose, let us deliver on the promise of shared prosperity, a better life and a better future for the people of Africa," he said.

President Hichilema called on African nations to walk the talk on integration by unlocking the continent's resources for the benefit of its people and the vast African market.

He said that Africans are responsible for developing Africa, noting that others will follow if citizens take the lead.

"We are all saying the right things. We must now take the extra steps to realise this vision. And nobody will do it other than ourselves," he said.

title: Are global oil reserves sufficient to withstand renewed US-Iran war?

content:
Oil prices have climbed towards their highest levels in five months as attacks on tankers in and around the Strait of Hormuz mount and efforts to end the United States-Israel war on Iran are deadlocked.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, rose by more than $2 to $110.85 a barrel on Wednesday, close to a five-month peak.

A day earlier, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said two tankers were “set ablaze” after hitting mines at what it called an illegal crossing point in the strait. Then, on Thursday, the IRGC said it hit [seven more tankers](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/22/iran-says-seven-ships-hit-in-hormuz-strait-warns-us-of-wider-response) although Washington dismissed the claim. In a statement, the IRGC said four of the vessels were transferring oil when they were targeted and caught fire overnight.

In September, the Houthis, an armed group also known as Ansar Allah (Arabic for Supporters of God), seized territory in Yemen close to the Bab al-Mandeb strait, a critical chokepoint into and out of the Red Sea and a gateway to Egypt’s Suez Canal.

The escalation came as the world’s emergency oil stocks, already tapped heavily since the Iran war began on February 28, sit at their lowest levels in decades.

Al Jazeera put a question to analysts: If fighting resumes in full, the Strait of Hormuz is shut off completely and Houthi attacks choke off Bab al-Mandeb, how long could the world’s reserves last?

Here’s what you need to know:

## What emergency oil reserves are there?

Strategic oil reserves are stockpiles of crude oil and fuel held by governments or by companies on their behalf for use in a supply emergency.

The International Energy Agency (IEA), which was established in 1974 after the Arab oil embargo, coordinates most of them. Its importing members must hold at least 90 days of net imports. China and India are not members.

## How much of the reserves has already been released this year?

A record amount.

On March 11, days after the start of the US-Israel war on Iran, the IEA’s 32 members agreed to make [400 million barrels](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/3/13/iea-announces-release-of-400-million-barrels-of-oil-but-is-it-enough) available from emergency supplies, more than double the volume released after Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

The US pledged 172.2 million barrels from its Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) and Japan 79.8 million, according to IEA figures.

The SPR has since fallen to 283 million barrels, its lowest level since October 1982, according to the US Department of Energy.

Much of that oil was lent rather than sold and must be returned with extra barrels, according to the US Energy Information Administration.

Iran’s IRGC says four ships hit in Gulf, three others struck mines near Hormuz

## How much oil is left?

Far less than before the war began in February, and not all of it can be used.

Aaron Kildow, a senior crude oil analyst at Sparta Commodities, told Al Jazeera that global strategic stocks excluding China and Iran have fallen by nearly 327 million barrels since the end of December 2025 with the US, Europe and Japan accounting for about 95 percent of the draw.

He estimated that leaves only about 400 million barrels of usable reserves worldwide, excluding China’s stockpile, which is unlikely to be exported, and Gulf stocks, which could be cut off by a total closure of Hormuz.

Nearly half of these available stocks are in Japan.

Europe has about 76 million barrels uncommitted, but members such as Germany are holding some back for a local emergency, Kildow said.

“Europe is the real wildcard, both on timing and willingness,” Kildow said.

Meanwhile, China’s onshore crude stocks stand at 1.13 billion barrels, down from 1.23 billion in late February but still enough for about 80 days of refinery intake, Muyu Xu, a senior crude oil analyst at the analytics firm Kpler, told Al Jazeera.

India’s reserves cover just eight days of its imports, the Reuters news agency reported.

## What would a full closure of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandeb mean?

Before the war, about one-fifth of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas supplies, or roughly 20 million barrels of oil a day, passed through the Strait of Hormuz.

Saudi Arabia has increased the amount of crude it transports from its oilfields in the east to its Red Sea port of Yanbu in the west via the East-West Pipeline, thereby bypassing Hormuz.

But there have been strikes on that pipeline, and tankers heading south from Yanbu must pass through Bab a-Mandeb, where the Iran-backed Houthis declared a blockade on Saudi shipping in July.

Only a confirmed 373,000 barrels a day of [Saudi crude](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/5/yemen-forces-claim-to-seize-dhubab-sites-near-bab-al-mandeb-from-houthis) have transited Bab al-Mandeb so far this month, the lowest level since February, Xu said, with most Yanbu cargoes now heading north via Egypt instead.

If Hormuz were shut and the Houthis blocked all Saudi tankers, Gulf producers could export only through a few pipelines and Yanbu’s northbound route, Xu said.

That would leave about 7.5 million barrels a day of Middle Eastern crude, against 16.8 million now, a shortfall of about 9.3 million barrels a day, she estimated.

“If such attacks occur, the supply disruption could be even more severe and prolonged,” Xu said, referring to strikes on oilfields, terminals and pipelines.

[Al Jazeera]

## So how long would reserves last?

Not for long – possibly just weeks, according to experts.

If Kpler’s estimated shortfall had to be covered entirely from the roughly 400 million usable barrels that Kildow identified, they could not, in practice, be released that fast. Japanese and South Korean reserves can move quickly, Kildow said, but US barrels are staged over three months, and Europe’s contribution is uncertain.

Chris Beauchamp, chief market analyst at IG Group, said the world was fortunate after the first closure. “The salient feature of March and beyond was how a crisis didn’t actually develop. We got away with it,” he said.

“I don’t think the global economy will be as lucky next time if there is a protracted conflict,” Beauchamp said. “A month or two is all we have.”

The world would not literally run out of oil. Instead, prices would rise until enough demand disappeared. “One hundred fifty dollars [per barrel] becomes a very distinct possibility, which then sees significant demand destruction,” Beauchamp said.

The sharpest squeeze would be on diesel, which is already nearly double the price of crude, the IEA said.

Refiners would compete for crude grades rich in diesel, “a cost that ultimately lands on consumers,” Kildow said.

Video Duration 2 minutes 26 seconds

2:26

US envoy Tom Barrack questions Gulf alliances as Qatar mediates US-Iran talks

## Who would feel it first?

Asian importers with thin reserves.

Most Gulf exports in September and October went to Asian buyers, and India and Pakistan are among the most exposed, Kildow said, adding that their nearest alternative supply, from West Africa, is 25 to 28 days away by sea, compared with two days from Fujairah in the United Arab Emirates.

“The squeeze won’t hit uniformly. It lands fastest and hardest where reserves are thinnest and substitute supply is farthest away,” Kildow said.

## Who would gain?

Oil producers far from the Gulf.

In the second quarter of this year, as the US-Iran war was under way, ExxonMobil reported earnings of $14.5bn, its [highest in four years](https://www.aljazeera.com/features/2026/8/4/why-are-oil-companies-posting-record-profits-amid-iran-war-disruption) while Chevron posted $12bn, its best in six years and Shell more than doubled its earnings to nearly $10bn. Their profits are largely down to the high oil prices.

A second shock would send refiners scrambling for supplies from the US, Latin America, West Africa and Russia, Xu said.

“This would allow non-Middle Eastern producers to benefit from higher crude prices, potentially alongside lower transportation costs,” she said.

In August, US President Donald Trump said companies such as ExxonMobil and Chevron were “making too much money based on a shortage”.

zh_title: 陆军启动关岛防空营重点应对中国和朝鲜威胁 - 美国海军学院新闻
summary: 美国陆军下士。 2019 年 2 月 6 日，在关岛安德森空军基地的末段高空区域防御 (THAAD) 系统教练机上进行导弹装卸演习时，第 94 陆军防空与导弹防御司令部鹰爪特遣队的爱国者发射站增强型操作员兼维护员罗赫利奥·阿尔格塔 (Rogelio Argueta) 下达命令。 美国陆军照片 美国陆军最近启动了一个驻关岛防空营，旨在保护该岛免受中国和朝鲜日益严重的空中和导弹威胁。第43防空炮兵团第3营，活跃
content:
美国陆军下士。 2019 年 2 月 6 日，关岛安德森空军基地，第 94 陆军防空与导弹防御司令部“爪子”特遣部队的爱国者发射站增强型操作员兼维护员罗赫利奥·阿格塔 (Rogelio Argueta) 在末段高空区域防御 (THAAD) 系统教练机上进行导弹装卸演习时发出命令。美国陆军照片

美国陆军最近在关岛部署了一个防空营，旨在保护该岛免受中国和朝鲜日益先进的空中和导弹威胁。

10月16日组建的第43防空炮兵团第3营将继承“黑爪”特遣部队的关岛防御职责。上一次陆军轮换任务始于 2013 年，旨在应对潜在的朝鲜弹道导弹威胁。

近年来，随着中国人民解放军火箭军的崛起，该任务的重点已扩大到在潜在冲突中抵御中国导弹的攻击。 [五角大楼于 2023 年启动关岛防御系统计划](https://news.usni.org/2023/05/10/pentagon-starts-work-to-build-ballistic-missile-defense-capability-in-guam)满足击败北京的弹道、巡航和高超音速武器所需的要求罢工[.](https://news.usni.org/2023/05/10/pentagon-starts-work-to-build-ballistic-missile-defense-capability-in-guam)
陆军在该营启动的新闻稿中写道：“关岛的战略位置使其成为美国在整个地区军事行动的重要组成部分，支持联合部队行动，同时使防空和导弹防御成为保护支持这些任务所需的部队和基础设施的关键部分。”

2026 年 10 月 16 日，隶属第 94 陆军防空与导弹防御司令部第 43 防空炮兵团、第 38 防空炮兵旅第 3 营的美国陆军士兵参加在关岛安德森空军基地举行的启动仪式。美国陆军照片

随着印太对手远程精确打击能力的增强，地面部队着眼于在关岛加强态势。 3-43 ADA 将运行爱国者、末段高空区域防御和新的中级火力防护能力系统，[_星条旗报_于 8 月报道_。](https://www.stripes.com/theaters/asia_pacific/2026-08-21/guam-defense-patriot-ifpc-systems-22615488.html) 与传统的爱国者和萨德系统相比，IFPC 将提供针对飞机、导弹和无人机的中短程防御。

组合后，这些系统提供了一个分层网络，可以应对潜在的西太平洋冲突中可能出现的各种空中和导弹威胁。
“士兵们开发了连接传感器、指挥和控制系统、发射器和拦截器所需的新程序、关系和集成，以促进统一的防御架构。3-43 ADA 现在支持陆军对关岛战略防御系统的贡献是再合适不过了，”3-43 ADA BN 指挥官约书亚·乌内斯中校在新闻稿中说。

据陆军称，从特遣部队到营的过渡标志着国防部“在印度-太平洋地区建立永久防空能力”的承诺。

2025 年 12 月 16 日，在关岛安德森空军基地举行的指挥变更仪式上，分配到“利爪”特遣部队的美国陆军士兵列队。美国陆军照片

关岛目前的防空系统由六座陆军“萨德”发射装置和美国海军“宙斯盾梳”组成

【原文 English Original】
U.S. Army Cpl. Rogelio Argueta, Patriot Launching Station Enhanced Operator-Maintainer, assigned with Task Force Talon, 94th Army Air and Missile Defense Command gives commands, during a practice missile reload and unload drills on a Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD) system trainer at Andersen Air Force Base, Guam, Feb. 6, 2019. US Army photo

The U.S. Army’s recently activated a Guam-based air defense battalion meant to protect the island from increasingly advanced air and missile threats fielded by China and North Korea.

The 3rd Battalion, 43rd Air Defense Artillery Regiment, activated on Oct. 16, will inherit the defense of Guam responsibilities of Task Force Talon. The previous Army rotational mission began in 2013 to counter potential North Korean ballistic missile threats.

With the rise of the People’s Liberation Army Rocket Force in recent years, the mission has expanded its focus to defend against a barrage of Chinese missiles in a potential conflict. T[he Pentagon initiated plans for the Guam Defense System in 2023 t](https://news.usni.org/2023/05/10/pentagon-starts-work-to-build-ballistic-missile-defense-capability-in-guam)o meet the requirements needed to defeat Beijing’s ballistic, cruise and hypersonic strikes[.](https://news.usni.org/2023/05/10/pentagon-starts-work-to-build-ballistic-missile-defense-capability-in-guam)

“Guam’s strategic location makes it an important part of U.S. military operations throughout the region by supporting joint force operations while making air and missile defense a critical part of protecting the forces and infrastructure needed to support those missions,” reads the Army release on the battalion’s activation.

U.S. Army soldiers assigned to 3rd Battalion, 43rd Air Defense Artillery Regiment, 38th Air Defense Artillery Brigade, 94th Army Air and Missile Defense Command, participate in an activation ceremony on Andersen Air Force Base, Guam, Oct. 16, 2026. US Army photo

The ground branch has eyed a reinforced posture on Guam with the increase of Indo-Pacific adversaries’ long-range precision strike capabilities. The 3-43 ADA will operate Patriot, Terminal High Altitude Area Defense and new Intermediate Fires Protection Capability systems, [_Stars and Stripes reported_ in August.](https://www.stripes.com/theaters/asia_pacific/2026-08-21/guam-defense-patriot-ifpc-systems-22615488.html) Compared to the legacy Patriot and THAAD systems, IFPC will provide medium- to short-range defense against aircraft, missiles and drones.

When combined, the systems provide a layered network to engage a variety of air and missile threats that could be fielded in a potential Western Pacific conflict.

“The soldiers developed new procedures, relationships and integration required to connect sensors, command and control systems, launchers and interceptors to promote a unified defensive architecture. It’s only fitting that 3-43 ADA now stands up the Army’s contribution to the strategic Guam Defense System,” Lt. Col. Joshua Urness, 3-43 ADA BN commander, said in the release.

According to the Army, the transition from task force to battalion signals the Defense Department’s commitment “toward permanent air defense capabilities in the Indo-Pacific.”

U.S. Army soldiers assigned to Task Force Talon stand in formation during a change of command ceremony at Andersen Air Force Base, Guam, Dec. 16, 2025. US Army photo

Guam’s current air defenses are composed of six Army THAAD launchers and U.S. Navy Aegis Combat System warships assigned to its defense on an as-need basis. Future plans aim to integrate a networked system capable of conducting 360-degree detection and interception of air and missile threats.

Since Task Force Talon’s original mission over a decade ago, the complexity and quantity of Indo-Pacific missile threats has only increased. Today, the People’s Liberation Army Navy is in the [process of fielding](https://news.usni.org/2026/03/05/chinese-navy-expanding-nuclear-attack-boat-fleet-and-missile-strike-capabilities-oni-commander-says) more nuclear attack boats equipped with vertical launching systems. [The Pentagon has also said it expects the PLAN to have a nine carrier strike group force by 2035,](https://news.usni.org/2025/12/24/china-wants-nine-aircraft-carriers-by-2035-says-new-pentagon-report) which will expand Beijing’s blue water projection capabilities.

### [Aaron-Matthew Lariosa](https://news.usni.org/author/amlariosa)

Aaron-Matthew Lariosa is a freelance defense journalist. His coverage focuses on Philippine defense modernization, the South China Sea and U.S. efforts in the first island chain.

title: 一文读懂：中国有权要求美国军舰“无害通过”前事先通知吗？国际法怎么说？
summary: 中国星期二(10月20日)派遣海军力量监视美国海军查尔斯顿号(USS Charleston)在南中国海萨比纳浅滩(Sabina Shoal)附近的航行。美国则表示，中国试图执行其非法海洋主张，破坏地区稳定；美国将继续在国际法允许的范围内开展海空行动。 美国国务院美国东部时间星期二晚间在回应美国之音时表示，维护海洋自由、遵守国际海洋法对整个国际社会都至关重要。美国将继续在国际法允许的任何地方飞行、航行和行动，包括南中国海。 那么，中国是否有权要求美国军舰在“无害通过”相关海域前
content:
中国星期二(10月20日)派遣海军力量监视美国海军查尔斯顿号(USS Charleston)在南中国海萨比纳浅滩(Sabina Shoal)附近的航行。美国则表示，中国试图执行其非法海洋主张，破坏地区稳定；美国将继续在国际法允许的范围内开展海空行动。

美国国务院美国东部时间星期二晚间在回应美国之音时表示，维护海洋自由、遵守国际海洋法对整个国际社会都至关重要。美国将继续在国际法允许的任何地方飞行、航行和行动，包括南中国海。

那么，中国是否有权要求美国军舰在“无害通过”相关海域前事先通知，甚至获得批准？美国为什么认为自己有权继续行动？萨比纳浅滩的自然属性又与这场争议有什么关系？

**萨比纳浅滩的特殊之处**

萨比纳浅滩位于菲律宾巴拉望岛以西约75海里。菲律宾称其为埃斯科达浅滩(Escoda Shoal)，并认为它位于菲律宾的200海里专属经济区内。中国称其为仙宾礁。

其中的一个争议，是萨比纳浅滩究竟属于什么类型的自然地物，以及它在国际海洋法下能够产生哪些海洋权利。

耶鲁法学院高级研究学者， 法学教授彼得·达顿(Peter Dutton)说，萨比纳浅滩是一处低潮高地(low-tide elevation)，并非能够独立产生领海等海洋权利的岛屿。

“萨比纳浅滩是一处低潮高地，这意味着该浅滩没有任何部分能够永久露出水面。根据国际法，低潮高地被视为最近沿海国家大陆架的一部分。在这种情况下，最近的沿海国家是菲律宾。”他告诉美国之音。

这一问题涉及《[联合国海洋法公约](https://www.un.org/depts/los/convention_agreements/texts/unclos/part2.htm)》(United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea，简称UNCLOS)第13条。该条规定，低潮高地是指在低潮时露出水面、高潮时被淹没的自然形成陆地区域。如果低潮高地位于大陆或岛屿领海外界以内、距离不超过领海宽度，其低潮线可以用于测算领海宽度；如果它完全位于大陆或岛屿领海外，且距离超过领海宽度，则不拥有自己的领海。

通俗地说，一片浅滩不会因为退潮时露出水面，就自动成为一座可以产生领海和专属经济区的岛屿。

达顿还说：“作为一处低潮高地，萨比纳浅滩本身不拥有领海或其他海洋权利。除非附近其他地物的领海覆盖该浅滩，否则浅滩周边海域属于享有航行等自由的海域。不过，即使在这种情况下，像‘查尔斯顿’号这样的军舰，在法律上仍有权在浅滩周边行使无害通过权。”

**中国有没有权要求美国军舰事先通知？**

中国称其对南中国海包括萨比纳浅滩的广泛海域拥有领海主权，并反对美国军舰在其所称的相关海域开展行动。

中国解放军南部战区海军新闻发言人尹刚海军大校星期二通报，美军查尔斯顿号当天凌晨“冲闯南沙群岛仙宾礁（菲称萨比纳礁）附近海域。”

澳大利亚西悉尼大学法学院副教授洛厄尔·包蒂斯塔(Lowell Bautista)告诉美国之音，中国不能仅凭自己的主权主张，就要求外国军舰在周边海域航行前获得许可或提前通知。

萨比纳浅滩的自然属性已经决定了这一点，但即使是一国领海和专属经济区，外国船舶均享有国际法保护的“无害通过权”。根据《联合国海洋法公约》，“无害通过”即“继续不停和迅速”通过。“无害通过”的军舰不会展开任何军事演练和直升机升空等行动。

包蒂斯塔解释，根据《联合国海洋法公约》第58条和第87条，各国船舶，包括军舰，在专属经济区内享有航行自由，通常不需要事先获得沿海国许可。专属经济区则可延伸至基线以外200海里。沿海国在这里主要享有渔业、海底资源开发等方面的权利。

“中国主张，外国在专属经济区内进行军事活动须征得中国同意，但这一观点并未得到《联合国海洋法公约》的支持，也遭到大多数海洋国家的反对。无论如何，过境属于行使航行自由的行为，而航行自由是《公约》所保护的最基本自由。”他告诉美国之音。

但1992年中国出台的《中华人民共和国领海及毗连区法》要求外国军用船舶进入中国领海，须经中国政府批准，即便是“无害通过”。

“即使在领海内，沿海国拥有的管辖权要强得多，《联合国海洋法公约》第17条仍承认所有国家的船舶，包括军舰，均享有无害通过权，但须遵守《公约》规定的相关要求。”包蒂斯塔说。领海通常延伸至海岸基线以外12海里，沿海国在这里享有主权。

他补充说，虽然美国不是《联合国海洋法公约》的缔约国，但美国接受并依据习惯接受公约中的许多航行自由规则。中国则是公约缔约国，受其相关规定约束。

**美国的立场：航行自由不需要中国批准**

美国国务院就此事回应美国之音时表示，维护海洋自由、遵守国际海洋法对整个国际社会都至关重要。美国将继续在国际法允许的范围内开展行动，包括在南中国海飞行和航行。

国务院指责中国试图执行其所称的非法海洋主张，损害了地区稳定，也侵害了美国及其他国家的合法权利和自由。

美国的立场是：不能因为中国声称对某片海域拥有权利，就认定美国军舰必须先得到中国批准才能航行。

**核心总结：**

根据《联合国海洋法公约》第13条，萨比纳浅滩的自然属性决定其附近地区不能被称为领海，所以中国对美国军舰的指控并没有法律依据。

根据《联合国海洋法公约》第58条和第87条，各国船舶，包括军舰，在专属经济区内享有航行自由，通常不需要事先获得沿海国许可。

根据《联合国海洋法公约》第17条，即使是在领海内，外国军舰原则上也享有无害通过权；中国要求外国军舰进入其领海前事先获得批准的立场，本身就不符合国际法的规定。

title: Title deeds key to unlocking SA agriculture’s full potential
summary: South Africa’s agriculture is entering a period of change, which may bring shared prosperity. For some time, we have talked about the country having “two agricultures”: one commercially oriented and white, and one resource-poor, smallholder
content:
South Africa’s agriculture is entering a period of change, which may bring shared prosperity. For some time, we have talked about the country having “two agricultures”: one commercially oriented and white, and one resource-poor, smallholder and black.

South Africa’s land history largely explains these disparities, but inefficiencies in land reform have also compounded them.

The South African government has acquired land in the open market over the years but hasn’t successfully transferred it to deserving black farmers with title deeds.

Farmers have typically received short-term leases, which hindered their agricultural possibilities. But this is changing. The government is now releasing the state land with title deeds.

Speaking in Stutterheim in Eastern Cape on 8 October 2026, President Cyril Ramaphosa underscored the point that the state-owned land would be transferred to beneficiaries with title deeds.

This was a build-up to the message the President has already underscored on 2 June 2026, when he delivered the Presidency’s Budget Vote speech, which carried vital messages for the long-term growth of South Africa’s agriculture.

### **Productive land**

Among other things, the President stated that “access to productive land is essential to grow our agricultural output further, create jobs and lift people out of poverty. Over time, the government has acquired around 2.5 million hectares of land under the Proactive Land Acquisition Strategy programme”.

He further stated that “this land has generally been leased to beneficiaries on a short-term basis, which limits their ability to borrow money, invest in the land, grow agricultural production and contribute to the rural economy”.

We concur and believe the lack of title deeds has been the major constraint to inclusive growth in South Africa’s agriculture. With the President now signalling the start of the title-deeds release process, we may start to see some positive action to grow the sector.

The President further stated that “as part of our efforts to revitalise rural economies, to strengthen land rights and support the inclusion of black farmers in commercial agriculture, we have embarked on a concerted programme to release this land with title deeds to deserving beneficiaries. The Minister of Land Reform and Rural Development will outline the details of the programme to convert agricultural leases to title deeds.”

Essentially, this step is fundamental to achieving the goals outlined in Chapter 6 of the National Development Plan (NDP) and, thereafter, in the Agriculture and Agro-processing Master Plan (AAMP). Both documents highlighted the sector’s potential to grow and create new jobs. In fact, the NDP indicates that the sector and its value chain could create close to a million new jobs.

### Title deeds open up job opportunities

Matumeleng Jali removes covers that keep soil cool and deter pests before harvesting spinach at the Costa farm in Klippoortje, Boksburg. (Photo: Felix Dlangamandla)

Part of the prerequisites for those jobs was through strengthening land rights and allocating the land in the government’s books to the deserving beneficiaries. Over time, South Africa’s primary agriculture sector has delivered jobs, from 718,000 at the end of 2012, when the NDP was published, to 960,000 in the first quarter of 2026. The sector’s value chain also created employment during this period.

Still, these job gains were far below the nearly million jobs the NDP envisaged in the sector and its value chain.

One constraint on job gains was the slow progress in releasing land with title deeds. Now that the President has directed the release of this land with title deeds, we see greater opportunities for growth and job creation in the sector.

The Department of Land Reform and Rural Development has heeded this call and is now releasing this land.

Essentially, releasing the land will be a powerful step towards boosting inclusive growth in agriculture. This land is also key to ensuring we finally make progress in implementing the AAMP.

Importantly, organised agriculture, labour and agribusinesses, among other key stakeholders, will continue to play a role in boosting inclusive growth in the sector, having helped draft the AAMP.

In essence, agriculture remains one of the sectors of our economy with potential for growth and job creation. The President’s important step to strengthen land rights is key to realising this vision and supporting the rural economies.

Importantly, this also signals that property rights are intact in South Africa and that investment in farming is protected. **DM**

_Wandile Sihlobo is the Presidential Envoy on Agriculture and Land. He is also the chief economist of the Agricultural Business Chamber of South Africa and a senior research fellow in the Department of Agricultural Economics at Stellenbosch University._

title: U.S. Curb on Chinese Drones Hurts American Users
summary: Foreign tourists select handheld photography equipment at a DJI flagship store in Shenzhen. (PHOTO: XINHUA) U.S. restrictions on Chinese-made drones are hurting cash-strapped American police departments, forcing some to scramble for ways to
content:
Foreign tourists select handheld photography equipment at a DJI flagship store in Shenzhen. (PHOTO: XINHUA)
U.S. restrictions on Chinese-made drones are hurting cash-strapped American police departments, forcing some to scramble for ways to afford the more expensive American-made alternatives, according to an October 12 report by NPR.

The report quoted Jon Beal, head of the Law Enforcement Drone Association (LEDA), as saying Chinese-made drones are "light years ahead of what our American drones are able to do."

Beal said Chinese company DJI offers a drone with an impressive high-resolution thermal camera that costs less than 10,000 USD. In comparison, American-made drones have lower flight-time capabilities, thermal imaging and zoom. They usually cost between 20,000 USD and 50,000 USD, depending on the type and the model.

In recent years, the U.S. has steadily erected barriers to the import and sale of Chinese drones. In December 2025, the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) added foreign-produced unmanned aircraft systems and critical components to its "Covered List," restricting the authorization of new models for import and sale. In July 2026, the FCC sought to label civilian drones as "military-grade," expanding the scope of restrictions. In addition, several other U.S. government agencies have repeatedly used their regulatory powers to target Chinese drones.

The difficulties facing U.S. police departments are just one example of the wider consequences of these restrictions. Similar problems are emerging across multiple industries.

According to Construction Executive, a U.S. construction industry news outlet, 36 percent of American contractors are using drones, and nearly all of them rely on Chinese products. The U.S. government's prohibition on the use of Chinese drones by contractors working on government projects has put these businesses under pressure.

Sales of new agricultural spray drones in the U.S. fell by 60 percent in 2025, largely because of U.S. Customs and Border Protection interventions in DJI shipments, U.S. agricultural news website AgFunderNews reported.

Eric Ringer, president of the American Spray Drone Coalition, described the industry as "very much in flux," with some U.S. spray drone operators buying up any existing DJI models that are not enmeshed in the ban.

The performance advantage of Chinese drones is a major reason many American users would rather continue using older Chinese models than switch to domestic alternatives.

Last year, the U.S. Department of Homeland Security's National Urban Security Technology Laboratory evaluated drones in Manhattan, New York City. As the surrounding highrises interfered with control signals, three drones were unable to fly reliably: one could not determine its position, another failed to take off, and a third temporarily lost contact.

By contrast, the two DJI drones tested at the same time operated normally, according to a report by U.S. drone industry news outlet DroneXL.

However, the U.S. government's test report mentioned only the scores of the American drones while deliberately concealing the test results of the Chinese drones. The U.S. government appears unwilling to let the public fully understand the performance advantages of Chinese drones, nor does it want to face the reality of its own products lagging behind.

However, if police officers and firefighters in New York are forced to use substandard American drones to carry out missions in the densely built and heavily populated Manhattan, it has the potential of creating enormous public safety risks.

At present, drone technology is still undergoing iterative development. Restrictions on Chinese drones will prevent the American public and various institutions from using the latest Chinese drone products, effectively creating an artificial technological divide — and this time, it is the U.S. that will be losing.

Reports indicate that DJI is about to launch a new generation of drones and drone stations that can quickly swap batteries without waiting for recharging. DroneXL lamented in its report that this clearly demonstrates the losses caused to the U.S. by the "Covered List," as law enforcement agencies in other countries no longer have to endure a 27-minute charging time.

As for the so-called security issues of Chinese drones that the U.S. has repeatedly hyped, facts have proven them to be a fabricated pretext for trying to suppress China's related industries and engaging in trade protectionism. From October last year to March this year, American cybersecurity firm OnDefend conducted an independent security review of multiple DJI drone models. The results found no backdoors, no data flowing out of the U.S., and no viable network hijacking pathways.

Drones are becoming increasingly integrated into economic development, public safety, urban governance, agricultural production and everyday life. Restricting Chinese drones will not serve as a "protective shield" for the development of the U.S. drone industry. Instead, it will create a range of unnecessary problems across different applications.

The U.S. government should listen to drone users across industries. Persisting with its current course could ultimately result in even greater losses.
