title: China’s Antarctic marine protected area has a Soviet name, with more Russian fingerprints emerging
summary: Alongside Russia, China has spent some 15 years thwarting most proposed marine protected areas (MPAs) in Antarctica. Now a dossier attributed to Beijing wants to forge its own in the Soviet-named “Cosmonauts Sea”, under a protection model i
content:
Alongside Russia, China has spent some 15 years thwarting most proposed marine protected areas (MPAs) in Antarctica. Now a dossier attributed to Beijing wants to forge its own in the Soviet-named “Cosmonauts Sea”, under a protection model it is trying to embed in the Southern Ocean’s governing rules. Credited to the “delegation of China”, the 105-page dossier comprises three documents: the marine reserve pitch; the science motivation backing it; and a proposal seeking to reorder Antarctica’s official MPA rule book. The documents note being “submitted” to the premier MPA and fisheries talks on 3 and 4 September - reflecting the annual deadline for the negotiations now underway behind closed doors in Hobart, Tasmania. A Daily Maverick examination of the Commission for the Conservation of Antarctic Marine Living Resources’ (CCAMLR) negotiating records has linked key elements of the Beijing-credited rule changes to technical hurdles repeatedly advanced by Moscow. These hurdles feature ever-tighter data demands and other criteria that could further retard four long-delayed MPA proposals. There is a catch: the “127,000km²” Cosmonauts Sea MPA trumpets krill closures where - anti-fishing advocates say - no krill is actually being caught. Unless each of the consensus-based Commission’s current 27 members renewed or amended it - or adopted a replacement - the mooted MPA would expire after just 20 years. Based on the Cosmonauts Sea proposal, a sole member could veto the renewal of an entire MPA allowing it to sink without a vote to abolish it. One document in the dossier aims to delete foundational conservation objectives, including climate resilience, from the MPA rule book - known as “Conservation Measure 91-04”. All Commission states, including fellow BRICS member South Africa, would first have to agree before the proposed rules could have any effect. Dr Matthew Savoca, a Stanford University research associate with a special interest in the impacts of krill fishing, told Daily Maverick that he could not comment on the documents as he had not seen them. But he said he “would ask that China start” by finally approving another MPA proposal “covering portions of the Antarctic Peninsula and South Orkney Islands”, which has been “on the table in various forms for a decade”. Savoca said: “Once that is in place, we can move on to other regions; there’s no shortage of spectacular and important places in Antarctica that need safeguarding.”
(Photo: Youenn Kerdavid / Sea Shepherd Global)

](https://cdn.dailymaverick.co.za/i/O2wZY_nLseva9xEg9LVZnYsrjuw=/200x100/smart/filters:strip_exif()/file/attachments/orphans/ME-Tiara-ChinaMPAFollowUpII5_256530.jpg) A whale surfaces near the krill vessel Antarctic Endeavour in the Southern Ocean, 26 January 2024. (Photo: Youenn Kerdavid / Sea Shepherd Global) ### **Russia’s earlier proposals** In 2022, Moscow proposed amending the Commission’s MPA rule book, [first adopted in 2011](https://cm.ccamlr.org/sites/default/files/2024-11/91-04-2011.pdf). Similar to the latest Cosmonauts Sea campaign of 2026, the Russian delegation aimed to impose new criteria on MPA proposals - including the East Antarctic MPA advanced by Australia, the EU and France back in 2012. Paragraphs “5.60” to “5.63” of the Commission’s [2022 annual meeting report](https://meetings.ccamlr.org/system/files/meeting-reports/e-cc-41-rep.pdf) record the Moscow-led propositions as well as Beijing’s response. Moscow’s ideas, Beijing said, “could contribute to a roadmap for MPA establishment”. [At the Commission’s October 2023 meeting](https://meetings.ccamlr.org/system/files/meeting-reports/e-cc-42-rep_2.pdf) in Hobart, paragraphs 5.30 to 5.33 show that the Russian diplomats again pursued sweeping changes to the rule book - insisting on suspending MPA talks until their demands had been met. [At the special meeting](https://meetings.ccamlr.org/system/files/meeting-reports/e-cc-sm-iii-report.pdf) convened in Santiago a few months before, the delegation of China had complained that the two approved MPAs - the 2009 South Orkney and 2016 Ross Sea marine parks - were “not demonstrably contributing to the mitigation and adaptation to climate change impacts since their establishment many years ago”. “Most” Commission members hit back, saying the “precautionary approach requires it to act despite uncertainties and knowledge gaps”. They said Russian attempts to rewrite the rules “presented unachievable barriers to adopting MPAs”. “Many” members would continue the battle in Hobart that same year. “The best available science,” they argued, “is sufficient to establish MPAs.” They described the rule book as “fit for purpose” and compared the Russian approach to “constraints and inconsistencies” that would pile on “more obstacles to the adoption of MPAs”. Given this heated negotiating record, Moscow’s proposals failed to secure consensus. The overlaps between Moscow’s earlier demands and Beijing’s latest proposals help explain why. Where, in 2022 and 2023, the Russian delegation had demanded “sufficient” evidence as a higher standard for “best available science”, the 2026 proposed rules call for “multi-year systematic oceanographic surveys” - without saying how many years would be “multi”. Where Moscow demanded a “mandatory” checklist, the proposed rules from the Chinese delegation envisage a “standardised procedure”. And where Moscow called for talks to be suspended until the rules were rewritten, the Chinese delegation has devised its own obstacle course: rewrite the rules, revise existing proposals, then consider approving them. Neither Beijing nor Moscow has backed any other MPA since agreeing to the 2 million km 2 Ross Sea MPA a decade ago. If ever approved, the four lagging South American and Europe-led MPA proposals would make up about 4.5 million km 2 - a Southern Ocean area larger than the EU. The East Antarctic MPA would span about 1 million km 2 – about eight times the size of the Cosmonauts’ Greece-sized pitch, which carries the historic name of a Soviet Sea [that has not been adopted](https://iho.int/uploads/user/pubs/standards/s-23/S-23_Ed3_1953_EN.pdf) by the International Hydrographic Organisation. ### **A “fresh” approach? What “some” members actually backed** In Beijing’s telling, “some” members have described its ongoing campaign for a so-called “step-by-step” approach as a “fresh outlook”. China’s delegation recalls this narrative in the proposed rule-book changes, arguing each step is designed to build out details that would end the fish fight and nail the consensus member states long for. As shown by [the minutes of the 2024 talks](https://meetings.ccamlr.org/system/files/meeting-reports/e-cc-43-rep.pdf), the delegation’s account is correct. But in CCAMLR-speak, “some members” are not the same as “many” or even “most”. Indeed, the envoys from South Africa - a major krill gateway through the port of Cape Town - [seemed to feel anything but fresh](https://meetings.ccamlr.org/system/files/meeting-reports/e-cc-44-rep.pdf) at the 2025 talks. Flagging a “continued deadlock” on how to combat concentrating fishing, they suggested they could smell something rotten - and that it was undermining the Commission’s “credibility”. A longtime supporter of the four MPA proposals, Pretoria stressed it was “optimistic that the members will continue to engage in insatiable efforts on the margin to move CCAMLR [to] overcome these untenable circumstances”. It urged the Commission to “continue progress as a global leader in conservation and fisheries management”. A Weddell seal lies in the Antarctic sun. (Photo: iStock) ### **China’s guiding principle: “Understanding, protection and use of Antarctica”** Daily Maverick asked Professor Nengye Liu, a specialist in China’s engagement with the Antarctic Treaty System (ATS), to explain Beijing’s approach to MPAs. “The guiding principle of China’s Antarctic activities is understanding, protection and use of Antarctica. This has been repeatedly mentioned by senior Chinese officials and is also going to be integrated into China’s forthcoming Antarctic Activities and Environmental Protection Law,” said Liu, who is based at Singapore Management University’s Yong Pung How School of Law. Liu observed that “China’s latest Cosmonauts Sea MPA proposal to CCAMLR, which may be seen as a surprise move at first glance, actually follows and operationalises the guiding principle. “There is a Chinese saying: ‘All variations stem from the same underlying principle - 万变不离其宗 - that captures this move well. The MPA as a last resort, seasonal protection, limited tenure, these all clearly reflect the Chinese government’s belief about what an MPA should look like and where exactly to draw the line between protection and use of Antarctica in the foreseeable future.” Liu saw diplomatic advantages in the initiative. “From a diplomatic point of view, this is a smart move. It not only helps shift China’s negative image in Western media as a rising power who is obstructing marine conservation, but also enhances China’s bargaining power in CCAMLR meetings.”
(Photo: Alice Bacou / Sea Shepherd Global)](https://cdn.dailymaverick.co.za/i/V5LghIzJ4BP9OP9vgVHG4o40zCY=/200x100/smart/filters:strip_exif()/file/attachments/orphans/ME-Tiara-ChinaMPAFollowUpII4_794795.jpg) An Adélie penguin stands on Antarctic ice, with a krill fishing vessel looming in the mist behind it, 5 April 2025. (Photo: Alice Bacou / Sea Shepherd Global) ### **A ‘very small’ protected area with an expiry date** Karen Scott, an ATS specialist and law professor at the University of Canterbury, argued that time limits were not fresh MPA concepts. For instance, the Ross Sea MPA has a 35-year duration and requires active renewal. Limited krill and toothfish harvesting is permitted. “All of these compromises have been subject to critique with questions being asked as to whether they are genuinely marine protected areas,” said Professor Scott. “The fact that they have occurred before does not mean that we want to replicate them again and the very small area apparently proposed by China also raises significant questions,” added Scott, who could not comment on the documents as she had not reviewed them. “China has argued over the last few years that CCAMLR needs to amend the MPA framework within which proposals are developed although its papers proposing amendments have yet to gain traction. It will be interesting to see how this proposal sits with the existing CCAMLR MPA framework or whether it departs from previously agreed principles.” ### **Climate objectives marked for deletion** [As first reported by Daily Maverick](https://antarcticinsight.com/exclusive-china-proposes-its-own-antarctic-marine-protected-area-in-a-soviet-named-sea/), Beijing’s amendments would strike two conservation objectives from the MPA rule book: “The protection of features critical to the function of local ecosystems” and “the protection of areas to maintain resilience or the ability to adapt to the effects of climate change”. The rule book’s sole remaining climate change reference would no longer be an objective. It would merely “recognise” that MPAs “maintain the ability to adapt in the face of climate change”, which contradicts China’s earlier argument. Dr Ally Kristan, a research associate at Duke University Marine Lab, said that krill vessels spend “the vast majority of active fishing hours in penguin foraging ranges during both the summer and winter’. Kristan pointed to “[collapsing penguin colonies](https://www.smithsonianmag.com/smart-news/one-of-the-worlds-largest-chinstrap-penguin-colonies-is-shrinking-fast-180989676/)” and plummeting fur seal populations as krill became less available during Antarctic warming: “It’s difficult scientifically to disentangle the impacts of climate change versus fisheries, but MPAs with continuous, year-round commercial fishing prohibitions are one of the

# Chinese man who promoted surrogacy for same-sex couples deported

10/23/2026 04:24 PM

[](jsvscript:)[](jsvscript:)[](javascript:void(0))[Listen](javascript:)

[Link](javascript:)[Whatsapp](javascript:)[Reddit](javascript:)[Line](javascript:)[Email](javascript:)

To activate the text-to-speech service, please first agree to the privacy policy below.

Photo courtesy of local authorities

Kaohsiung, Oct. 23 (CNA) A Chinese influencer who promoted surrogacy-related services for same-sex couples has been deported and fined NT$200,000 (US$6,100), the Kaohsiung City government said Friday.

According to the city's health bureau, the influencer posted videos promoting fan meetups in Taiwan and providing information on how to have a child through assisted reproduction.

The bureau said the man violated Taiwan's Medical Care Act, which prohibits entities other than medical institutions from advertising medical services. The man was neither a licensed medical institution nor a physician, it added.

Given his large social media following and wide reach, the fine was increased to NT$200,000 in accordance with the law, the bureau said.

The bureau also said Taiwan's Assisted Reproduction Act stipulates requirements for medical providers, eligible recipients and procedures, while commercial surrogacy is not currently permitted.

It urged people seeking fertility services to consult qualified medical institutions and physicians.

Meanwhile, the National Immigration Agency ordered the man, who was caught in Kaohsiung on Thursday, to be deported, saying he had entered Taiwan on a tourist visa but engaged in activities inconsistent with the purpose of his visit, in violation of regulations governing mainland Chinese visitors.

The man, known as "Berlinsun" on social media, has more than one million followers on Instagram and Douyin.

According to local media, he and his partner live in Malaysia and have shared their experience of having children through egg donation and surrogacy on social media.

(By Lin Chiao-lien and Lee Hsin-Yin)

title: Hong Kong government unveils first phase of Lan Kwai Fong beautification
zh_title: 香港政府公布兰桂坊美化工程第一阶段
summary: 香港 香港政府已完成兰桂坊美化工程的第一阶段，其中包括灯光艺术、43 米长的壁画和升级的铺路。该项目旨在通过公私合作振兴夜生活区并吸引更多游客。 [![图片 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk) 作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编 2026 年 10 月 23 日 15:00 香港时间 · 10 月 23 日更新， 15:19 · 阅读2分钟 图片：[香港特区政府新闻公报](https://www.info.gov.hk/gia/general/202610/23/P
content:
香港
香港政府已经完成了兰桂坊美化工程的第一阶段，其中包括灯光艺术、43米长的壁画和升级的铺路。该项目旨在通过公私合作振兴夜生活区并吸引更多游客。

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

2026 年 10 月 23 日 15:00 香港时间 · 更新于 10 月 23 日 15:19 · 阅读时间 2 分钟

 图片：[香港特区政府新闻公报](https://www.info.gov.hk/gia/general/202610/23/P2026102300462.htm)

香港政府已经完成了兰桂坊美化工程的第一阶段，兰桂坊是该市标志性的夜生活和餐饮区。该项目于 2026 年 10 月 23 日宣布，包括灯光艺术展示、大型壁画和升级铺装，以增强该地区的吸引力并吸引更多游客。

结合投影技术和灯光效果的灯光艺术秀将于周五、周六、周日和公众假期晚上 7 点至凌晨 2 点进行。这场三分钟的表演在德己立街的石墙和附近的人行道上上演，每 10 分钟重复一次。首次亮相的主题是万圣节，主题会根据不同的节日和活动而变化。
兰桂坊协会委托街头艺术团队All in One在德己立街旁的挡土墙上创作一幅43米长的壁画，一直延伸至永乐里。这幅壁画的标题是“兰桂坊的过去和现在的转变”，其中包含一个二维码，供游客更多地了解该地区。该协会还将在10月24日至31日举办万圣节活动，邀请游客穿着服装欣赏这些装置。

发展局发言人表示：“这只是兰桂坊升级至2.0版本的起点。”该局将美化兰桂坊径附近的垃圾收集站及兰桂坊休息区，并于2027年中开始重修核心区的剩余道路。 2027年第一季，第二阶段将展开“场所营造”顾问研究，研究范围将涵盖威灵顿街、宝华街及砵典乍街等周边街道。计划包括升级街道设施、改善行人标志以及与砵典乍街产生协同效应。

与此同时，该局支持在干诺道中与毕打街交界处进行大型装置。业主出资扩阔毕打街的人行道，以改善行人流量。该局表示，这些努力体现了政府在2026年施政报告中概述的振兴香港第一个核心商业区中环的承诺。

Hong Kong
The Hong Kong government has completed the first phase of a beautification project for Lan Kwai Fong, featuring light art, a 43-metre mural, and upgraded paving. The project aims to revitalise the nightlife district and attract more visitors through public-private collaboration.

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

23 Oct 2026 at 15:00 HKT · updated 23 Oct, 15:19 · 2 min read

 Image: [香港特區政府新聞公報](https://www.info.gov.hk/gia/general/202610/23/P2026102300462.htm)

The Hong Kong government has completed the first phase of a beautification project for Lan Kwai Fong, the city's iconic nightlife and dining district. Announced on 23 October 2026, the project includes light art displays, a large-scale mural, and upgraded paving to enhance the area's appeal and attract more visitors.

A light art show combining projection technology and lighting effects will run on Fridays, Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays from 7pm to 2am. The three-minute show, staged on a stone wall and nearby pavement at D'Aguilar Street, will be repeated every 10 minutes. The debut theme is Halloween, with themes to change for different festivals and events.

The Lan Kwai Fong Association commissioned street art team All in One to create a 43-metre mural on a retaining wall beside D'Aguilar Street, extending to Wing Lo Lane. Titled “Lan Kwai Fong's Past and Present Transformation”, the mural will include a QR code for visitors to learn more about the district. The association will also hold Halloween events on 24 and 31 October, inviting visitors to enjoy the installations in costume.

A spokesman for the Development Bureau said: “This is only the starting point for upgrading Lan Kwai Fong to version 2.0.” The bureau will beautify the refuse collection station near Lan Kwai Fong Path and Lan Kwai Fong Sitting Area, and begin repaving remaining roads in the core area by mid-2027. In the first quarter of 2027, it will launch a “placemaking” consultancy study for the second phase, which will cover surrounding streets such as Wellington Street, Po Wah Street and Pottinger Street. Plans include upgrading street furniture, improving pedestrian signage, and creating synergy with Pottinger Street.

Meanwhile, the bureau has supported a large installation at the junction of Connaught Road Central and Pedder Street. The building owner has funded widening of the pavement on Pedder Street to improve pedestrian flow. The bureau said these efforts demonstrate the government's commitment, as outlined in the 2026 Policy Address, to rejuvenate Central, Hong Kong's first core business district.

## 对于台湾市长来说，“台风休息日”是一次重大的政治考验

一位专家表示，在选举年，市长宣布因台风停工和停课的可能性会增加 31%。

听

· 5:21 分钟

周四，当台风占比接近该地区时，巨浪袭击了台湾北部基隆的海岸。图片来源：Chiang Ying-Ying/Associated Press

2026 年 10 月 22 日

在台湾，台风不仅仅是造成洪水和破坏的热带风暴。他们可能会因为人们意想不到的原因而决定市长连任的机会。

每年夏季和秋季期间，这个亚热带岛屿都会遭受几次飓风袭击，市县市长必须决定是否下令“台风休息日”，届时政府办公室、学校和大多数企业将关闭。
台湾一直在为台风“占比”做好准备，它一度是超强台风，也是[2026 年最强风暴](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/21/weather/super-typhoon-champi-strongest-storm-year.html)。周四，台北市市长蒋万安宣布周五为台风日，并敦促居民小心。预计风暴将经过台湾东北部，带来大雨和时速141英里的风。

对于许多人来说，这一决定并不令人意外，尤其是因为天气预报。蒋介石将在 11 月底面临连任，而台风天很受居民欢迎，他们经常在家里度过这一天。如果风暴强度比预期弱，许多人就会去购物、看电影或唱卡拉 OK。 （蒋介石是国民党党员，他与执政的民进党的受欢迎的立法委员沉普马的竞争十分激烈。）

周五，台湾主岛几乎所有市县都已停工停课。

由于台风在台湾日常生活中司空见惯，因此是否宣布台风日等决定对选民来说很重要。据当地出版物《新闻镜头》报道，2001 年至 2023 年间，台北有 [40 个台风假](https://www.thenewslens.com/article/190034)，平均每年几乎两天。其他城市，例如经常遭受暴风雨袭击的东北沿海宜兰市，在此期间放假45天。
研究台风天选举政治的内华达大学副教授奥斯汀·王 (Austin Wang) 表示，在选举年，市长宣布停工和停课的可能性会增加 31%。

他说，与其他可能需要数月或数年评估的政策不同，一两天内就可以清楚官员是否做出了正确的决定。例如，如果宣布台风日并且风暴非常严重，那么官员就会做出正确的决定。事实上，市长办公室独自决定是否休息，这也意味着该决定完全由市长负责。

“对于人们来说，这是一个非常简单的标准来评价现任者的工作做得好还是不好，”王先生说。他说，谈到连任时，“人们会记住市长的决定是正确还是错误。”

## For Taiwan’s Mayors, a ‘Typhoon Day Off’ Is a Major Political Test

One expert said the likelihood that a mayor announces closure of work and school because of a typhoon increases 31 percent during an election year.

Listen

· 5:21 min

A high wave hitting the shore in Keelung, northern Taiwan, on Thursday, as Typhoon Champi approached the area.Credit...Chiang Ying-Ying/Associated Press

Oct. 22, 2026

In Taiwan, typhoons are not just tropical storms that cause flooding and damage. They can make or break a mayor’s chance at re-election for reasons one might not expect.

Several times a year between summer and fall, when the subtropical island is hit by cyclones, city and county mayors must decide whether to order a “typhoon day off,” when government offices, schools and most businesses will close.

Taiwan has been bracing for Typhoon Champi, which was at one point a super typhoon and the [strongest storm of 2026](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/21/weather/super-typhoon-champi-strongest-storm-year.html). On Thursday, the mayor of Taipei, Chiang Wan-an, called a typhoon day off for Friday, and urged residents to be careful. The storm is expected to pass the northeastern part of Taiwan, bringing heavy rain and winds of 141 miles per hour.

The decision did not come as a surprise to many, not least because of the weather forecast. Mr. Chiang faces re-election in late November, and typhoon days are popular with residents, who often spend the day at home. If the storm turns out to be weaker than forecast, many go shopping, to the movies or to sing karaoke. (Mr. Chiang, a member of the Nationalist Party, also called the Kuomintang, is in a close race with Puma Shen, a popular legislator from the governing Democratic Progressive Party.)

Almost all cities and counties across Taiwan’s main island had suspended work and class on Friday.

Because typhoons are such a common part of daily life in Taiwan, decisions like whether or not to call a typhoon day matter to voters. Between 2001 and 2023, Taipei had [40 typhoon days off](https://www.thenewslens.com/article/190034), an average of almost two days a year, according to The News Lens, a local publication. Other cities like Yilan on the northeastern coast, which is often hit badly by storms, had 45 days off in that period.

According to Austin Wang, an associate professor at the University of Nevada who has studied the electoral politics of typhoon days, the likelihood that a mayor announces closure of work and school increases 31 percent during an election year.

Unlike other policies that can take months or years to evaluate, he said, it is clear within a day or two whether an official made the correct call. For instance, if a typhoon day is called and the storm turns out to be severe, the official made the right decision. The fact that the mayor’s office alone determines whether to call a day off also means that the decision is entirely the mayor’s responsibility.

“It is a very easy criteria for people to evaluate whether their incumbent was doing a good job or a bad job,” Mr. Wang said. When it comes to re-election, he said, “people will remember if the mayor made the right or wrong decision.”

Tickets for many high-speed trains leaving Taipei during working hours on Friday were fully or almost fully booked on Thursday. Supermarkets stocked extra supplies of water, produce and instant noodles, a common staple during typhoons.

On social media, residents discussed their plans to spend the four-day weekend binge watching television shows and sleeping. (Monday is a public holiday in Taiwan.) Earlier in the day, residents left comments on Mr. Chiang’s Facebook page, asking him to announce a day off.

Despite the popularity of such days, unnecessarily calling one can come back to haunt a candidate. Business groups often oppose typhoon days off because of the cost to companies, most of which still pay their employees for the day. Taiwan’s stock market also closes for the day if work and school are suspended in Taipei.

In July, when Typhoon Bavi approached Taiwan, Mr. Chiang ordered a day off on a Friday for residents to prepare for the storm’s arrival on the weekend. Commentators and his political rivals accused him of inventing the concept of a “typhoon preparation day” just to pander to voters.

But not calling one quickly enough may be even worse. When Typhoon Mikra passed over central Taiwan in June, the mayors of the city of Hsinchu and the county of Hsinchu, home to Taiwan’s largest semiconductor companies, were criticized for not issuing a typhoon day off. The next day, as the storm arrived, the county mayor, Yang Wenke, issued an apology and announced the suspension of work and school. That storm left two people dead.

Lai Ching-te, the president of Taiwan, has been both praised and derided for his weather-related decisions. In 2012, when Typhoon Tembin approached the southern city of Tainan, Mr. Lai, then that city’s mayor, decided it would be business as usual.

When the storm proved to be light, he earned the nickname “God Lai.”

But the next year, when once again he resisted pressure to declare a day off during another typhoon, the storm caused severe flooding in his city. He issued a public apology.

[Lily Kuo](https://www.nytimes.com/by/lily-kuo)is a China correspondent for The Times, based in Taipei.

[Pei-Lin Wu](https://www.nytimes.com/by/pei-lin-wu) is a reporter and researcher covering Taiwan and China for The Times.

title: Burkina Faso Restores Death Penalty
summary: _Chilling Message to Junta Critics Amid Sweeping Crackdowns_ [Burkina Faso](https://www.hrw.org/africa/burkina-faso)'s unelected [parliament](https://www.assembleenationale.bf/) has unanimously [adopted](https://www.rfi.fr/fr/afrique/202610
content:
_Chilling Message to Junta Critics Amid Sweeping Crackdowns_

[Burkina Faso](https://www.hrw.org/africa/burkina-faso)'s unelected [parliament](https://www.assembleenationale.bf/) has unanimously [adopted](https://www.rfi.fr/fr/afrique/20261021-burkina-faso-la-junte-au-pouvoir-r%C3%A9tablit-la-peine-de-mort) a new penal code that restores the death penalty for high treason, terrorism, acts of espionage, parricide and importation of expired or prohibited products. The country had [abolished](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2018/06/burkina-faso-abolition-of-death-penalty-a-hardwon-victory/) the death penalty for ordinary crimes in 2018 while its last known judicial execution [took place](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/11/11/burkina-faso-plans-reinstate-death-penalty) in 1988.

Reinstating capital punishment sends a chilling message to critics of the military junta and risks becoming another tool to suppress dissent. Since the [September 2022 military coup](https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-63098217), Burkina Faso's junta has steadily dismantled civic and political rights. Authorities have [banned media outlets](https://www.hrw.org/news/2026/05/06/burkina-fasos-junta-escalates-attack-on-information), suspended [unions](https://www.hrw.org/news/2026/05/27/burkina-fasos-largest-student-union-suspended-for-criticizing-junta) and [civil society organizations](https://www.hrw.org/news/2026/04/20/burkina-faso-crackdown-on-civil-society), [abolished multiparty politics](https://www.hrw.org/news/2026/02/05/burkina-fasos-junta-pulls-the-plug-on-political-life), and subjected critics to arbitrary detention, [enforced disappearances](https://www.hrw.org/news/2026/06/22/burkina-faso-prominent-journalist-forcibly-disappeared-2-years-on), [unlawful conscription](https://www.hrw.org/news/2025/07/31/burkina-faso-releases-conscripted-journalists-activist), and [torture](https://www.hrw.org/report/2026/04/02/none-can-run-away/war-crimes-and-crimes-against-humanity-in-burkina-faso-by-all#21).

Keep up with the latest headlines on [WhatsApp](https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaIdDi8Bqbr263erhw1K) | [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/allafrica/)

Justice Minister Edasso Rodrigue Bayala [defended](https://www.aib.media/?p=171531) the decision to reinstate the death penalty as a necessary measure to combat terrorism. He said that armed groups exploited the previous law's leniency by promising new recruits they would face no more than life imprisonment if convicted of terrorist acts.

Human Rights Watch opposes all capital punishment because of its inherent cruelty. The unfairness of death sentences in Burkina Faso would be exacerbated by the country's [ill-equipped](https://www.hrw.org/report/2026/04/02/none-can-run-away/war-crimes-and-crimes-against-humanity-in-burkina-faso-by-all#21) justice system. All terrorism-related cases are handled by the Specialized Judicial Unit Against Terrorism-Related Crimes, established in 2017. Human Rights Watch [documented](https://www.hrw.org/report/2026/04/02/none-can-run-away/war-crimes-and-crimes-against-humanity-in-burkina-faso-by-all) in April the special court's slow investigations and serious procedural failures that undermine defendants' fair trial rights.

A former terrorism court judge once [explained to me](https://www.hrw.org/report/2026/04/02/none-can-run-away/war-crimes-and-crimes-against-humanity-in-burkina-faso-by-all#21) that judges sometimes kept suspects in detention despite insufficient evidence, fearing the military might summarily execute them if released. He described the dilemma as "better to violate the right to liberty in order to preserve the right to life." With the death penalty's return, even that grim calculation may no longer hold.

Reversing course on the death penalty runs counter to a broader international movement toward abolition. The [United Nations General Assembly](https://www.ohchr.org/en/topic/death-penalty/international-framework) and the [African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights](https://achpr.au.int/index.php/en/adopted-resolutions/544-resolution-death-penalty-and-prohibition-torture-and-cruel) have [urged](https://www.ohchr.org/en/topic/death-penalty/international-framework) states to establish moratoriums on executions, narrow the scope of capital punishment, and progressively reduce the number of offenses punishable by death with a view to its eventual abolition.

Restoring capital punishment will not resolve Burkina Faso's security crisis. In a system already plagued by serious due process failures, the death penalty merely heightens the risk of irreversible injustice.

_[Ilaria Allegrozzi](https://www.hrw.org/about/people/ilaria-allegrozzi), Senior Sahel Researcher_

# BASEBALL/Chiang Kun-yu wins 7th straight CPBL Gold Glove

10/22/2026 07:23 PM

[](jsvscript:)[](jsvscript:)[](javascript:void(0))[Listen](javascript:)

To activate the text-to-speech service, please first agree to the privacy policy below.

202CTBC Brothers shortstop Chiang Kun-yu. CNA photo Oct. 21, 2026

Taipei, Oct. 22 (CNA) CTBC Brothers shortstop Chiang Kun-yu (江坤宇) won his seventh consecutive Gold Glove on Thursday as Taiwan's Chinese Professional Baseball League (CPBL) announced its annual defensive awards.

Chiang, who has won the award every year since 2020, extended the league record for consecutive Gold Gloves by an infielder. His teammate Sung Sheng-jui (宋晟睿) was among this year's first-time winners.

Chiang committed four errors in 425 fielding chances, recording 180 putouts, 241 assists and 57 double plays. His .991 fielding percentage was up from .990 last year.

Wei Chuan Dragons second baseman Li Kai-wei (李凱威) won his fifth straight Gold Glove after making just one error in 464 chances. Sung won his first outfield award with a .996 fielding percentage.

Uni-President 7-Eleven Lions outfielder Chen Chieh-hsien (陳傑憲) and Brothers outfielder Yueh Cheng-hua (岳政華) missed out, ending streaks of four and two straight awards, respectively.

The other outfield winners were Wei Chuan's Kuo Tian-shin (郭天信), who won his fifth career award, and the TSG Hawks' Chen Wun-jie (陳文杰), whose error-free season earned him his third.

Rounding out the Gold Glove lineup were Uni-Lions pitcher Brock Dykxhoorn, Rakuten Monkeys catcher Sung Jia-xiang (宋嘉翔), Fubon Guardians first baseman Fan Kuo-chen (范國宸) and Wei Chuan third baseman Liu Ji-hong (劉基鴻).

The announcements followed Monday's unveiling of the CPBL's 2026 all-league team, known as the "Best Nine," along with a separate award for best designated hitter.

Wei Chuan's John Gant was selected at pitcher after leading the league with a 1.49 ERA and 136 strikeouts over 133 1/3 innings.

The other selections were Uni-Lions catcher Chen Chung-yu (陳重羽), Fubon first baseman Fan and second baseman Lin Ze-bin (林澤彬), Uni-Lions third baseman Pan Chieh-kai (潘傑楷), and Wei Chuan shortstop Chang Cheng-yu (張政禹).

Chen Chieh-hsien, Rakuten's Chen Chen-wei (陳晨威) and Kuo filled the outfield positions.

TSG's Steven Moya won his third straight best designated hitter award after leading the league with 126 hits, 20 home runs and 90 RBIs.

Both sets of awards were decided by 41 voters, including three representatives from the league's statistics department.

The awards ceremony will be held Nov. 2 at the Taipei Marriott Hotel.

(By Chao Yen-hsiang)

# 西藏发生里氏 7.0 级地震，为 2024 年 1 月以来中国最强地震
周四晚上，西藏发生了 7.0 级地震，这是自 2024 年 1 月以来中国发生的最强地震，造成至少两人受伤，那曲震中附近的一些房屋出现裂缝。

晚上10点33分左右，中国西南部西藏地区发生7.0级地震。周四（1433 GMT），中国地震台网中心（CENC）表示。国家广播公司称，地方当局在震中附近的一个村庄发现至少两人受伤，距离震中最近的村庄的一些房屋出现裂缝。此次地震是自 2024 年 1 月以来中国遭遇的最强烈地震。

震中位于西藏北部那曲地区一个人烟稀少的高海拔县城，震中位于西藏北部那曲地区一个人口稀少的高海拔县。

# Magnitude 7.0 earthquake strikes Tibet, strongest in China since January 2024

A magnitude 7.0 earthquake struck Tibet on Thursday evening, the strongest in China since January 2024, with at least two injured and some houses cracked near the epicentre in Nagqu.

[![Image 4: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

 By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

 22 Oct 2026 at 23:13 HKT · 1 min read

A magnitude 7.0 earthquake struck China's southwestern region of Tibet at around 10:33 p.m. (1433 GMT) on Thursday, the China Earthquake Networks Center (CENC) said. Local authorities have found at least two people injured in a village near the epicentre, with some houses in villages closest to the epicentre showing cracks, the state broadcaster said. The quake is the strongest to hit China since January 2024.

The epicentre was in a sparsely populated, high-altitude county in Nagqu, northern Tibet, at a depth of 10 km (6.2 miles). The average elevation within 5 km of the epicentre is about 4,864 metres (15,960 feet), CENC data showed.

Videos released by local officially run media showed people leaving their homes and seeking shelter outside or in their cars parked on the street. One resident reported being awakened by the strong quake and heard the house squeaking in the tremor.

The quake was clearly felt in the local area, CENC said. The epicentre was around 400 km from the Tibetan capital of Lhasa. Local fire and rescue teams have mobilised and are heading to the affected region, state media said.

A string of smaller tremors of around magnitude 3 and 4 have been recorded in surrounding regions following the magnitude 7 quake, CENC data showed. In 2010, a magnitude 7.1 tremor struck Yushu in neighbouring Qinghai province, killing at least 2,698 people and leaving nearly 300 people missing.

title: Over half blame CCP for undermining cross-strait peace: MAC poll - Focus Taiwan
zh_title: MAC民意调查：过半数人指责中共破坏两岸和平 - 聚焦台湾
summary: 中新社台北10月22日电 陆委会周四表示，超过一半的受访者认为中国共产党正在破坏台海和平，这一比例比5月份的类似民意调查增加了近5个百分点。调查发现，52.3%的受访者将责任归咎于中共，高于5月份的47.4%，而28.5%的受访者认为台湾和中共都有责任，低于33.3%。与此同时，6%的人将责任归咎于台湾，而此前这一比例为7.9%，而13.2%的人表示他们不知道或没有任何意见
content:
中新社台北10月22日电 陆委会周四表示，超过一半的受访者认为中国共产党正在破坏台海和平，这一比例比5月份的类似民意调查增加了近5个百分点。

调查发现，52.3%的受访者将责任归咎于中共，高于5月份的47.4%，而28.5%的受访者认为台湾和中共都有责任，低于33.3%。

与此同时，6%的人将责任归咎于台湾，而此前这一比例为7.9%；13.2%的人表示不知道或没有意见，高于此前的11.3%。

周四在台北发布调查结果的例行新闻发布会上，被问及这些变化时，陆委会副主任兼发言人梁文杰指出，过去五个月里，中国海警、科考船和海上民兵船只在台湾以东海域的活动有所增加。

自六月以来，中国加强了台湾东部海域的海警巡逻，八月还在该地区发现了一艘疑似中国海上民兵船只。

梁引述了最近揭露的涉嫌中国在台湾进行跨国镇压的案件。

最近的案件包括 7 月份在台中袭击台湾政治评论员矢板明夫的事件，一名香港帮派成员于本月初被起诉。检察官表示，这次袭击的目的是恐吓矢板。
另一起案件涉及喜剧演员黄逸豪，他在九月份涉嫌一场交通事故中受伤。周三，五人因这起事件被起诉，检察官称这起事件与他嘲笑中国国家主席习近平的笑话有关。

梁说：“我认为公众可以感受到谁在破坏和平。”他指出了近5个百分点的增长。

调查还发现，80.6%的人支持增加台湾国防预算，以增强其自卫能力，高于5月份的71.9%。

与此同时，78.8%的人认为中华民国（台湾的官方名称）和中华人民共和国（中国的官方名称）并不从属，这一比例高于5月份的72.6%。

这项调查受陆委会委托，由民意调查公司益普索于10月15日至17日和10月19日通过电话采访台湾20岁及以上的成年人进行。

据 MAC 称，共收集到 1,073 份有效回复，置信度为 95%，误差幅度为正负 2.99 个百分点。

（赖阳光）

结局/AW

【原文 English Original】
Taipei, Oct. 22 (CNA) More than half of respondents to a Mainland Affairs Council (MAC) survey believe the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) is undermining peace across the Taiwan Strait, an increase of nearly 5 percentage points from a similar poll in May, the agency said Thursday.

The survey found that 52.3 percent of respondents blamed the CCP, up from 47.4 percent in May, while 28.5 percent said both Taiwan and the CCP were responsible, down from 33.3 percent.

Meanwhile, 6 percent blamed Taiwan alone, compared with 7.9 percent previously, while 13.2 percent said they did not know or had no opinion, up from 11.3 percent.

Asked about the changes at a regular news briefing in Taipei on Thursday, where the survey results were released, MAC deputy head and spokesperson Liang Wen-chieh (梁文傑) pointed to increased activity by Chinese coast guard, research and maritime militia vessels in waters east of Taiwan over the past five months.

China has stepped up coast guard patrols off eastern Taiwan since June, while a suspected Chinese maritime militia vessel was also spotted in the area in August.

Liang cited recently uncovered cases involving suspected Chinese transnational repression in Taiwan.

Recent cases include a July assault on Taiwan-based political commentator Akio Yaita (矢板明夫) in Taichung, for which a Hong Kong gang member was indicted earlier this month. Prosecutors said the attack was intended to intimidate Yaita.

Another case involved comedian Huang Yi-hao (黃逸豪), who was injured in an allegedly staged traffic accident in September. Five people were indicted Wednesday over the incident, which prosecutors said was linked to jokes he told mocking Chinese President Xi Jinping (習近平).

"I think the public can feel for themselves who is undermining peace," Liang said, noting the nearly 5-percentage-point increase.

The survey also found that 80.6 percent supported increasing Taiwan's defense budget to strengthen its self-defense capabilities, up from 71.9 percent in May.

Meanwhile, 78.8 percent agreed that the Republic of China (Taiwan's official name) and the People's Republic of China (China's official name) are not subordinate to each other, up from 72.6 percent in May.

The survey, commissioned by the MAC, was conducted by polling firm Ipsos from Oct. 15 to 17 and on Oct. 19 through telephone interviews with adults aged 20 and above in Taiwan.

According to the MAC, 1,073 valid responses were collected, with a 95 percent confidence level and a margin of error of plus or minus 2.99 percentage points.

(By Sunny Lai)

# Three dead in fall at TSMC's Kaohsiung plant after steel beam screws snap

Four workers fell from height at TSMC's F22 plant in Kaohsiung on Tuesday evening when connecting plate screws snapped during steel beam installation, killing three and leaving one critically injured. The Southern Taiwan Science Park Bureau halted lifting work and will impose fines pending investiga

[![Image 4: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

 By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

 21 Oct 2026 at 01:24 HKT · updated 21 Oct, 04:25 · 1 min read

Share:

[](https://wa.me/?text=Three%20dead%20in%20fall%20at%20TSMC%27s%20Kaohsiung%20plant%20after%20steel%20beam%20screws%20snap%20https%3A//clb.org.hk/en/business/Three-dead-in-fall-at-TSMC-s-Kaohsiung-plant-after-steel-bea-3725ea "WhatsApp")[](https://t.me/share/url?url=https%3A//clb.org.hk/en/business/Three-dead-in-fall-at-TSMC-s-Kaohsiung-plant-after-steel-bea-3725ea&text=Three%20dead%20in%20fall%20at%20TSMC%27s%20Kaohsiung%20plant%20after%20steel%20beam%20screws%20snap "Telegram")[](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A//clb.org.hk/en/business/Three-dead-in-fall-at-TSMC-s-Kaohsiung-plant-after-steel-bea-3725ea "Facebook")[](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https%3A//clb.org.hk/en/business/Three-dead-in-fall-at-TSMC-s-Kaohsiung-plant-after-steel-bea-3725ea&text=Three%20dead%20in%20fall%20at%20TSMC%27s%20Kaohsiung%20plant%20after%20steel%20beam%20screws%20snap "X")[](https://clb.org.hk/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection# "Email")

Three workers died and one was critically injured after falling from height at [TSMC](https://clb.org.hk/en/business/TSMC-posts-sixth-straight-record-profit-on-AI-chip-demand-cb8bf9)'s F22 plant in the Nanzih campus in Kaohsiung on Tuesday evening during steel beam installation work, authorities said.

The accident occurred at 4.53pm during the P4 new construction project. Four workers employed by contractor Shang Hao Machinery Co Ltd were installing equipment on the outside of the third floor when connecting plate screws suddenly snapped, causing the giant component to lose support and fall, pulling the workers down with it.

Rescuers found three workers without breathing or heartbeat at the scene. The fourth was conscious but seriously injured. All were taken to nearby hospitals, where the three were pronounced dead and the fourth remained in intensive care.

The Southern Taiwan Science Park Bureau said it has ordered a halt to steel beam lifting work at the P4 site and barred anyone from disturbing the scene. It said it would assist victims' families with funeral and compensation matters and would impose work stoppages and fines under the Occupational Safety and Health Act pending investigation.

[TSMC](https://clb.org.hk/en/business/TSMC-posts-record-quarterly-revenue-on-AI-chip-demand-beatin-47f0c8) said its dedicated rescue personnel provided first aid immediately and notified authorities. It said the site falls under the contractor's responsibility, the works have been voluntarily suspended, and its safety team is cooperating with authorities to clarify the cause. It will urge and assist the contractor with follow-up condolences and aftercare for families.

title: Zimbabwe Faces Prolonged Fuel Cost Pressure As Oil Price Relief Unlikely Before 2028
summary: Zimbabwe's fuel-import-dependent economy could remain exposed to international oil market volatility into 2027 after the International Energy Agency (IEA) warned that global energy markets are unlikely to return to normal next year. IEA exe
content:
Zimbabwe's fuel-import-dependent economy could remain exposed to international oil market volatility into 2027 after the International Energy Agency (IEA) warned that global energy markets are unlikely to return to normal next year.

IEA executive director Fatih Birol said there was no credible pathway for oil markets to normalise in 2027 as the conflict in the Middle East continues to disrupt supplies, shipping routes and refining capacity.

Brent crude, the international oil benchmark, was trading above US$111 per barrel on Tuesday, October 20, reflecting renewed concerns over supply disruptions and the potential escalation of the conflict.

The crisis has placed additional pressure on global fuel markets, particularly diesel, as damage to refineries and constrained exports limit the availability of refined petroleum products.

Keep up with the latest headlines on [WhatsApp](https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaIdDi8Bqbr263erhw1K "https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaIdDi8Bqbr263erhw1K") | [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/allafrica/ "https://www.linkedin.com/company/allafrica/")

Birol said the possibility of further disruptions could not be ruled out, warning that overlapping crises in the Middle East could prolong market instability.

The Strait of Hormuz, a critical shipping route for global energy supplies, remains a major concern for oil traders and importers. Before the conflict, approximately one-fifth of global oil and natural gas supplies passed through the waterway.

The International Energy Agency has already coordinated the release of up to 400 million barrels of oil from strategic reserves held by member countries to help cushion the impact of supply disruptions. Further releases could be considered if market conditions deteriorate.

For Zimbabwe, sustained increases in international oil prices present risks for fuel import costs, transport operators, manufacturers, farmers and other businesses that rely on petroleum products.

Higher fuel costs can feed into freight charges, production expenses and the distribution of goods, potentially putting additional pressure on consumer prices and business margins.

Transport and logistics companies are particularly exposed because fuel is a major operating expense. An extended period of elevated diesel prices could force operators to increase charges or absorb higher costs, depending on competition and demand.

Agriculture and manufacturing could also face increased production costs through fuel-dependent machinery, generators and the transportation of raw materials and finished products.

Zimbabwe's exposure will depend on international crude and refined-product prices, regional supply conditions, exchange-rate movements and domestic fuel pricing arrangements.

The IEA's October oil market report projects global oil demand to fall by 2.6 million barrels per day in 2026 as higher prices, supply constraints and weaker economic conditions weigh on consumption. Although demand is expected to recover partially in 2027, the agency says global oil use will remain below 2025 levels.

The agency has also warned that depleted inventories and continuing supply disruptions could leave fuel markets vulnerable to further shocks.

For businesses, the outlook reinforces the importance of monitoring fuel-related expenses, reviewing logistics contracts and incorporating energy price volatility into operating budgets.

While a recovery in supply could eventually ease pressure on international markets, the IEA's assessment suggests that companies and fuel-importing economies should not assume a swift return to stable prices in the coming year.

The duration of the Middle East conflict, the restoration of disrupted production and refining capacity, and the security of major shipping routes will remain key determinants of the global oil price outlook.

title: Tanzania: Can Tanzania Set Its Sights On China's Graphite Crown?
summary: Tanzania wants to overtake China in graphite production within 15 years. It is a bold target for a country with substantial reserves but only a small share of global output. The announcement signals its intention to become a major force in
content:
Tanzania wants to overtake China in graphite production within 15 years. It is a bold target for a country with substantial reserves but only a small share of global output. The announcement signals its intention to become a major force in the fast-growing battery materials market.

"We are going to surpass China in terms of production," Minerals Minister Anthony Mavunde told a mining forum in London this month, citing Tanzania's estimated 6% share of global graphite reserves. However, there is a vast difference between that ambition and the current state of output. Tanzania must decide whether it can build a competitive industry or will remain a supplier of raw material processed elsewhere.

Graphite is a key component in lithium-ion batteries used in electric vehicles and energy storage systems. A global drive for electrification will push demand for critical minerals like graphite even higher. Extraction will have to increase regardless though another problem lies in the supply chains. Processing capacity is heavily concentrated in China, with American and European manufacturers now looking for different sources of processed graphite.

Tanzania has a credible starting point. The [US Geological Survey](https://pubs.usgs.gov/publication/mcs2026 "https://pubs.usgs.gov/publication/mcs2026") estimates that it produced 75,000 tonnes of natural graphite in 2025, more than twice its estimated 2024 output. While the rate of growth is relentless China, produced about 1.4 million tonnes that year. Closing the gap would require Tanzania to expand far faster than its established competitor.

Keep up with the latest headlines on [WhatsApp](https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaIdDi8Bqbr263erhw1K "https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaIdDi8Bqbr263erhw1K") | [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/allafrica/ "https://www.linkedin.com/company/allafrica/")

Growth will require investment, which is beginning to follow. In August, Tanzania signed a [$100 million agreement](https://www.spglobal.com/energy/en/news-research/latest-news/metals/081826-tanzania-eyes-50000-mtyear-graphite-output-under-new-100m-china-deal-minister "https://www.spglobal.com/energy/en/news-research/latest-news/metals/081826-tanzania-eyes-50000-mtyear-graphite-output-under-new-100m-china-deal-minister") with Chinese state-owned Henan Yudi Mining Company to develop a graphite project in Morogoro. Tanzania will hold a 17% stake in the venture, which is targeting annual production of 50,000 tonnes.

Another project in the works is the Australian-backed Lindi Jumbo project, designed to produce 40,000 tonnes a year over an estimated 24-year mine life. Projects like these show growing commercial interest, although planned capacity can take years to become actual output.

The bigger challenge for Tanzania lies beyond extraction.

China's advantage comes from both the volume it mines and its control of the technology that turns graphite into battery-grade material. The IEA estimates that China handles more than 90% of battery-grade graphite refining. Countries with abundant deposits can therefore remain dependent on Chinese facilities for higher-value production.

That dependence presents Tanzania with a difficult choice. Chinese investment can speed up mine development and bring capital and expertise. Yet it may do little to establish an independent domestic processing industry. If Tanzania cannot add value at home, much of the industry's economic benefit will continue to flow overseas.

Mavunde recognised the problem and says the government wants minerals to be processed domestically.

Meeting that goal will require reliable electricity and major upgrades to industrial and transport infrastructure. Tanzania is already well on its way as the [completion](https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/tanzania-commissions-countrys-largest-hydropower-plant-2026-08-22/ "https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/tanzania-commissions-countrys-largest-hydropower-plant-2026-08-22/") of the the Julius Nyerere Hydro Power Plant nearly doubled Tanzania's energy generation capacity to 4646MW. The [near completed](https://africa.businessinsider.com/local/markets/tanzania-edges-closer-to-dollar42-billion-gas-deal-in-push-to-become-east-africas/pfx544q "https://africa.businessinsider.com/local/markets/tanzania-edges-closer-to-dollar42-billion-gas-deal-in-push-to-become-east-africas/pfx544q") USD $42 billion-dollar LNG project led by Shell and Equinor will double Tanzania's capacity again to 8000MW. This exponential increase in energy generation will allow for competitive processing. Any processing plants will also have to meet the exacting purity standards set by international battery manufacturers.

Geopolitics creates an opening. The United States and Europe are trying to reduce their dependence on Chinese battery materials. In July 2025, the US announced a preliminary anti-dumping duty of 93.5% on certain Chinese graphite anode materials, showing how closely critical minerals are now tied to trade policy.

Tanzania could benefit from this push to diversify supply. In August, Australian developer [EcoGraf](https://www.spglobal.com/energy/en/news-research/latest-news/metals/081226-ecograf-secures-german-offtake-deal-for-tanzanian-graphite-project "https://www.spglobal.com/energy/en/news-research/latest-news/metals/081226-ecograf-secures-german-offtake-deal-for-tanzanian-graphite-project") secured a preliminary long-term offtake arrangement with a German graphite trader for its planned Epanko project. The deal points to potential European demand for Tanzanian graphite.

#### Sign up for free AllAfrica Newsletters

Get the latest in African news delivered straight to your inbox

Being an alternative to China will not be enough. International buyers will expect competitive prices and reliable delivery at a consistent quality. Tanzania must meet those demands while avoiding excessive reliance on any one market.

The opportunity also extends beyond Tanzania's borders. Processing minerals from neighbouring countries could help the country become a regional manufacturing and export hub.

Overtaking China within 15 years remains unlikely but Tanzania does not need to become the world's largest graphite producer to succeed. A more realistic goal is to build a competitive industry that keeps more processing and revenue at home.

Success will ultimately be measured by how much value Tanzania can create from its graphite before it leaves the country.

title: Nigeria: Federal Govt Mum As Nigeria Loses 20 Visa-Free Destinations in Latest Passport Ranking
summary: The Nigerian government has not replied to the request by LEADERSHIP to respond to a disturbing report that the country has lost access to 20 visa-free destinations, with the country's passport ranking falling from 90th position in July 202
content:
The Nigerian government has not replied to the request by LEADERSHIP to respond to a disturbing report that the country has lost access to 20 visa-free destinations, with the country's passport ranking falling from 90th position in July 2026 to 181st in the latest IziVisa Passport Ranking Index.

LEADERSHIP reported on Tuesday that data published on IziVisa.com show that Nigerian passport holders can travel to 24 countries without a visa, obtain visas on arrival in 16 countries, and access 43 countries through electronic visas.

The latest figures represent a decline from the 44 destinations Nigerians could visit without a visa in July 2026, highlighting reduced travel access for holders of the country's passport.

In a statement on its website, IziVisa explained that passports are ranked by the number of destinations their holders can access without obtaining a visa in advance.

At the time of filing this updated report, the Spokesman of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Oluwafemi Adeniyi, had yet to respond to our request regarding this development, despite calls and messages sent to him.

However, a foreign affairs analyst, who preferred anonymity, bemoaned the situation, stressing that "it is a sad situation for the country, which demonstrates how low the country has sunk among the comity of nations" even as he challenged the Nigerian government to, as a matter of urgency, strive to remove the country from this unfortunate path.

The LEADERSHIP initial report noted that the index considers different categories of travel access, including visa-free entry, visas on arrival and electronic visas, to assess the international mobility available to passport holders.

The United Arab Emirates leads the 2026 IziVisa ranking, with its passport providing access to 185 of 198 documented destinations through visa-free entry, visas on arrival or electronic visas.

Switzerland occupies second position, with access to 120 destinations without a visa, 26 destinations offering visas on arrival and 37 accessible through electronic visas.

Other countries featuring prominently in the ranking include Luxembourg, Malta, Denmark, Spain and Finland.

IziVisa said the differences between passports at the top and bottom of its ranking illustrate disparities in access to international travel. The index uses the number of destinations accessible without a prior visa as a measure of freedom of movement.

Separately, the July 2026 edition of the Henley Passport Index placed Nigeria 90th out of 199 passports assessed worldwide, with a visa-free score of 44 destinations.

The ranking, released by Henley & Partners, represented a one-place decline from Nigeria's 89th position in the April 2026 edition, although its visa-free score remained unchanged at 44 destinations.

According to Henley & Partners, the index marked the organisation's 20th anniversary and assessed 199 passports against 227 travel destinations using data from the International Air Transport Association.

Among African countries, South Africa ranked 49th globally, with visa-free access to 101 destinations. Botswana followed in 61st position, with access to 81 destinations, while Morocco ranked 67th with 71 destinations.

Kenya occupied 68th position, with access to 70 destinations, while Ghana ranked 70th with a visa-free score of 67.

Nigeria ranked alongside the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Turkmenistan in the Henley Passport Index, with each passport offering visa-free access to 44 destinations.

However, the reported IziVisa ranking should not be treated as directly comparable to the Henley Passport Index, as the two rankings use different methodologies and destination coverage.

# Taiwan Coffee Festival to feature brands from Indonesia, Japan, Vietnam

10/21/2026 05:36 PM

[](jsvscript:)[](jsvscript:)[](javascript:void(0))[Listen](javascript:)

Yunlin County Magistrate Chang Li-shan (right). CNA photo Oct. 21, 2026

Taipei, Oct. 21 (CNA) The 2026 Taiwan Coffee Festival in Yunlin County will bring together 170 brands, including coffee businesses from Indonesia, Japan and Vietnam, to build international ties and find new markets, the county government said Wednesday.

The festival will be held at Green Tunnel Park in Gukeng Township over two weekends, Oct. 31-Nov. 1 and Nov. 7-8, featuring coffee forums, award-winning Yunlin coffee and activities highlighting coffee cultures from around the world, the government said.

Yunlin County Magistrate Chang Li-shan (張麗善) said the event aims to connect Taiwan's coffee industry with international markets by bringing local and overseas brands together to share expertise and explore business opportunities.

The festival will also feature a "central Taiwan coffee map" linking coffee shops in Taichung, Nantou, Changhua, Yunlin and Chiayi, the county government said.

Visitors can collect digital stamps at participating coffee shops and nearby attractions, extending the festival beyond the main venue, it said.

(By Chiang Yi-ching and Lee Hsin-Yin)

content:
新北中新网10月21日电 周三，五人因涉嫌在一名中国公民的贿赂下策划交通事故，导致讽刺中国国家主席习近平的喜剧演员黄逸豪受伤而被起诉。

起诉书称，新北检察官正在寻求对一名郑姓男子判处五年零六个月以上的有期徒刑。这名中国公民只称他为“K”，据称他是联系策划这次袭击的。

检察官没有透露有关这名中国公民的更多细节，并告诉中央社，K 的背景仍在调查中。

检察官将此案描述为所谓的中国跨境镇压，旨在压制反对的政治观点，类似于台北检察官对 5 月 29 日黄计划在喜剧俱乐部表演的场所发生的袭击的描述。

## 涉嫌上演交通事故

下午4点54分左右，一辆载着两人的汽车撞到了这位44岁的喜剧演员，当时他正在新北永和区骑摩托车回家。检察官称，9 月 11 日，他的右骨盆挫伤。

检察官表示，根据闭路电视录像显示，当天早上 7 点 31 分，车内的两名男子和一名范姓男子在胡同入口处等候，这起事故促使对黄的政治观点是否为动机进行调查。
检察官称，调查显示，黄姓司机、在副驾驶座拍摄这一事件的廖姓男子以及在喜剧演员接近时向司机发出警报的范某，均受雇实施袭击。

三人受雇于一名游姓男子，他策划了与程的“意外”。检察官称，程从 7 月 25 日到 8 月期间利用监控和安装在他摩托车上的 GPS 追踪器来追踪这位喜剧演员的行踪和日常生活。

据检方称，“K”承诺支付 45 万新台币（13,870 美元），以在一场交通事故中折断黄一豪的胳膊和腿，目的是阻止他在 9 月 20 日在喜剧俱乐部表演，并预付了新台币 25 万新台币。

检方称，该团伙通过短信应用程序向“K”发送了黄某的医疗证明电子副本，并冒充保险公司帮助黄某提出索赔，而程某并未收到剩余的新台币20万元。

他们补充说，“K”对黄毅豪仅受轻伤感到不满。

## 寻求的句子

此次调查由新北检警、法务部调查局台北市办事处联合开展，自10月6日起，共分3次突击搜查8处地点。

检察官称，经法院批准，这五名嫌疑人已被拘留。
检方表示，被告曾为台湾境外敌对势力工作，镇压异见、制造社会恐惧、破坏台湾民主法治，罪行尤为严重。

五人被指控企图严重伤害以及非法收集和使用个人数据。程还面临使用电子设备非法记录私人活动的指控。他面临着五人中最长的监禁刑期。

检方正在寻求尤有期徒刑五年以上，黄有期徒刑四年，范某有期徒刑三年零六个月，廖有期徒刑两年零七个月。

New Taipei, Oct. 21 (CNA) Five people were indicted Wednesday for allegedly staging a traffic accident that injured comedian Huang Yi-hao (黃逸豪), who has satirized Chinese President Xi Jinping (習近平), after being paid to do so by a Chinese national.

New Taipei prosecutors are seeking a prison sentence of more than five years and six months for a man surnamed Cheng (鄭), whom the Chinese national identified only as "K," allegedly contacted to plan the attack, according to the indictment.

Prosecutors did not disclose further details about the Chinese national, telling CNA that K's background remains under investigation.

Prosecutors described the case as alleged Chinese cross-border repression intended to silence opposing political views, similar to how Taipei prosecutors characterized an attack at a venue called Comedy Club on May 29, where Huang was scheduled to perform.

## Alleged staged traffic accident

A vehicle carrying two people hit the 44-year-old comedian as he was riding his scooter home in New Taipei's Yonghe District at around 4:54 p.m. on Sept. 11, leaving him with a contusion to his right pelvis, prosecutors said.

Prosecutors said the accident prompted an investigation into whether Huang's political views were a motive after a review of CCTV footage showed the two men in the vehicle and a man surnamed Fan (范) waiting at an alley entrance from 7:31 a.m. that day.

An investigation showed that the driver, also surnamed Huang (黃), a man surnamed Liao (廖) who filmed the incident from the front passenger seat, and Fan, who alerted the driver when the comedian was approaching, were hired to carry out the attack, prosecutors said.

The three were hired by a man surnamed You (游), who planned the "accident" with Cheng. Cheng had tracked the comedian's movements and routine from July 25 through August using surveillance and a GPS tracker placed on his scooter, prosecutors said.

"K" had promised Cheng NT$450,000 (US$13,870) to break Huang Yi-hao's arms and legs in a traffic accident, the objective being to prevent him from performing on Sept. 20 at Comedy Club, with NT$250,000 paid upfront, according to prosecutors.

Cheng did not receive the remaining NT$200,000 after the group sent "K" an electronic copy of Huang's medical certificate via a messaging app, which they obtained by pretending to be an insurance company helping him file a claim, prosecutors said.

"K" was unhappy that Huang Yi-hao suffered only minor injuries, they added.

## Sentences sought

The investigation was jointly conducted by New Taipei prosecutors, police and the Taipei City Field Office of the Ministry of Justice Investigation Bureau, which raided eight locations in three operations since Oct. 6.

The five suspects have been detained with court approval, prosecutors said.

Prosecutors said the defendants had worked for a hostile force outside Taiwan to suppress dissent, create fear in society and undermine Taiwan's democracy and rule of law, adding that the offense was particularly serious.

The five were charged with attempted serious injury and illegally collecting and using personal data. Cheng also faces a charge of illegally recording private activities using an electronic device. He faces the longest prison sentence sought among the five.

Prosecutors are seeking more than five years for You, four years for Huang, three years and six months for Fan, and two years and seven months for Liao.

## May attack

During the May 29 attack four bags containing a mixture of paint and human feces were thrown at Comedy Club, damaging its glass, floors and walls. Huang was rehearsing for shows scheduled for that night and the next day when the attack took place at 6:45 p.m. The performance was postponed for one hour as a result.

Taipei prosecutors later indicted a man surnamed Liu (劉), alleging an unidentified Chinese national instructed him to carry out the attack and that he recruited a man surnamed Kuo (郭) for NT$50,000.

Prosecutors linked the May attack to clips of Huang mocking Xi during a December 2025 performance at the venue that later went viral on social media.

According to United Daily News, Huang satirized Xi in a comedy routine, mocking his appearance, including his heavy build and resemblance to Winnie the Pooh, while mocking Xi's education, saying he earned a law doctorate based on an agricultural thesis despite having only a primary school education.

The routine also touched on issues including Hong Kong's pro-democracy movements against an extradition bill, China's COVID-19 lockdowns and censorship, the report said.

Responding to the May attack, China's Taiwan Affairs Office said it was unaware of case details, dismissing allegations of cross-border repression as "groundless."

## Huang's response

Speaking to reporters Wednesday, Huang said the vehicle suddenly swerved right after he parked his scooter in an alley, hitting the scooter before striking him which limited the severity of his injuries.

The people in the car immediately got out, apologized and invited him to sit inside, but he declined because he did not know who they were.

As they appeared friendly and repeatedly expressed concern for him, Huang said he did not think much of it at the time and it was only after investigators reviewed surveillance footage that he learned the crash had been planned.

Huang said he was not surprised that China uses intermediaries to infiltrate Taiwan, noting that some gang members, to his knowledge, help China carry out such activities. However, he said he did not expect it to happen to him.

In a Facebook post Wednesday, Huang thanked law enforcement involved in the investigation for handling the case without taking a break over the National Day holiday, saying he had invited them to watch his show in November.

"I spent just two and a half minutes criticizing Xi Jinping on stage in Taiwan, and was later targeted in a feces attack and a deliberate vehicle collision," he said.

"If people are already treated this way for criticizing the Chinese Communist Party before it controls Taiwan, how can we expect to retain freedom of speech if it does one day?"

(By Tsao Ya-yen and Shih Hsiu-chuan)

# Japan September exports rise 16.7% year-on-year, missing forecasts

Japan's September exports grew 16.7% year-on-year, driven by semiconductor and AI demand, but missed the 20.1% market forecast. Imports rose 18.9%, and the trade deficit widened to ¥536.6 billion. Exports to the US surged 22.9%, while those to China increased 8.6%.

[![Image 4: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

 By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

Japan's exports rose 16.7 per cent in September from a year earlier, marking the 13th consecutive month of growth, the Ministry of Finance said. The increase was supported by strong external demand for semiconductors and artificial-intelligence-related products, but fell short of the market expectation of 20.1 per cent.

Import growth slowed to 18.9 per cent in September, below the forecast of 19.6 per cent. The trade deficit stood at 536.6 billion yen (US$3.6 billion), far exceeding the market estimate of 181.0 billion yen.

By destination, exports to the United States jumped 22.9 per cent year-on-year in September. Shipments to China rose 8.6 per cent, to Asia climbed 17.5 per cent, and to the European Union increased 10.5 per cent.

In South Korea, exports during the first 20 days of this month more than doubled from a year earlier, driven by record-high chip sales. Semiconductor exports surged more than 2.2 times and accounted for nearly 45 per cent of total exports during the period.

(File photo)

26 October 2026

[Capital FM (Nairobi)](https://capitalfm.africa/ "Visit Capital FM (Nairobi)")

Nairobi — President William Ruto has mourned the 23 people killed in a road accident at Kanga near Mtito Andei along the Nairobi-Mombasa Highway, calling for greater caution among motorists and stricter safety inspections for public service vehicles (PSVs).

In a condolence message shared on social media, Ruto expressed sympathy with the families and friends of the victims, describing the incident as a devastating loss for the affected families and the country.

"I convey my heartfelt condolences to the families and friends of the 23 people who lost their lives in the tragic road accident," the President said, adding that the country shared in their grief.

He also wished those injured in the crash a quick recovery.

The President urged all motorists, particularly drivers operating public service vehicles, to exercise caution and observe traffic regulations to prevent further loss of life on Kenyan roads.

Ruto further directed relevant authorities to conduct thorough inspections of public service vehicles to ensure they comply with the required safety standards.

The directive comes amid renewed concerns over road safety following the fatal collision at Kanga, near Mtito Andei, on the busy Nairobi-Mombasa Highway.

The President said vehicle inspections should help ensure that public service vehicles meet the required safety standards, as part of efforts to prevent road accidents.

The accident has renewed calls for motorists to adhere to traffic rules and for authorities to strengthen enforcement of road safety regulations.

The Nairobi-Mombasa Highway is a key transport corridor connecting the capital to the Coast, carrying passenger buses, commercial vehicles and private motorists.

Ruto's call places renewed emphasis on responsible driving, compliance with traffic regulations and regular inspections of public service vehicles.

The President's message did not provide further details on the cause of the crash or the condition of those injured.

[Capital FM](https://capitalfm.africa/police-tighten-nairobi-security-with-checkpoints-ahead-of-defiant-saba-saba-protests/ "https://capitalfm.africa/police-tighten-nairobi-security-with-checkpoints-ahead-of-defiant-saba-saba-protests/")

Police setting up checkpoints in Nairobi (file photo)

26 October 2026

Cape Town — Nairobi police arrested several protesters on Monday as officers and demonstrators clashed in running battles across the CBD over rising fuel prices and the cost of living, The Eastleigh Voice [reports](https://eastleighvoice.co.ke/news/416253/several-protesters-arrested-as-police-clash-with-demonstrators-over-fuel-prices-in-nairobi "https://eastleighvoice.co.ke/news/416253/several-protesters-arrested-as-police-clash-with-demonstrators-over-fuel-prices-in-nairobi").

Protesters gathered on Moi Avenue and Kimathi Street despite a heavy police deployment, carrying placards reading 'Remove taxes on fuel'. The protests followed the Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority's latest pricing review for the October-November cycle, which pushed petrol in Nairobi to Sh226.96 per litre, diesel to Sh227.76, and kerosene to Sh219.87.

In a letter dated October 22 and received at police headquarters the same day, the Coalition of Human Rights Defenders said the demonstration aimed to highlight the burden of fuel costs on households and businesses. Organisers estimated 500 to 900 participants, and pledged to keep the march orderly and respect the rights of other members of the public.

26 October 2026

Gabon has[lifted](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c6x2w0ngejneo "https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c6x2w0ngejneo")its eight-month social media ban, which was introduced in February over concerns that online content was fuelling conflict and deepening divisions.

The ban took effect on 17 February, with the High Communication Authority (HAC) saying online content was fuelling conflict and deepening divisions in the country.

The restriction drew widespread criticism, particularly from young people and businesses reliant on platforms such as Facebook, TikTok, YouTube and Instagram. Many users resorted to virtual private networks (VPNs) to bypass the ban.

The ban came at a time when Gabonese President Brice Oligui Nguema faced a wave of social unrest less than a year after his election.

The suspension came amid social unrest, including strikes by teachers and civil servants over pay and working conditions.

The opposition said the suspension was an abuse of power.

title: Interpol to push asset tracing at Hong Kong general assembly
zh_title: 国际刑警组织将在香港大会上推动资产追查
summary: 国际刑警组织秘书长瓦尔德西·乌尔基扎 (Valdecy Urquiza) 表示，国际刑警组织第 94 届大会将于 11 月 30 日至 12 月 3 日在香港举行，重点讨论追踪犯罪资产、人工智能相关犯罪和国际警务合作。 [![图片 1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk) 作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编 2026 年 10 月 26 日 06:00 香港时间 · 3 分钟阅读国际刑警组织寻求加强追踪和扣押犯罪资产方面的国际合作，第 94 届会议将讨论一项新能力
content:
香港
国际刑警组织秘书长瓦尔德西·乌尔基扎 (Valdecy Urquiza) 表示，国际刑警组织第 94 届大会将于 11 月 30 日至 12 月 3 日在香港举行，重点讨论追查犯罪资产、人工智能相关犯罪和国际警务合作。

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

2026 年 10 月 26 日 06:00 香港时间 · 阅读时间 3 分钟

国际刑警组织秘书长瓦尔德西·乌尔基扎表示，国际刑警组织正在寻求加强追查和扣押犯罪资产方面的国际合作，并将在香港举行的第 94 届大会上讨论新的能力。

大会将于 11 月 30 日至 12 月 3 日在香港举行，来自 196 个成员国的 2,000 多名代表将齐聚一堂，讨论执法重点、全球挑战和国际刑警组织的未来战略。

乌尔奎扎表示：“香港是金融、贸易和数字服务的中心，也是我们将国际执法界聚集在一起的完美地点。”他形容香港是一个积极而忠诚的合作伙伴，并指出从当地警察部队借调到国际刑警组织的警官贡献了专业知识，特别是在金融犯罪调查方面。
香港警务处处长周一鸣表示，大会的筹备工作已于2025年初开始，由政务司司长担任主席的香港特别行政区督导委员会、保安局局长领导的跨部门专责小组以及警务处处长领导的警队工作小组组成三层协调架构。他表示，香港致力于确保会议安全可靠，并利用这次活动加强与海外执法机构的伙伴关系，同时展示香港的安全和举办重大国际活动的能力。

乌尔基扎引用了国际刑警组织的银色通缉令倡议作为该组织希望在大会上推进的新能力的一个例子。该计划的重点是帮助执法机构调查和追踪犯罪组织隐藏在不同司法管辖区的金融资产。国际刑警组织已对该倡议进行了为期两年的试点，并希望成员国予以支持。周还强调了金融调查和预防欺诈的重要性，称诈骗占该市 9 月份报告的犯罪案件的一半左右。他指出国际合作打击金融犯罪的重要性，并指出香港已建立反诈骗平台FRONTIER+，帮助海外合作伙伴追查资金并拦截可疑交易。
与人工智能相关的犯罪是今年大会议程上的另一个问题。乌尔奎扎表示，人工智能使犯罪环境变得更加复杂，使犯罪组织能够到达他们以前无法进入的地区，并以其他犯罪领域未曾见过的规模开展活动。他表示，国际刑警组织正在通过三个领域解决与人工智能相关的犯罪问题：了解犯罪集团如何使用人工智能、帮助执法机构利用人工智能提高调查效率和分析大量数据、以及促进警察负责任地使用人工智能。

乌尔基扎表示，国际刑警组织作为一个技术平台的作用是让其 196 个成员国的警察机构保持联系，并在政治分歧的情况下实现合作。周说香港h

Hong Kong
Interpol's 94th General Assembly in Hong Kong from 30 November to 3 December will focus on tracing criminal assets, AI-related crime and international police cooperation, Secretary-General Valdecy Urquiza said.

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

26 Oct 2026 at 06:00 HKT · 3 min read

INTERPOL is seeking to strengthen international cooperation in tracing and seizing criminal assets, with a new capability set to be discussed at its 94th General Assembly in Hong Kong, Secretary-General Valdecy Urquiza said.

The General Assembly will take place from 30 November to 3 December in Hong Kong, bringing more than 2,000 representatives from its 196 member countries to discuss law enforcement priorities, global challenges and INTERPOL's future strategy.

“Hong Kong is a hub for finance, trade, digital services, and is the perfect location for us to bring the international law enforcement community together,” Urquiza said. He described Hong Kong as an active and committed partner, noting that officers seconded from the local police force to INTERPOL had contributed expertise, particularly in financial crime investigations.

Hong Kong Police Commissioner Joe Chow Yat-ming said preparations for the assembly had begun in early 2025, with a three-tier coordination structure comprising the HKSAR Steering Committee chaired by the Chief Secretary for Administration, an Inter-departmental Task Force led by the Secretary for Security, and the Force Working Group headed by the Commissioner of Police. He said the city is committed to ensuring a safe and secure conference and to use the event to strengthen partnerships with overseas law enforcement agencies while showcasing Hong Kong's security and ability to host major international events.

Urquiza cited INTERPOL's Silver Notice initiative as an example of the new capabilities the organisation hopes to advance at the General Assembly. The initiative focuses on helping law enforcement agencies investigate and trace financial assets that criminal organisations hide in different jurisdictions. INTERPOL has conducted a two-year pilot of the initiative and hopes member countries will endorse it. Chow also highlighted the importance of financial investigations and fraud prevention, saying scams accounted for about half of reported crime cases in the city in September. He pointed to the importance of international cooperation in tackling financial crime, noting Hong Kong had established the anti-scam platform FRONTIER+ to help overseas partners trace funds and intercept suspicious transactions.

Artificial-intelligence-related crime is another issue on this year's General Assembly agenda. Urquiza said AI had made the criminal landscape more complex, enabling criminal organisations to reach regions they had previously been unable to access and operate on a scale not seen in other areas of crime. INTERPOL is addressing AI-related crime through three areas: understanding how criminal groups use AI, helping law enforcement agencies use AI to improve investigative efficiency and analyse large amounts of data, and promoting the responsible use of AI by police, he said.

Urquiza said INTERPOL's role as a technical platform was to keep police agencies across its 196 member countries connected and enable cooperation despite political differences. Chow said Hong Kong hoped to strengthen operational and intelligence-sharing ties with Asian counterparts while expanding training and capacity-building cooperation with other regions, including Africa. The force also hoped to provide training for overseas officers and send its own personnel to learn from international partners, he added. Chow said the Hong Kong International Academy of Policing will also be established on 11 November, with the aim of bringing international policing experience to Hong Kong and sharing local expertise with overseas partners.
